title: onsemi and Synaptics Announce Revised Merger Agreement

onsemi and Synaptics Announce Revised Merger Agreement
Show side navigation

Revised Terms to Deliver Higher onsemi Shareholder Value through Immediate EPS Accretion 
Amended Agreement Follows Thorough Review of Unsolicited Competing Proposal 
SCOTTSDALE, Ariz. and SAN JOSE, Calif. – Oct. 1, 2026 – onsemi (NASDAQ: ON) and Synaptics Incorporated (NASDAQ: SYNA) ("Synaptics") today announced they have amended their June 25, 2026 merger agreement. The amendment follows an unsolicited competing proposal received from a third party.
Under the revised agreement, onsemi will acquire Synaptics for $123 per share in cash for an aggregate value of approximately $5.7 billion as compared to approximately $7 billion for the prior agreement. The transaction is expected to be immediately accretive to onsemi’s non-GAAP earnings per share and provides value certainty for Synaptics’ shareholders.
“As was the case when we initially announced the acquisition, Synaptics addresses an important aspect of our strategic direction, and we believe the revised merger agreement represents a more financially attractive transaction for our shareholders,” said Hassane El-Khoury, President and CEO of onsemi. “The all-cash transaction delivers higher value to our shareholders through lower total cost consideration, and we now expect the transaction to be immediately accretive to non-GAAP EPS upon closing. In addition, we have identified incremental opportunities to create shareholder value beyond the previously announced $200 million of annual run-rate synergies. These additional benefits from revenue synergies and insourcing of a portion of Synaptics’ production are expected to be realized after the initial 18 months post-close, further strengthening the long-term earnings and cash flow profile of the combined company.”
El-Khoury continued, “Synaptics is accretive to our long-term model, with a strong growth outlook and attractive gross margin profile that will help accelerate onsemi’s evolution. Additionally, Synaptics complements growth in our AI data center business, and brings to onsemi its highly profitable human-machine interface, and sensing products businesses that generate strong and predictable cash flows, providing the combined company with a durable funding engine to accelerate its connected compute capabilities.”
After careful review with its financial and legal advisors, the Synaptics Board unanimously determined that the onsemi transaction, as amended, continues to be in the best interests of Synaptics and its shareholders.
"Our Board has been singularly focused on delivering the best outcome for our shareholders, and today's amended agreement reflects that commitment," said Rahul Patel, Synaptics President and CEO. “By transitioning to an all-cash structure, we are providing value certainty at a meaningful premium as compared to current value. We are confident this path is the right choice for our shareholders."
The transaction will be financed through a combination of cash on hand and committed financing. onsemi has obtained fully committed debt financing from Morgan Stanley. The amended merger agreement does not include a closing condition related to onsemi’s financing.
The transaction is still expected to close by mid-2027, subject to approval by Synaptics shareholders, the receipt of required regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions. The transaction has been approved by the United States Federal Trade Commission, and regulators in other jurisdictions are reviewing the transaction.

title: Amkor Technology and NVIDIA Advance Strategic Partnership for AI Infrastructure
source: Amkor Technology - Investor Press Releases / Press Releases
content_text:
Amkor Technology and NVIDIA Advance Strategic Partnership for AI Infrastructure
New $1.3 billion agreement supports further expansion in South Korea , building on the companies’ recent Arizona collaboration 
TEMPE, Ariz. --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 21, 2026--
Amkor Technology, Inc. (Nasdaq: AMKR), a leading provider of outsourced semiconductor packaging and test services, today announced additional investments in South Korea for capacity expansion initiatives with NVIDIA. With this latest commitment, Amkor’s multi-year agreements with NVIDIA in Arizona and South Korea total $3 billion . The initiatives support growing demand for next-generation AI and accelerated computing platforms.
Advanced packaging technologies are essential to enabling the performance, power efficiency and integration required for next-generation computing systems. The prepayments align Amkor's manufacturing capacity with NVIDIA’s long-term growth plans and support increasing demand for advanced packaging solutions.
“Our partnership with NVIDIA underscores the critical role advanced packaging plays in enabling next-generation AI platforms,” said Kevin Engel , president and chief executive officer of Amkor Technology . “These investments build on our global manufacturing footprint and strengthen our ability to support customers through our operations in both the United States and South Korea.”
“Growing demand for accelerated computing is increasing the need for advanced packaging capacity,” said Debora Shoquist , executive vice president, operations of NVIDIA. “Our work with Amkor helps us scale production of current and next-generation platforms while strengthening the resilience of our global supply chain.”
This collaboration further strengthens Amkor’s role as a strategic manufacturing partner for NVIDIA and reinforces the companies’ shared commitment to supporting the continued expansion of AI infrastructure.
Amkor will also exhibit at NVIDIA GTC Washington, D.C. from Nov. 30 - Dec. 3 , where the company will showcase its advanced packaging and test capabilities and engage with customers, policymakers and industry leaders.
About Amkor Technology, Inc. 
Amkor Technology, Inc. (Nasdaq: AMKR) is the world’s largest U.S. headquartered OSAT and is a global leader in outsourced semiconductor packaging and test services. With a strong track record of innovation, a broad and diverse geographic footprint and solid partnerships with lead customers, Amkor delivers high-quality solutions that enable the world’s leading semiconductor and electronics companies to bring advanced technologies to market. The company’s comprehensive portfolio includes advanced packaging, wafer-level processing, and system-in-package solutions targeting applications for smartphones, data centers, artificial intelligence, automobiles and wearables. For more information visit amkor.com .

title: Ouster Sensors Play Key Role in Forterra's Lancer Completing 1,426 Missions and 88 Casualty Evacuation Operations in Ukraine
content_text:
Ouster Sensors Play Key Role in Forterra's Lancer Completing 1,426 Missions and 88 Casualty Evacuation Operations in Ukraine
October 21, 2026
PDF Version 
Expanding a multi-year strategic partnership to enhance soldier safety while increasing force projection, Forterra plans to further advance its AutoDrive platform with Ouster REV8 native color lidar for next-gen defense vehicles 
SAN FRANCISCO --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 21, 2026-- Ouster, Inc. (Nasdaq: OUST), a leader in sensing and perception for Physical AI, and Forterra , the leader in autonomous mission systems for military operations in contested environments, today announced that Forterra's Lancer autonomous ground vehicles have completed 1,426 missions and 88 casualty evacuation operations in Ukraine including Ouster Rev7 OS1 digital lidar at the core of their sensor fusion perception stack. Forterra built and delivered 105 Lancers in under six months, and across more than 7,300 miles they have run routes that would otherwise have put a crew inside the vehicle.
This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261021344872/en/ 
Forterra's Lancer keeps crews out of harm's way, this one lost on a mission in Ukraine with no one aboard.
The Lancers arrived in Ukraine in October 2025 . Built on the Polaris RANGER XP 1500 and modified in theater with Starlink for resilient communications, each vehicle carries up to 750 kilograms of critical equipment to the war fighters. Lancers are operating in high danger zones where persistent drone surveillance makes crewed vehicles high value targets and creates unnecessary risk for personnel. Instead, uncrewed Lancer systems deliver essential supplies and evacuate wounded soldiers without undue risk to additional personnel.
“Forterra exists to take people out of harm’s way, and in Ukraine , Lancer is doing that every day under constant drone surveillance,” said Forterra CEO Josh Araujo . “As we advance AutoDrive toward higher levels of autonomy, Ouster sensors give us the perception foundation required by the next generation of vehicles.”
To date, Forterra has integrated AutoDrive across more than 50 vehicle platforms deployed in over ten countries. This includes the Squad Multipurpose Equipment Transport (SMET) program and the Marine Corps ROGUE Fires platform, which recently entered Block 2 production, making it the most widely deployed autonomous driving system in the defense industry and the first system fielded by the U.S . military to enable autonomous maneuver of ground vehicles.
Forterra’s AutoDrive capability is built upon Forterra’s 24 years of operational experience and over $500 million invested in engineering development and operations. Throughout a multi-year partnership, Ouster digital lidar has been a key part of Forterra’s AutoDrive platform and its operational success.
Ouster's sensors enable 360-degree situational awareness for autonomous ground vehicles operating in complex and unpredictable environments. Each Ouster OS1 sensor covers ground that would otherwise require several narrow field-of-view sensors, which means fewer units for Forterra to integrate, power, and maintain on every vehicle. Additionally, lidar ranges are independent of ambient light, and dual returns report both an obscurant and the surface behind it, so perception holds in fog, dust, rain, and darkness.
"Forterra operates autonomous ground vehicles in some of the most challenging environments on the planet, where reliable perception and safety are critical to the vehicle operators and soldiers," said Angus Pacala , co-founder and CEO of Ouster. "Ouster's technology gives these vehicles a detailed, real-time understanding of their surroundings, helping them navigate complex terrain and operate with greater confidence when GPS, road markings and ideal conditions cannot be relied upon."
Next- Gen Sensing , Built to Automotive Standards 
Ouster's next-generation native color digital lidar, Rev8, is designed for ASIL-B functional safety to ISO 26262, cybersecurity to ISO 21434, and support for automotive ethernet, all requirements that unmanned ground vehicle programs increasingly demand.
Off-road work causes constant vibration and shock and subjects lidar sensors to temperatures that swing from arctic cold to desert heat. Rev8 is the most rugged lidar family Ouster has built yet, qualified from -40 °C to +85 °C and ingress-protected against dust and water, allowing sensing in the harshest conditions. Rev8 also captures color in the same silicon as the 3D data, giving perception software a second channel alongside range for classifying what is in the scene.
About Ouster 
Ouster (Nasdaq: OUST) is a leader in sensing and perception for Physical AI across industrial, robotics, automotive, and smart infrastructure. With a unified platform of high-performance digital lidar, cameras, AI compute, sensor fusion and perception software, and AI models, Ouster delivers solutions that improve quality of life in the physical world. Headquartered in San Francisco, CA , Ouster has a global presence serving thousands of customers with offices in the Americas , Europe , and Asia-Pacific . For more information about our products, visit www.ouster.com , contact our sales team , or connect with us on X or LinkedIn .
About Forterra 
Forterra is the autonomy backbone for distributed, mission-aware, resilient military operations in contested environments. Building the foundational autonomy platforms that coordinates weapons, sensors, and users through distributed mobility, compute, and communications, anywhere, under fire, without risking human life, Forterra empowers its customers to deploy autonomy as a force multiplier, extending reach, readiness survivability and effectiveness across the battlespace and industrial applications. Forterra is headquartered in Clarksburg, Md., with offices in Arlington, Va., Winter Park, Fl., Ketchum, Id. and Palo Alto, Ca. To learn more, go to forterra.com .

title: 3M and AWS collaborate to advance optical connectivity innovation
content_text:
3M and AWS collaborate to advance optical connectivity innovation
Oct 21, 2026 • 10:28 AM EDT 
Download as PDF
AWS is investing in 3M's Expanded Beam Optical technology for its data center infrastructure 
SAINT PAUL, Minn. , Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- 3M  (NYSE: MMM) and  Amazon Web Services (AWS) today announced an expanded strategic collaboration. AWS plans to deploy and scale 3M's Expanded Beam Optical (EBO) platform for its data center infrastructure. Together, the two leading American companies will advance co-innovation and investment in optical connectivity and the critical infrastructure needed for next-generation super intelligence (SI), also known as artificial intelligence (AI). 
"AWS's adoption of 3M's EBO platform demonstrates the potential of our optical connectivity technology to meet the performance demands of next-generation data center infrastructure," said Wendy Bauer, Group President of 3M's Transportation and Electronics Business Group. "By combining AWS's infrastructure expertise and scale with 3M's innovation and materials science capabilities, we can accelerate EBO deployment, advance our transformation and strengthen U.S. innovation and investment." 
"Our work with 3M reinforces our commitment to supporting good jobs here in the U.S.," said Jens Gruenkemeir, Vice President of Supply Chain & Procurement at Amazon. "Beyond powering the services people use every day, from online banking and hospital data records to streaming entertainment and retail purchases, our data center investments are unlocking economic opportunities in the communities where we invest and across the supply chain, including the hundreds of jobs being supported by 3M as a result of its collaboration with Amazon."   
The collaboration and related investments are expected to strengthen the U.S. economy by supporting more than 500 jobs directly and indirectly, including the creation of more than 100 new roles through 2027 across Minnesota, Texas and Wisconsin. These planned roles will support customer co-innovation, technology advancement and supply chain development across 3M's optical networking portfolio and help accelerate industrywide adoption through collaboration with partners. 
3M expects to contribute nearly $0.5 billion to the U.S. economy through its optical connectivity business. This investment will accelerate innovation in optical networking and fiber termination, enable commercialization at scale and drive adoption across the data center industry.
The collaboration builds on 3M's announcement earlier this year that it will double production capacity at its Menomonie, Wisconsin, manufacturing facility, and is expected to support U.S. manufacturing partners involved in equipment and production scale-up throughout the supply chain.

title: Infineon collaborates with NVIDIA on gallium nitride-based power conversion systems for 800 VDC AI data centers
content_text:
Infineon collaborates with NVIDIA on gallium nitride-based power conversion systems for 800 VDC AI data centers
Business & Financial Press
Oct 21, 2026 
Munich, Germany – 21 October 2026 – Infineon Technologies AG (FSE: IFX / OTCQX: IFNNY) is advancing its collaboration with NVIDIA on 800 Volt direct current (VDC) power architectures for AI data centers. Timed with NVIDIA's GTC Berlin developer conference, the announcement centers on the high-voltage intermediate bus converter (IBC), one of the most critical and demanding conversion stages in the power delivery chain of AI data centers. Infineon's gallium nitride (GaN) technology is emerging as well-suited technology of choice for this stage. This builds on the companies' joint work first announced in May 2025 and detailed further in October 2025, which centered on enabling serviceable, hot-swappable 800 VDC server racks.
“AI is fundamentally reshaping the demands we place on power infrastructure, and semiconductors are at the heart of solving that challenge,” said Jochen Hanebeck, CEO, Infineon Technologies AG. “Our collaboration with NVIDIA on 800 Volt power architectures shows what is possible when deep semiconductor expertise meets the pace of innovation required by AI. Gallium nitride-based system solutions are a key enabler of this next generation of data centers, and Infineon is proud to help power the AI era from grid to core.”
Driven by the extreme power draw of AI workloads, data centers have adopted intermediate-bus architectures in which an IBC steps down the main bus voltage feeding accelerator cards into a lower-voltage rail, allowing downstream stages to efficiently generate the tight core and point-of-load rails that AI processors require. This multi-stage approach reduces distribution losses, all while meeting strict constraints on board area, thermal limits and uptime. As AI infrastructure scales, 800 VDC is being introduced alongside existing AC and lower-voltage DC architectures as an additional distribution option for higher-density compute.
Gallium nitride is well suited to meet these requirements. Compared to silicon, GaN allows power devices to switch significantly faster with lower losses, which enables higher switching frequencies of up to 1 MHz at the IBC stage. This in turn allows the size of magnetic components and passives to shrink considerably, directly translating into higher power density and lower board heights, a critical advantage as rack space becomes an increasingly scarce resource in AI data centers. At the same time, GaN's low conduction and switching losses support best-in-class conversion efficiency, helping to limit heat generation even as power levels per rack continue to climb toward the megawatt range. These characteristics make GaN the preferred semiconductor technology today capable of meeting the combined demands of power density, efficiency, and fast transient response at the IBC stage, a position Infineon has built on the back of many years of leadership in GaN development and manufacturing. In combination with PSoC™ control C3 and EiceDRIVER™ product families, full system solutions for IBCs are provided by Infineon.
Infineon's GaN portfolio supports the full range of conversion ratios required at the HV IBC stage, including 800 V to 50 V, 800 V to 12 V, and 800 V to 6 V, giving data center operators the flexibility to optimize rack architectures without compromising on power density or efficiency. At this combination of high switching frequency, power density and efficiency, the GaN power switches are used to their full benefits. Infineon’s technology leadership in power semiconductors relies on extensive in-house manufacturing capabilities as well as application and system expertise built up over many years. The company’s portfolio spans IBC solutions across silicon, gallium nitride and silicon carbide , supporting customers along the entire range of their design requirements.
Infineon and NVIDIA collaborate along the entire data center power chain. In addition to IBCs, this also includes power path protection solutions, as announced in October 2025 , targeting safety and service aspects such as the hot-swap controller functionality and enabling future server boards to operate in 800 VDC power architectures.
This advanced collaboration underscores Infineon's position as a grid-to-core power semiconductor partner for AI infrastructure, supplying solutions across the full power delivery chain, from grid-facing power supply units to the point of load at the processor.
About Infineon
Infineon Technologies AG is a global semiconductor leader in power systems and IoT. Infineon drives decarbonization and digitalization with its products and solutions. The Company had around 57,000 employees worldwide (end of September 2025) and generated revenue of about €14.7 billion in the 2025 fiscal year (ending 30 September). Infineon is listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange (ticker symbol: IFX) and in the USA on the OTCQX International over-the-counter market (ticker symbol: IFNNY).

title: BASF signs Letter of Intent with Taiwan’s Ministry of Economic Affairs to advance next-generation semiconductor manufacturing
content_text:
BASF signs Letter of Intent with Taiwan’s Ministry of Economic Affairs to advance next-generation semiconductor manufacturing
Establishing new production capacity for semiconductor materials supporting chip technologies below 2 nanometers  
Expanding BASF’s Kuanyin site with a strengthened Innovation Center and advanced quality analysis capabilities  
Strengthening supply chain resilience and enhancing customer support in Taiwan and beyond  
Taipei – October 20, 2026 – BASF today signed a Letter of Intent (LOI) with Taiwan’s Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), underscoring its long-term commitment to supporting the growth of Taiwan’s semiconductor ecosystem. Through this investment, BASF’s Electronic Materials business is expanding its Kuanyin site in Taoyuan with additional production capacity for advanced semiconductor materials, enhanced quality analysis capabilities, and an expanded Innovation Center. The investment is designed to support increasing global demand for leading-edge semiconductor manufacturing technologies, including advanced nodes below 2 nanometers, while strengthening supply chain resilience and customer proximity.
“Taiwan is a global hub for semiconductor innovation and manufacturing, with leading-edge process technologies and a highly integrated industry ecosystem. Setting the strategic base for BASF’s global Electronic Materials operations in Taiwan in 2025 reflected the strategic importance of Taiwan within the global semiconductor ecosystem and reinforced our confidence in the market’s long-term growth potential,” said Gops Pillay, President, Global Operating Division of BASF.
As the semiconductor industry progresses toward process nodes below 2 nanometers, demand for advanced, high-purity specialty chemical formulations continues to rise. Through the expansion of its Kuanyin site, BASF will strengthen its Innovation Center and broaden its technical and analytical capabilities for leading-edge semiconductor technologies supporting the AI era. The investment will deepen collaboration with key industry partners, enabling the joint development of next-generation materials while reinforcing Taiwan’s position as a global semiconductor innovation hub.
The investment will further strengthen BASF’s local manufacturing, quality assurance and technical service capabilities in Taiwan, enabling the company to provide customers with a more reliable supply of advanced semiconductor materials, faster technical support, and closer collaboration. At the same time, it will enhance supply chain resilience and reinforce BASF’s role as a trusted long-term partner to the semiconductor industry.
“The signing of this Letter of Intent marks another important milestone in BASF’s long-term commitment to the semiconductor industry,” said Jens Liebermann, Senior Vice President, Global Electronic Materials business and Chairman of BASF Taiwan. “As semiconductor technologies continue to advance, innovation in materials must keep pace with our customers’ evolving needs. By strengthening our local manufacturing, innovation, and technical service capabilities, we are deepening collaboration with our customers and accelerating the development of materials solutions for future technology generations, while further enhancing supply chain resilience.”
As a trusted materials partner to the global semiconductor industry, BASF’s Electronic Materials business has maintained a strong presence in Taiwan for more than two decades. The business provides high-performance process chemicals and customized formulation solutions for the advanced semiconductor and display industry as well as specialized metal systems for consumer electronics applications. 
 
About BASF’s Dispersions & Resins division  
The Dispersions & Resins division of BASF develops, produces and markets a range of high-quality polymer dispersions, resins, additives and electronic materials worldwide. These raw materials are used in formulations for several industries, including coatings, construction, adhesives, printing and packaging, electronics and paper. With its comprehensive product portfolio and extensive knowledge of the industry, the Dispersions & Resins division offers its customers innovative and sustainable solutions and helps them advance their formulations. For further information about the Dispersions & Resins division, please visit  www.dispersions-resins.basf.com 
 
About BASF 
At BASF, we create chemistry for a sustainable future. Our ambition: We want to be the preferred chemical company to enable our customers’ green transformation. We combine economic success with environmental protection and social responsibility. Around 95,000 employees in the BASF Group contribute to the success of our customers in nearly all sectors and almost every country in the world. Our portfolio comprises, as core businesses, the segments Chemicals, Materials, Industrial Solutions, and Nutrition & Care; our standalone businesses are bundled in the segments Surface Technologies and Agricultural Solutions. BASF generated sales of around €60 billion in 2025. BASF shares are traded on the stock exchange in Frankfurt (BAS) and as American Depositary Receipts (BASFY) in the United States. Further information at  www.basf.com

"We delivered another quarter of strong results, including solid sales growth, continued margin expansion, double-digit EPS growth, and robust free cash flow," said William Brown, 3M Chairman and CEO. "Improving productivity through structural transformation and a stronger pipeline of differentiated technologies reinforce our confidence in the full-year outlook and long-term growth and margin potential. Strategic and operational highlights
The following are recently announced highlights:
3M entered into an expanded strategic commercial relationship with Amazon to deploy and scale 3M's optical connectivity and other Data Center related products. 3M issued a warrant to Amazon to purchase up to 3.2 million shares of 3M common stock based upon the achievement of $6 billion in cumulative sales of optical connectivity and other Data Center related products over the next seven years, and other event-based milestones.
3M is collaborating with Genius Electronic Optical Co., Ltd. (GSEO), an optical technology company, to advance technology development and manufacturing for 3M's Expanded Beam Optics (EBO) solutions. In support of these efforts, 3M is investing to acquire ~4.7% of GSEO's common shares. The collaboration brings together 3M's EBO technology leadership, optical interconnect expertise, materials science, manufacturing scale and customer relationships with GSEO's precision optics manufacturing capabilities and production scale.
3M introduced Cooling Film technology for fleet and rail applications , expanding its portfolio of thermal management solutions for transportation customers. Applied to vehicle roofs, the highly reflective performance film uses thermal management technology to reduce heat buildup and help keep interiors noticeably cooler.
3M showcased how its materials science expertise supports innovation in golf equipment through its collaboration with PING . By pairing PING's expertise in club design and custom manufacturing with 3M's broad portfolio of materials science solutions, the two companies can collaborate on engineering solutions that turn complex technical challenges into repeatable, high-quality results on the course.
3M and BOE established a joint innovation laboratory to accelerate next-generation display technology development.  The joint research and development platform brings together BOE's display innovation and end-use application expertise with 3M's materials science capabilities to accelerate higher-performance solutions across LCD, OLED and MLED applications, including improvements in light efficiency, foldable displays and ultra-narrow bezel processes.
3M continued to expand its work with U.S. and international government customers, with third-quarter awards supporting defense, health care, and emergency response needs. Awards included PELTOR™ communication and hearing protection solutions for various U.S. military services and Scott SCBAs for the U.S. Navy, respirator and SCBA products for the National Institutes of Health, and respirators for international customers, reflecting 3M's growing work with government partners around the world.

title: 3M announces collaboration with GSEO to advance Expanded Beam Optical manufacturing and development
content_text:
3M announces collaboration with GSEO to advance Expanded Beam Optical manufacturing and development
Oct 19, 2026 • 5:31 PM EDT 
Download as PDF
ST. PAUL, Minn. , Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- 3M (NYSE: MMM) today announced a collaboration with Genius Electronic Optical Co., Ltd.  (GSEO, Taiwan: 3406), an optical technology company, to advance technology development and manufacturing for 3M's Expanded Beam Optical (EBO) solutions. In support of these efforts, 3M expects to make a strategic investment to acquire approximately 4.7% of GSEO's common shares as part of the company's private placement of newly issued shares, subject to customary closing conditions.
The collaboration brings together 3M's EBO technology leadership, optical interconnect expertise, materials science, manufacturing scale and customer relationships with GSEO's precision optics manufacturing capabilities and production scale. Together, the companies aim to support EBO commercialization and long-term capacity expansion to meet growing demand from hyperscale data centers and other advanced connectivity applications.
"3M is investing in capabilities and partnerships that can accelerate innovation for our customers," said William Brown, 3M Chairman and CEO. "By selecting GSEO as a manufacturing partner and investing in the company, we are strengthening the path to scale next-generation optical connectivity solutions for high-performance data center infrastructure."
GSEO's existing precision optics manufacturing capabilities and technical development experience are expected to support manufacturing readiness for 3M's EBO ferrules, co-packaged optics solutions and related optical interconnect applications. The collaboration is part of 3M's broader EBO ecosystem strategy, which includes continued work with customers and partners across the optical interconnect market.
"GSEO is pleased to expand its relationship with 3M as we work together to advance optical interconnect solutions for next-generation data center infrastructure," said Micro Kuo, GSEO CEO and President. "This collaboration brings together complementary technology and manufacturing strengths to support continued innovation and help meet the performance demands of high-growth connectivity markets."
3M expects the strategic investment to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to customary closing conditions.

title: BASF and HSCC are pursuing a potential joint venture across the polyamide 6 value chain
content_text:
BASF and HSCC are pursuing a potential joint venture across the polyamide 6 value chain
Braine l’Alleud, Belgium, and Fuzhou, China; October 19, 2026 – BASF SE and Highsun Holding Group (HSCC) have signed a non-binding Memorandum of Understanding to explore the combination of their respective European activities across the polyamide 6 (PA6) value chain in a 50:50 joint venture. Additionally, both companies are evaluating the inclusion of their global extrusion activities outside of North America in the joint venture. The engineering plastics downstream businesses of BASF and HSCC are not in scope of the evaluation. 
“The European chemical industry needs to become more competitive. It requires supportive industrial policies as well as consolidation to create stronger companies that are better positioned to compete successfully on a global scale. BASF intends to actively shape this development,” said Dr. Markus Kamieth, Chairman of the Board of Executive Directors of BASF SE. “Together with HSCC, we are exploring opportunities to strengthen our polyamide 6 businesses by combining the most competitive assets, the best technologies and the best commercial expertise both companies have to offer. The combination of selected complementary assets in a cost-efficient setup would strengthen our competitive position through improved asset utilization and lower costs, supporting attractive long-term offerings for our customers.”
Project teams from both companies have been established and will advance the evaluation of the potential cooperation.
As a leading producer of polyamide 6 and precursors, BASF is serving multiple industries including packaging and textiles. With production assets in Ludwigshafen, Germany; Antwerp, Belgium; Caojing, China; and Freeport, Texas, the company operates one of the largest production networks for polyamides worldwide. 
“BASF is a global leading chemical company with outstanding technological capabilities and deep industry heritage. We are looking forward to examining possible collaboration opportunities with BASF to jointly take our polyamide 6 and precursor businesses to the next level. We believe this cooperation could unlock strong synergies between both parties and deliver more competitive products and solutions to customers,” said Chen Zhong, President and CEO of HSCC.
Headquartered in Fuzhou, Fujian Province, China, HSCC is a multinational enterprise integrating chemicals, chemical fibers, and advanced new materials. The group is recognized as a leading producer of caprolactam and operates 31 manufacturing centers at different locations in China as well as in Europe, building a fully integrated value chain from basic chemical raw materials to high end new materials.
  
About BASF 
At BASF, we create chemistry for a sustainable future. Our ambition: We want to be the preferred chemical company to enable our customers’ green transformation. We combine economic success with environmental protection and social responsibility. Around 95,000 employees in the BASF Group contribute to the success of our customers in nearly all sectors and almost every country in the world. Our portfolio comprises, as core businesses, the segments Chemicals, Materials, Industrial Solutions, and Nutrition & Care; our standalone businesses are bundled in the segments Surface Technologies and Agricultural Solutions. BASF generated sales of around €60 billion in 2025. BASF shares are traded on the stock exchange in Frankfurt (BAS) and as American Depositary Receipts (BASFY) in the United States. Further information at  www.basf.com . 
 
About Highsun Holding Group (HSCC)  
Founded in Fujian China in 1984, HSCC, the world’s leading caprolactam producer, delivers comprehensive solutions across the polyamide industry chain and advanced new materials. Headquartered in Changle, Fuzhou, Fujian Province, the company operates four global industrial bases in Fujian Province, Jiangsu Province, Guangdong Province, and Limburg, the Netherlands. Collaborating with leading industry partners, HSCC drives the large-scale adoption of sustainable technologies – including chemical recycling – pioneering the transition to a zero-carbon future. By aligning industrial progress with environmental stewardship, the company fosters a symbiotic relationship between economic growth and planetary well-being. Further information at  www.hscc.com .

title: Chemours and Local Officials Take Action to Protect Refrigerant Intellectual Property at Chillventa
content_text:
Chemours and Local Officials Take Action to Protect Refrigerant Intellectual Property at Chillventa
October 19, 2026
PDF Version 
Action reflects Chemours' commitment to innovation, intellectual property protection, our customers, and fair competition in the refrigerants industry 
WILMINGTON, Del. , Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Chemours Company ("Chemours") (NYSE: CC), a global chemistry company, today announces that it has taken action to protect its intellectual property relating to refrigerant technology during Chillventa 2026 in Nuremberg, Germany . Local courts issued injunctions against four companies infringing upon Chemours' intellectual property and patents of select hydrofluoroolefin (HFO) refrigerant blends.
This action showcases Chemours' unwavering commitment to protecting its innovation and intellectual property investments in advanced refrigerant technologies and across applications. Enforcing intellectual property rights supports industry-wide innovation, fair competition, our customers, and continued technology development.
"Innovation does not happen by accident; it is built on years of research, development, and investment," said Joseph Martinko , President, Thermal & Specialized Solutions at Chemours. "Protecting intellectual property is essential to preserving incentives for innovation, advancing refrigerant technology, and supporting fair competition. Chemours will continue to take appropriate action to defend its intellectual property rights and protect the innovations that help our customers meet evolving industry needs."
Chemours is actively working with enforcement authorities around the globe and educating customers, vendors, and other stakeholders to raise awareness about these Patent Infringing products and the importance of buying genuine refrigerants .
About The Chemours Company 
The Chemours Company (NYSE: CC) is a global leader in providing industrial and specialty chemicals products for markets, including coatings, plastics, refrigeration and air conditioning, transportation, semiconductor and advanced electronics, general industrial, and oil and gas. Through our three businesses – Thermal & Specialized Solutions, Titanium Technologies, and Advanced Performance Materials – we deliver application expertise and chemistry-based innovations that solve customers' biggest challenges. Our flagship products are sold under prominent brands such as Opteon™, Freon™, Ti-Pure™, Nafion™, Teflon™, Viton™, and Krytox™. Headquartered in Wilmington, Delaware and listed on the NYSE under the symbol CC, Chemours has approximately 5,700 employees and 28 manufacturing sites and serves approximately 2,400 customers in approximately 110 countries. For more information, visit chemours.com or follow us on LinkedIn .

title: Research conducted at University of Michigan published in Anesthesia & Analgesia Practice demonstrates GE HealthCare End-tidal Control software may help to reduce fresh gas flow
source: GE Healthcare - Investor News Releases / Investor News / Press Releases
content_text:
Research conducted at University of Michigan published in Anesthesia & Analgesia Practice demonstrates GE HealthCare End-tidal Control software may help to reduce fresh gas flow
October 16, 2026
PDF Version 
Study of nearly 13,000 adult general anesthesia cases found clinician use of End-tidal Control software i at a large multisite academic medical center was associated with a reduction in fresh gas flow, sevoflurane consumption and estimated CO 2 equivalents during maintenance of anesthesia
End-tidal Control software automatically adjusts fresh gas flow concentrations of O 2 and anesthetic agent concentrations to maintain targets set by the clinician, and, as one study shows, with more accuracy versus manual control for safe ii , low-flow iii anesthesia
CHICAGO --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 16, 2026--
GE HealthCare (Nasdaq: GEHC) today announced the publication of research conducted at the University of Michigan iv evaluating the use of End-tidal Control software across a large multisite academic health system in Anesthesia & Analgesia Practice . The retrospective observational study analyzed 12,818 adult general anesthesia cases performed at University of Michigan Health – Ann Arbor locations between April 1, 2023 and September 30, 2024 on anesthesia machines with End-tidal Control software.
The study found End-tidal Control was used in 6,755 cases (52.7%) and its use was associated with:
62.3% reduction in median fresh gas flow during maintenance of anesthesia
39.3% reduction in sevoflurane consumption
“Health systems are looking for practical ways to support clinicians while advancing more sustainable care,” said John Beard , MD, anesthesiologist and Chief Medical Officer of Patient Care Solutions at GE HealthCare . “This research at the University of Michigan adds important real-world evidence of End-tidal Control use at scale and how it may help reduce fresh gas flows and anesthetic agent consumption.”
End-tidal Control software supports the clinician in maintaining clinician-set targets for end-tidal anesthetic agent and oxygen concentrations with greater accuracy than manual adjustments. v End-tidal Control supports low-flow anesthesia, which may help reduce the amount of anesthetic agent utilized and potentially lower greenhouse gas emissions and costs. vi 
“Our team wanted to understand not only if End-tidal Control would be chosen for use in routine practice, but also how its use was associated with anesthesia delivery and environmental measures across a large academic health system,” said Douglas A. Colquhoun, MB ChB, MSc, MPH, Associate Professor of Anesthesiology at the University of Michigan vii . “These findings suggest that End-tidal Control had a high adoption rate and, when used in real-world practice by anesthesia clinical teams it could translate to significant reductions in fresh gas flow resulting in projected cost saving and benefits for the environment.”
The study also found variation in End-tidal Control use was significantly driven by the in-room anesthesia clinician, underscoring the importance of workflow, education and implementation considerations when deploying anesthesia technologies at scale.
GE HealthCare designs anesthesia solutions to support care that can help clinicians think one step ahead. End-tidal Control software can be used with the Aisys™ CS 2 anesthesia delivery system to enhance perioperative care.
About GE HealthCare Technologies Inc. 
GE HealthCare is a leading global healthcare solutions provider of advanced medical technology, pharmaceutical diagnostics, and AI, cloud and software solutions that help clinicians tackle the world’s most complex diseases. Serving patients and providers for 130 years, GE HealthCare is delivering bold innovations designed for the next era of medicine across its Advanced Imaging Solutions, Pharmaceutical Diagnostics and Patient Care Solutions segments to help clinicians deliver more personalized, precise patient care. We are a $20.6 billion business with approximately 54,000 colleagues working to create a world where healthcare has no limits.
GE HealthCare is proud to be among 2026 Fortune World’s Most Admired Companies™.

title: Double recognition for BASF
content_text:
Double recognition for BASF's PA6 recycling pilot technologies: MATERIALICA Award 2026 winner and runner-up at the Fakuma Innovation Award 2026
Depolymerization and solvent-based recycling demonstrated at pilot scale for high-quality recycled materials in automotive applications 
Technologies show potential to support circularity and CO 2 reduction in the automotive industry following further development and scale-up 
Collaboration along the value chain with Mercedes-Benz AG, ZF Group and Pöppelmann K-TECH was essential for the pilot projects 
Ludwigshafen, October 16, 2026 – BASF has received two awards for pilot projects exploring innovative approaches to closing the loop on engineering plastics. The two recycling projects for polyamide 6 (PA6) presented at K 2025 – depolymerization and solvent-based recycling – received both the MATERIALICA Award 2026 (winner in the category “CO 2 Efficiency”) and the Fakuma Innovation Award 2026 (2nd place in the category “sustainability”). The awards recognize the technological progress achieved at pilot scale and the potential of both processes to contribute to closed material loops for demanding automotive applications in the future. Together with Mercedes-Benz, ZF and Pöppelmann K-TECH, the technologies were successfully demonstrated under pilot conditions on near-production components designed to closely reflect real series applications rather than purely demonstrative parts. Further development and scale-up would be required for industrial-scale implementation.
With these two complementary advanced recycling approaches, BASF and the consortium mentioned above are investigating how different waste streams from the automotive industry could be addressed in the future. The pilot projects aim to demonstrate the technical feasibility of recovering high-quality polyamide 6 from end-of-life vehicles and reusing it in demanding engineering applications. 
If successfully developed and scaled to industrial operation, these processes could contribute to meeting future requirements of the European End-of-Life Vehicles Regulation (ELVR), which is driving increased use of recycled materials in vehicles. 
 
Depolymerization: From end-of-life parts back to the monomer 
In the depolymerization pilot, used PA6 components, such as heavily contaminated transmission oil pans from end-of-life vehicles, were chemically broken down into their original monomer, caprolactam. After purification and repolymerization, the material was transformed into PA6 with properties comparable to virgin material. Together with ZF, BASF processed the resulting glass-fiber-reinforced PA6 compound into a stabilizer link for Mercedes-Benz. Under the conditions applied, the components met all mechanical requirements and exhibited processing behavior comparable to virgin material. These results confirm the fundamental technical feasibility of the approach; further work would be required to establish its viability at industrial scale. 
 
Solvent-based recycling unlocks complex waste streams 
Solvent-based recycling was demonstrated at pilot scale using complex waste fractions such as automotive shredder residue (ASR). In the process, PA6 and PA66 were separated from the mixed shredder fraction and cleaned, with PA6 selectively recovered by solvent extraction. Together with Pöppelmann K-TECH, BASF processed the resulting recycled material into a chain guide rail for Mercedes-Benz, a highly stressed engine component with demanding requirements for wear resistance, temperature resistance and media resistance. The results indicate that this approach can technically recover high-quality engineering plastics from complex, previously hard-to-recycle waste streams. Further development and scale-up would be required to assess the potential for industrial implementation, which could ultimately be pursued by other market participants rather than BASF.
 
Recognition for circularity in the automotive industry 
The two award-winning pilot projects demonstrate the technical potential of closed PA6 loops, including the use of waste streams that have previously been difficult or impossible to recycle and the incorporation of recycled materials into highly stressed automotive components. Initial life cycle analyses at pilot-project level also indicate the potential for a significantly reduced Product Carbon Footprint (PCF) compared with virgin material. These findings are promising but do not yet constitute proof of industrial-scale performance.
“Being awarded second place at the Fakuma Innovation Award 2026 and winning the MATERIALICA Award 2026 confirms the potential of our advanced recycling technologies. Together with our partners, we have demonstrated at pilot scale that PA6 from end-of-life vehicles can be recovered and used in demanding automotive components. This is an important proof of technical feasibility on the path towards a truly circular economy,” says Oliver Geiger, Senior Manager Sustainability Performance Materials at BASF.
 
Strong partnerships as a key success factor 
Turning end-of-life vehicles into a source of high-quality materials requires more than technology. It takes a strong ecosystem approach and close collaboration across the value chain. Together, BASF, Mercedes-Benz, ZF and Pöppelmann K-TECH produced real automotive components from recycled end-of-life vehicle PA6 and successfully validated them under pilot conditions. The collaboration provides a foundation for the additional technical, economic and operational work needed before any potential industrial-scale implementation.
 
About BASF  
At BASF, we create chemistry for a sustainable future. Our ambition: We want to be the preferred chemical company to enable our customers’ green transformation. We combine economic success with environmental protection and social responsibility. Around 95,000 employees in the BASF Group contribute to the success of our customers in nearly all sectors and almost every country in the world. Our portfolio comprises, as core businesses, the segments Chemicals, Materials, Industrial Solutions, and Nutrition & Care; our standalone businesses are bundled in the segments Surface Technologies and Agricultural Solutions. BASF generated sales of around €60 billion in 2025. BASF shares are traded on the stock exchange in Frankfurt (BAS) and as American Depositary Receipts (BASFY) in the United States. Further information at www.basf.com . 
About BASF’s Performance Materials division  
BASF’s Performance Materials division drives the transformation of the plastics industry by uniting sustainability with high performance. Our materials expertise, deep industry know-how, and broad product portfolio make us the preferred partner for comprehensive solutions across the plastics lifecycle. With dedicated material-focused teams, strong R&D power, and a global production network close to our customers, we deliver tailored offerings that meet regional and industry specific needs. Our products enhance performance and efficiency in key sectors such as automotive, construction, consumer goods, and industrial applications. Together with our partners, we embark on #OurPlasticsJourney towards a more circular and sustainable future. In 2025, the Performance Materials division achieved global sales of €6.4 billion. 
Join #OurPlasticsJourney on LinkedIn https://on.basf.com/PM_LinkedIn and in our newsletter https://on.basf.com/PM_Newsletter. 
Further information at https://www.performance-materials.basf.com .

title: onsemi and Sungrow Advance Utility-Scale Energy Storage Performance with SiC Hybrid Technology
content_text:
onsemi and Sungrow Advance Utility-Scale Energy Storage Performance with SiC Hybrid Technology
Show side navigation 
October 14, 2026
Share :
Select
Facebook 
Twitter 
LinkedIn 
Advanced EliteSiC hybrid technology maximizes usable energy as electricity demand surges 
Summary 
As AI-driven electricity demand accelerates worldwide, utilities and energy providers are under growing pressure to store and deliver energy more efficiently. Battery energy storage system (BESS) providers are seeking advanced power conversion technologies to improve performance and system economics. To address these needs, Sungrow has adopted onsemi’s latest SiC hybrid power module technology for its PowerTitan 3.0 energy storage platform. The design improves system efficiency, helping utilities and energy providers increase usable energy output while lowering operating costs.
News Highlights 
onsemi’s EliteSiC hybrid power module enables the highest-density battery energy storage system deployments, helping energy providers meet growing electricity demand from AI, renewable energy and electrification
New BESS architecture improves inverter-level efficiency by 0.4%, helping maximize energy delivered to the grid while reducing losses and improving reliability
Sungrow’s PowerTitan 3.0 energy storage platform integrates onsemi’s latest EliteSiC hybrid power module technology, optimized for high-power DC-AC energy conversion in utility-scale battery storage applications
SCOTTSDALE, Ariz., October 14, 2026 — onsemi (Nasdaq: ON) today announced that Sungrow, a global leader in renewable energy technology, has adopted onsemi’s latest EliteSiC silicon carbide (SiC) hybrid power module technology for the Sungrow PowerTitan 3.0 energy storage platform. The integration enables improved efficiency and enhanced system performance for utility-scale battery energy storage systems (BESS).
Helping Sungrow Deliver More Usable Energy 
The PowerTitan 3.0 platform incorporates onsemi’s high-density power integrated modules (PIMs) , optimized for advanced three-level inverter architectures used in high-power energy storage applications.
Compared with the previous-generation platform, the new architecture improves inverter-level efficiency by 0.4%, enabling higher-power battery storage deployments without sacrificing efficiency. The architecture supports power conversion units rated up to 450 kW, contributing to the platform’s increased power density and higher-power deployment capability.
With the performance advantages of SiC , the solution supports key system-level benefits including:
Peak efficiency exceeding 99.3% to reduce energy loss in utility-scale systems
Increased power density supports higher-power BESS deployments
Enhanced thermal performance supports reliable operation in high-power applications
Improved system economics through a hybrid SiC design optimized for large-scale deployment
The design win builds on a long-standing strategic relationship between onsemi and Sungrow. Through extensive engineering and validation activities, the companies collaborated throughout platform definition, system optimization and qualification to meet the demanding performance requirements of next-generation energy storage deployments.
“PowerTitan 3.0 represents Sungrow’s continued innovation in advanced energy storage system design,” said Chen Peng, General Manager of Energy Storage Conversion Product Line at Sungrow Energy Storage Business Unit. “By integrating advanced technologies and collaborating with strategic partners such as onsemi, Sungrow is accelerating the deployment of higher-performance storage solutions that deliver greater value throughout the lifecycle of energy assets. With growing market recognition, Sungrow estimates delivering 10 GWh of PowerTitan 3.0 across Europe in 2026, further supporting the region’s transition toward a more flexible and resilient energy system.”
“At utility scale, even small improvements in power conversion efficiency can have a meaningful impact on battery energy storage system (BESS) performance and total cost of ownership,” said Sergio Fissore, Vice President and General Manager, IPD Power Division, onsemi. “Our EliteSiC hybrid power module enables higher-efficiency, higher-density energy storage systems that help maximize usable energy and improve system reliability. Together with Sungrow, we're advancing the power conversion technologies needed to support the next generation of energy infrastructure.”
Why Fractions of a Percent Matter 
At utility scale, even small efficiency improvements can generate meaningful financial and environmental benefits. According to onsemi analysis, a 0.4% efficiency improvement delivered by the new SiC hybrid module could save more than 475 MWh of energy annually in a 100 MW battery energy storage installation compared with the previous-generation module.
Those energy savings can help reduce operating costs, increase usable energy delivered to customers and lower overall emissions. The architecture also enables higher overload capability and improved thermal performance, helping customers extract more usable energy from every storage asset.
Supporting the Infrastructure Behind the AI Era 
Utilities and energy providers are seeking ways to store more energy, reduce conversion losses and improve overall system economics to meet unprecedented demand amid the AI infrastructure buildout and electrification transition.
Industry forecasts project the battery energy storage market will more than double by 2030 as utilities invest in infrastructure needed to support increasing electricity demand and renewable energy deployment. At the same time, energy storage providers are moving toward higher-power, higher-voltage architectures to improve system economics.

title: Applied Materials Set to Outperform as AI Drives Sustained Demand for Wafer Fab Equipment Press Release Arow1-50 --> > -->
source: Applied Materials - Investor Relations / Investor Relations
content_text:
Applied Materials Set to Outperform as AI Drives Sustained Demand for Wafer Fab Equipment
Oct 13, 2026 at 12:45 PM EDT
PDF Version 
Company expects strong multi-year growth as global AI infrastructure buildout fuels demand for leading-edge foundry-logic, DRAM and advanced packaging – areas where Applied has built market leadership 
Expects wafer fab equipment (WFE) spending to grow faster through 2030 than over the past decade; targets more than 2 percentage points of WFE share gain from calendar 2025 to 2030 
Targets higher profitability through 2030 with non-GAAP gross margin target of approximately 54 percent and non-GAAP operating margin target of approximately 40 percent 
Committed to distribute 80 to 100 percent of free cash flow to shareholders over time 
SAN FRANCISCO , Oct. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- At its 2026 SEMICON West Investor Breakfast Presentation held today, Applied Materials, Inc. presented its longer-term growth expectations and outlined how its leadership in materials engineering positions the company to outperform the wafer fab equipment (WFE) market over the coming years.
“The global buildout of AI infrastructure is driving a new era of growth for wafer fab equipment,” said Gary Dickerson , President and CEO of Applied Materials. “Applied Materials has built leadership in the fastest growing areas of the market that have the greatest impact on AI computing performance, power efficiency and cost, and our advanced services offerings enable chipmakers to increase yield and fab output. Our industry-leading capabilities position Applied for continued growth and outperformance in the years ahead.”
The race for AI computing leadership requires tremendous technology innovation and capacity expansion to support infrastructure scaling, which is fueling sustained WFE investments – bigger than any of the industry’s past growth drivers. The growth and diversity of AI applications from generative to agentic and physical AI require increasing amounts of silicon. Applied expects leading-edge foundry-logic, DRAM and advanced packaging to drive around 75 percent of WFE growth from 2025-2030. Applied has strong number-one process equipment positions in all three areas and is targeting to gain more than 2 percentage points of WFE market share from calendar 2025 to 2030.
To support the industry’s capacity expansion, Applied is utilizing its unique eBeam technology and advanced service solutions to help chipmakers accelerate the ramp of new process nodes and optimize yield, output and cost in high-volume manufacturing. With the industry’s highest resolution and fastest imaging capabilities, Applied’s eBeam equipment portfolio is expected to generate $2 billion in revenue in calendar year 2026. The company is expecting service revenue to grow more than 20 percent this calendar year and to exceed $12 billion in revenue by calendar year 2030, representing a mid-teens compound annual growth rate.
“For the past 10 years, Applied Materials has been making strategic investments to build the industry’s most enabling portfolio for AI computing,” said Brice Hill , Senior Vice President and CFO. “As AI drives wafer fab equipment growth, we are focused on further increasing profitability and operating leverage while investing in R&D programs that will fuel our outperformance into the future.”
Based on the company’s expectations for semiconductor industry growth, Applied is investing to more than double its R&D lab and manufacturing capacity from current levels by 2030. The company yesterday unveiled its new Equipment and Process Innovation and Commercialization (EPIC) Center in Silicon Valley , the world’s largest facility dedicated to collaborative semiconductor process technology and manufacturing equipment R&D. To date, Applied has announced 15 EPIC Center partnerships with leading chipmakers, systems companies, equipment partners and universities. Applied has also recently expanded its manufacturing infrastructure in Austin, Texas , Singapore and Treviso, Italy .
Non-GAAP Financial Measures 
Forward-looking non-GAAP gross margin and non-GAAP operating margin targets for 2030 assume non-GAAP adjustments as applicable for future periods, which we are unable to predict without unreasonable efforts due to their inherent uncertainty. title: Charles River Collaborates with Magellan Stem Cells to Advance Stem Cell and Regenerative Medicine Development
source: Charles River - News Releases / Press Releases
content_text:
View printer-friendly version 
Charles River Collaborates with Magellan Stem Cells to Advance Stem Cell and Regenerative Medicine Development
PDF Version 
Collaboration leverages next-generation sequencing (NGS) services to advance development and commercialization of an off-the-shelf therapy for osteoarthritis and future programs 
WILMINGTON, Mass. --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 13, 2026--
Charles River Laboratories International, Inc. (NYSE: CRL) and Magellan Stem Cells , a private Australian biotech and cell-therapy firm, announce their collaboration to support Magellan in the development and clinical advancement of its proprietary stem cell-based therapies and regenerative medicine solutions. The partnership will leverage Charles River’s specialized expertise in biologics quality control, current Good Manufacturing Practice (cGMP) viral and release testing, and extensive development support services. By integrating Charles River's comprehensive testing and development solutions with Magellan’s advances in cell therapy development, manufacturing and clinical application, the collaboration aims to drive innovation and create shared value.
“Working with organizations at the forefront of innovation allows us to expand our GMP testing capabilities and help accelerate the delivery of safe, compliant therapies to patients,” said Kerstin Dolph , Corporate Senior Vice President, Global Manufacturing, Charles River. “We are excited to support Magellan as they work towards advancing Zelestrocel from the clinic to potential commercialization.”
Charles River will provide viral safety testing using cGMP Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS) for Cell and Gene Therapy (CGT), supporting a high-quality therapy development process aligned with international regulatory standards. Charles River’s NGS service offering highlights the Company's commitment to the 3Rs (Replacement, Reduction, Refinement) through its Alternative Methods Advancement Project™ (AMAP™), which develops and implements New Approach Methodologies (NAMs) and other innovative strategies to reduce reliance on animal testing while supporting efficient product development.
Magellan recently concluded Phase I/II clinical trials of its lead proprietary allogeneic, off-the-shelf stem cell therapy candidate – Zelestrocel - for osteoarthritis and is preparing to launch its pivotal Phase III program. Alongside this, Magellan has purposefully vertically integrated scalable manufacturing capability into its development pathway, having secured GMP certification from the Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) for its manufacturing facility in Melbourne, Australia (1 of only 4 GMP certified cell therapy manufacturing facilities in Australia ).
"As we prepare for the next stage of Zelestrocel's development, having access to advanced testing technologies and collaborating with experienced partners is critical to our success," said Magellan Stem Cells CEO Assoc. Professor Julien Freitag .
Magellan’s COO Nick Bliesner highlights that "Charles River's GMP NGS capabilities provide an innovative approach to viral safety testing that supports both product quality and regulatory readiness. This collaboration strengthens our ability to advance Zelestrocel toward commercialization with confidence."
Modernizing Biologics Testing with NGS
NGS is revolutionizing the way advanced therapeutics are characterized and tested, ensuring high-quality products are delivered to patients. NGS has transformed the landscape of genetic analysis and pathogen detection with its high throughput, scalability, and speed.
Charles River’s cGMP NGS testing services accelerate development timelines without compromising safety and meets regulatory requirements for accuracy, reliability, and compliance with GMP, FDA, EMA, and ICH Q5A and Q5B.
To further enhance NGS capabilities, Charles River has acquired Pathoquest, a leader in NGS solutions for in vitro characterization and quality control testing of biopharmaceutical products. The acquisition enables Charles River to deliver even faster and more advanced sequencing-based testing to clients across the development pipeline.
Biologics Testing Solutions
Backed by decades of cell banking and cell line characterization expertise , Charles River’s full range of CGMP-compliant cell bank production and storage services include 9 CGMP-compliant ISO-6 cleanroom suites, 8-10 week cell bank completion to release, and over 2,000 cell and viral banks produced supporting client programs from research and development through commercial manufacturing.
About the Alternative Methods Advancement Project (AMAP)
The Alternative Methods Advancement Project (AMAP) is a Charles River-led initiative dedicated to developing New Approach Methodologies (NAMs) and exploring innovative scientific and technological solutions aimed at reducing reliance on traditional animal testing. As we enter the next frontier of drug development, AMAP enables strategic, purpose-driven investment to shape a future in which more patients can access the treatments and medicines they need safely, swiftly, and successfully. AMAP is supported by our global, cross-functional Scientific Advisory Board led by Dr. Namandjé N. Bumpus .
About Magellan Stem Cells 
Magellan Stem Cells aims to develop innovative cell therapies with the capability of addressing unmet clinical needs, leading to significant community impact/benefit. Magellan’s leading proprietary cell therapy - Zelestrocel – is a defined allogeneic (donor) stem cell therapy for the treatment of osteoarthritis (OA). Magellan is founded on innovative research and development and clinical application, supported by a vertically integrated and scalable commercial manufacturing platform which provides the opportunity to address the unmet clinical need of OA (which affects >500million people globally). Visit: magellanstemcells.com.au 
About Charles River
Charles River provides essential products and services to help pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, government agencies and leading academic institutions around the globe accelerate their research and drug development efforts. Our dedicated employees are focused on providing clients with exactly what they need to improve and expedite the discovery, early-stage development and safe manufacture of new therapies for the patients who need them. To learn more about our unique portfolio and breadth of services, visit www.criver.com .
