title: Applied Materials Unveils $5 Billion EPIC Center in Silicon Valley to Accelerate Semiconductor Innovation for the AI Era Press Release Arow1-50 --> > -->
source: Applied Materials - Investor Relations / Investor Relations
content_text:
Applied Materials Unveils $5 Billion EPIC Center in Silicon Valley to Accelerate Semiconductor Innovation for the AI Era
Oct 12, 2026 at 4:30 PM EDT
PDF Version 
$5 billion  investment creates the world’s largest semiconductor equipment and process technology R&D facility 
Purpose-built to accelerate the path from breakthrough innovation to high-volume manufacturing of next-generation chipmaking technologies 
Leading chipmakers, systems companies, equipment partners and research universities have committed to develop inside EPIC 
 
SUNNYVALE, Calif. ,  Oct. 12, 2026  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) --  Applied Materials, Inc. , the leader in materials engineering for the semiconductor industry, today unveiled its Equipment and Process Innovation and Commercialization (EPIC) Center, a  $5 billion  capital investment* to build the world’s largest facility dedicated to collaborative semiconductor process technology and manufacturing equipment R&D. Inside the EPIC Center, leading chipmakers, systems companies, equipment partners and university researchers will work side by side with Applied’s scientists and engineers to accelerate the pace of chip innovation for the AI era.
“As AI infrastructure scales, the demands of high-performance computing are driving unprecedented complexity across the chipmaking roadmap,” said  Gary Dickerson , President and CEO of Applied Materials. “To win the race for AI leadership, our industry must rethink and re-engineer how we collaborate to develop and commercialize the next generation of semiconductor technologies. At EPIC, the world’s leading chipmakers, system designers, equipment partners and researchers will work side by side with our teams to accelerate the path from breakthrough materials innovation to high-volume manufacturing faster than ever before.”
Purpose-Built to Accelerate Innovation and Commercialization 
Unveiled today at Applied’s  Sunnyvale, California , campus, the EPIC Center represents one of the most complex R&D construction projects in the world. The 600,000-square-foot structure houses nearly four acres of advanced cleanroom space and required more than six million construction hours to complete. Its foundation holds enough concrete to fill 34 Olympic-sized swimming pools, and its steel-reinforced structure holds enough steel to build two  Eiffel Towers . Thirty-four roof trusses cover the cleanrooms, each spanning nearly 300 feet in length and weighing as much as 12 school buses.
EPIC is designed to reinvent the R&D model the industry has relied on for decades. In the traditional model, foundational materials research happens in one environment, equipment and process development in another, and process integration and pilot production in a third, with a careful handoff at every phase. The EPIC Center is designed to remove these handoffs, putting the people who invent the materials, build the equipment, and make the chips together in a state-of-the-art facility purpose-built for commercialization.
EPIC is founded on a simple conviction: the technologies the AI era demands are too complex and too consequential for any one company to invent alone. The EPIC Center opens with a founding roster that spans the AI technology stack. Founding partners TSMC, Intel, SK hynix, Micron and Samsung Electronics are joined by innovation partners Broadcom, Advantest, SCREEN, KIOXIA, and Besi; and by research partners  Arizona State University ,  Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute ,  Stanford University ,  UC Berkeley , and  UCLA Samueli School of Engineering . Each partner brings its own roadmap challenges and engineers into the facility, working in tight, secure learning cycles alongside Applied teams. Over time, additional companies and organizations are expected to join the EPIC ecosystem.
Leaders from many of the EPIC Center partner companies attended the unveiling event, getting a first glimpse inside the facility. The day started with a summit hosted by Dr.  Prabu Raja , President of the  Semiconductor Products Group  at Applied Materials, where R&D leaders from top semiconductor design, manufacturing and equipment companies discussed key challenges facing growth and progress in the global chip industry.
“Materials innovation has outgrown serial development – at today’s atomic-scale dimensions, many materials and materials interfaces behave in entirely new ways, and making them work at industry scale demands coordinated development and integrated solutions,” said Dr.  Prabu Raja . “EPIC is the only place where materials, process technology and equipment will be innovated in parallel, which increases the success rate of new materials and technologies. Because our customers’ own engineers help optimize the technology before it ever reaches their factory, what leaves EPIC arrives at the fab ready to ramp to high performance and high yield sooner.”
Applied expects the EPIC operating model to deliver returns on both sides of the partnerships. Chipmakers gain earliest access to next-generation materials and equipment, shorter learning cycles and a faster path to volume production. Applied gains visibility across several generations of emerging technology challenges, informing where the company directs its R&D investments to create value for customers and have its systems and services designed in.
Supporting Quotes from Industry and Academic Leaders 
“For three decades, TSMC and Applied Materials have grown together – pushing the boundaries of semiconductor technology through every major transition. Thirty years ago, the leading-edge production node was 350 nanometers. Today, it is 2 nanometers. Working hand-in-hand with the industry, we have shrunk features 175-fold. As chipmaking complexity grows exponentially, our partnership is more vital than ever. Beyond 2nm, collaborating with Applied gives us early access to the disruptive equipment technologies that define the future. This fast-tracks the leap from R&D to high-volume manufacturing for the energy-efficient AI architectures of tomorrow – including new architecture, low-resistance wiring, and advanced packaging. We are proud to be a founding partner of EPIC, accelerating the innovations that will power AI from the data center to the edge.” – Dr.  C.C. Wei , Chairman and CEO of TSMC 
“AI is creating a multi-trillion-dollar opportunity for the semiconductor industry. To capture it, we need continued innovation in transistors, interconnects and advanced packaging. At Intel, we see a path to more than a trillion transistors in a package by 2030. As architectures become more complex and R&D costs continue to rise, we need to move faster and work more closely with our equipment partners. EPIC gives our teams the opportunity to work side by side with Applied on materials and process innovation – helping us accelerate development, improve R&D efficiency and bring new technologies to market faster.” –  Lip-Bu Tan , CEO, Intel 
“Data-intensive AI workloads are driving massive demand for high-performance memory and storage, and innovation in materials and process technology is a critical enabler of next-generation memory. As a founding partner of EPIC, Micron will work side by side with Applied Materials to accelerate innovation and bring next-generation memory technologies from research to high-volume manufacturing at scale.” –  Sanjay Mehrotra , Chairman and CEO, Micron Technology 
“The defining challenge of AI computing is moving data fast enough to keep increasingly powerful processors fully utilized, and meeting that challenge requires memory with far greater bandwidth, speed and capacity. At EPIC, SK hynix and Applied will bring together our leadership in advanced memory with Applied’s leadership in materials engineering and semiconductor manufacturing technology to address major inflections across HBM, DRAM and NAND, and accelerate memory innovation for the AI era.” – Nohjung Kwak, President and CEO of SK hynix 
“Samsung takes an end-to-end view of AI-era computing – across leading-edge logic, memory and advanced packaging. Applied Materials brings uniquely broad process equipment leadership across all three domains, and at EPIC together we will develop, iterate and deploy breakthrough technologies faster than ever, at the pace AI scaling demands.” – Jaihyuk Song, Chief Technology Officer (CTO) of Device Solutions Division, Samsung Electronics 
“The next frontier of AI will be defined by how seamlessly the industry can integrate vast amounts of compute, memory and connectivity into high-performance systems, and that depends on breakthrough advances in advanced packaging. As an innovation partner at EPIC, Broadcom can engage earlier with Applied’s foundational technologies and manufacturing capabilities, connecting future system requirements to the packaging innovations needed to realize them and accelerating the path from concept to commercialization.” –  Charlie Kawwas , Ph.D., President of  Semiconductor Solutions Group , Broadcom 
“Future performance improvements will depend on advanced 3D architectures and heterogeneous integration. As these technologies converge, it becomes increasingly important to connect insights from front-end process development with those from back-end test and measurement. EPIC breaks down these traditional barriers by bringing together Applied Materials’ leadership in materials engineering and process control with Advantest's leadership in semiconductor test and measurement, including capabilities enabled through the Advantest Innovation Center. Together, we are helping the world’s leading semiconductor manufacturers improve yield, accelerate production ramps, and bring next-generation AI systems to market faster.” –  Doug Lefever , Representative Director and Group CEO, Advantest Corporation 
“At EPIC, we have a unique opportunity to co-optimize the critical wet and dry processes behind next-generation chip architectures. We can together accelerate the innovations required to master increasingly complex 3D devices and advanced packaging structures. By driving tighter process integration with materials engineering, we can help chipmakers unlock higher yields, faster production ramps, and the manufacturing scale required for the AI future.” –  Masato Goto , President and CEO, SCREEN Holdings Co., Ltd. 
“AI is making the world increasingly data-driven, and future breakthroughs will depend on memory, logic, and interconnect technologies working seamlessly within integrated systems. We believe the EPIC Center provides a powerful platform for collaboration across technology domains. By working closely with Applied Materials engineers and other partners, we can accelerate the development of next-generation memory technologies.” –  Hideshi Miyajima , Ph.D., Managing Executive Officer and Chief Technology Officer,  KIOXIA Corporation 
“The future of AI depends not only on more powerful chips, but on the chip-to-chip interconnects that drive performance, bandwidth and power efficiency. Besi and Applied recognized early that hybrid bonding would be foundational to next-generation AI systems, and by combining Besi’s leadership in precision die-to-wafer bonding with Applied’s leadership in front-end processing, we are advancing hybrid bonding technology to enable future high-performance 3D integrated devices. EPIC extends that model of high-velocity co-innovation across the ecosystem, accelerating the technologies that will shape future AI systems.” –  Richard Blickman , President and CEO, BE Semiconductor Industries (Besi) 
“ASU has developed a very strong working relationship with Applied Materials through the Materials-to-Fab Center at  ASU Research Park , and we are excited to dig deeper into this partnership at the EPIC Center, where researchers, engineers and manufacturers converge to accelerate bold ideas from the lab to breakthroughs in the fab. EPIC will also serve as a cornerstone for the semiconductor talent pipeline and by working alongside Applied’s scientists and engineers, our students will gain the systems-level perspective needed to drive the future of AI innovation.” –  Michael Crow , President,  Arizona State University 
“UC Berkeley has helped shape microelectronics from its earliest days, advancing the research and talent that continue to propel the semiconductor industry, and our collaboration with Applied Materials is a great example of how academia and industry must work together to meet the scale and opportunity of what’s ahead. The EPIC platform gives our researchers access to the same cutting-edge capabilities used by the world’s leading chipmakers, within a manufacturing-relevant environment, so ideas can be tested, refined and transformed much faster into the semiconductor breakthroughs that will advance the frontier of AI.” –  Rich Lyons , Chancellor,  UC Berkeley 
“Many of the technologies powering today’s AI revolution began in university labs years, often decades, before they transformed the world. As computing demand increases, we must accelerate the pace at which new semiconductor materials, devices and integration technologies move from discovery to deployment. As an inaugural research partner at the EPIC Center, RPI’s students and researchers gain access to world-class experts and a direct pathway to test and validate academic advances in real-world production environments – a powerful blueprint for high-velocity industry-academia collaboration in the AI era.” –  Martin Schmidt , President of RPI 
“The explosive growth of AI is pushing semiconductor technology researchers to find new ways to increase energy efficiency of semiconductor chips. Opportunities abound in discovering new materials and inventing new devices. Experimentation demands faster cycles of innovation and closer collaboration across the ecosystem. Beyond the existing broad research engagement between  Stanford  faculty and Applied Materials, the EPIC Center presents an additional opportunity that enables our students and researchers to engage directly with industry-scale tools and experts, accelerating discovery while gaining the industry-relevant experience needed to lead future advances in semiconductor manufacturing.” –  H.S. Philip Wong , Willard R. and  Inez Kerr Bell Professor  in the  School of Engineering ,  Stanford University 
“Accelerating semiconductor innovation in the new era of AI requires transformative collaboration between universities and industry partners more than ever before. UCLA has a long history of pioneering semiconductor research and innovation, and our collaboration with Applied Materials at the EPIC Center builds on that legacy by bringing together university research and industry expertise to advance the chip technologies that will define the future of computing while preparing the next generation of engineers.” – Ah-Hyung “Alissa” Park, Ronald and  Valerie Sugar Dean  of UCLA Samueli 
*Capital spending is expected to scale over time to approximately $5 billion as customer projects commence.

About the EPIC Center 
The EPIC Center (Equipment and Process Innovation and Commercialization) is Applied Materials’ flagship R&D facility in Silicon Valley, designed to compress the timeline from early-stage materials research to high-volume semiconductor manufacturing. By bringing chipmakers, equipment partners and university researchers into the same building as Applied’s scientists and engineers, EPIC enables parallel rather than sequential development of materials, equipment and process technology, shortening learning cycles and accelerating the commercialization of the innovations that will power the AI era. Learn more at www.appliedmaterials.com/us/en/epic.html .
About Applied Materials 
Applied Materials, Inc. (Nasdaq: AMAT) is the leader in materials engineering solutions that are at the foundation of virtually every new semiconductor and advanced display in the world. The technology we create is essential to advancing AI and accelerating the commercialization of next-generation chips. At Applied, we push the boundaries of science and engineering to deliver material innovation that changes the world. Learn more at www.appliedmaterials.com .

\r\n $5 billion investment creates the world’s largest semiconductor equipment and process technology R&D facility

\r\n Leading chipmakers, systems companies, equipment partners and research universities have committed to develop inside EPIC

$5 billion investment creates the world’s largest semiconductor equipment and process technology R&D facility 
Purpose-built to accelerate the path from breakthrough innovation to high-volume manufacturing of next-generation chipmaking technologies 
Leading chipmakers, systems companies, equipment partners and research universities have committed to develop inside EPIC 
SUNNYVALE, Calif., Oct. 12, 2026 – Applied Materials, Inc., the leader in materials engineering for the semiconductor industry, today unveiled its Equipment and Process Innovation and Commercialization (EPIC) Center, a $5 billion capital investment* to build the world’s largest facility dedicated to collaborative semiconductor process technology and manufacturing equipment R&D. Inside the EPIC Center, leading chipmakers, systems companies, equipment partners and university researchers will work side by side with Applied’s scientists and engineers to accelerate the pace of chip innovation for the AI era.
\r\n “As AI infrastructure scales, the demands of high-performance computing are driving unprecedented complexity across the chipmaking roadmap,” said Gary Dickerson, President and CEO of Applied Materials. “To win the race for AI leadership, our industry must rethink and re-engineer how we collaborate to develop and commercialize the next generation of semiconductor technologies. At EPIC, the world’s leading chipmakers, system designers, equipment partners and researchers will work side by side with our teams to accelerate the path from breakthrough materials innovation to high-volume manufacturing faster than ever before.”
\r\n 
\r\nPurpose-Built to Accelerate Innovation and Commercialization 
\r\n Unveiled today at Applied’s Sunnyvale, California, campus, the EPIC Center represents one of the most complex R&D construction projects in the world. The 600,000-square-foot structure houses nearly four acres of advanced cleanroom space and required more than six million construction hours to complete. Its foundation holds enough concrete to fill 34 Olympic-sized swimming pools, and its steel-reinforced structure holds enough steel to build two Eiffel Towers. Thirty-four roof trusses cover the cleanrooms, each spanning nearly 300 feet in length and weighing as much as 12 school buses.

content_text:
Applied Materials and UCLA Engineering Accelerate Semiconductor Innovation at the EPIC Center
Oct 8, 2026 at 4:05 PM EDT
PDF Version 
R&D programs to focus on speeding up the commercialization pipeline so chip technology moves from breakthrough research to full-scale manufacturing faster 
Collaborative work at the state-of-the-art facility in Silicon Valley pairs UCLA’s semiconductor research strength with Applied’s cutting-edge chipmaking equipment and process integration expertise 
SANTA CLARA, Calif. , Oct. 08, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Applied Materials, Inc. today announced that the UCLA Samueli School of Engineering will join the company’s EPIC Center in Silicon Valley as a research partner. Together with Applied’s scientists and engineers, UCLA researchers will work to solve semiconductor materials and integration challenges with a focus on shortening the time it takes to bring breakthrough research to commercialization.
“As the industry races to bring new AI chip technologies to market, the EPIC Center will play a pivotal role by convening the industry’s top innovators in a collaborative environment designed to accelerate the path from breakthrough research to full-scale manufacturing,” said Dr. Prabu Raja , President of the Semiconductor Products Group at Applied Materials. “UCLA has a long history of semiconductor technology innovation and Applied looks forward to welcoming their researchers to the EPIC Center where together we will work to solve the industry’s toughest challenges.”
The EPIC Center aims to accelerate chip R&D by bridging the gap between traditional academic innovation and industrial-scale development. UCLA researchers will have access to advanced chipmaking tools so that new ideas can be validated and tested in a commercial fab environment, thereby shortening the path from concept to production.
UCLA Samueli brings extensive expertise across semiconductor devices, materials, electronics and computing. In 1991, Henry Samueli co-founded Broadcom Corporation while teaching at UCLA . The school is also home to the Center for Heterogeneous Integration and Performance Scaling (CHIPS) Lab , which brings together researchers across disciplines to advance semiconductor technologies and address challenges in chip design, manufacturing and integration.
By collaborating at the EPIC Center, Applied Materials and UCLA will focus R&D programs on the semiconductor industry’s most critical challenges in areas including 3D chip scaling, advanced packaging and the discovery of new materials for improving energy-efficient AI compute performance. The work will complement and extend the efforts of UCLA’s Semiconductor Hub , which Applied joined as a co-founding member earlier this year. Applied’s ongoing commitment to strengthen the ties between industry and academia is aimed at empowering the next generation of engineers and researchers to bring semiconductor breakthroughs to market faster.
“Accelerating semiconductor innovation in the new era of AI requires transformative collaboration between universities and industry partners more than ever before,” said Ah-Hyung “Alissa” Park, Ronald and Valerie Sugar Dean of UCLA Samueli. “UCLA has a long history of pioneering semiconductor research and innovation, and this collaboration builds on that legacy by bringing together university research and industry expertise to advance the chip technologies that will define the future of computing while preparing the next generation of engineers.”
Applied’s new EPIC (Equipment and Process Innovation and Commercialization) Center in Silicon Valley represents the largest-ever U.S . investment in advanced semiconductor equipment R&D. The center is designed from the ground up to dramatically reduce the time it takes to commercialize breakthrough technologies from early-stage research to full-scale manufacturing. The facility is on track to become operational in 2026. Visit the EPIC Center website to learn more.

title: TOPPAN to Participate in ‘Rapidus CORE’ Global Ecosystem Framework
content_text:
TOPPAN to Participate in ‘Rapidus CORE’ Global Ecosystem Framework
Offering input on cutting-edge semiconductors as a Design Solution Associate to contribute to LSI design and development
Tweet 
Tokyo – October 8, 2026 – TOPPAN Inc. (TOPPAN), a TOPPAN Group company and wholly owned subsidiary of TOPPAN Holdings Inc. (TYO: 7911), will participate as a Design Solution Associate in the Rapidus Collaborative Open Rapid Ecosystem (Rapidus CORE)—a global ecosystem framework for the development and mass production of cutting-edge semiconductors to be established by Rapidus Corporation (Rapidus).
Background & Objectives
In recent years, driven by the rapid growth of AI, high-performance computing, and automated driving technologies, global demand has surged for cutting-edge logic semiconductors that deliver both exceptional processing power and high energy efficiency. Consequently, semiconductor manufacturing processes are transitioning to next-generation nodes, starting with the 2 nm generation. However, as process miniaturization advances, Large-Scale Integration (LSI) design has become extraordinarily complex. Increased risks in manufacturing lead to costly redesigns and heavier verification workloads, driving up development costs and lengthening time-to-market. Addressing these challenges requires advanced design solutions that seamlessly bridge design and manufacturing, alongside open collaborative frameworks.
To drive innovation across the entire semiconductor value chain—from design to front-end and back-end processes—and to accelerate next-generation LSI development by creating partner-driven value beyond traditional supply chain boundaries, Rapidus has launched Rapidus CORE, a global ecosystem framework.
As part of the initial rollout of Rapidus CORE, Rapidus announced Design Solution Associates, a group of design-related companies in which TOPPAN will participate. Design Solution Associates connect customers with Rapidus, providing specialized engineering resources and technical expertise to facilitate the rapid launch of semiconductor development. This collaborative model strengthens support systems from design through manufacturing tailored to diverse customer needs.
Some of TOPPAN’s core strengths are its expertise built over many years in LSI design technology and the optimization of Electronic Design Automation (EDA) environments. In particular, TOPPAN possesses extensive technical know-how in complex design solutions required for advanced process nodes, including low-power design, timing closure addressing Process, Voltage, Temperature (PVT) variations, and high-speed interface implementation.
By joining Rapidus CORE as a Design Solution Associate, TOPPAN will offer end-to-end support for Rapidus customers—from initial specification analysis to circuit design, layout, and physical verification. In doing so, TOPPAN will help significantly reduce the design complexity, cost, and risks associated with cutting-edge process nodes, contributing to establishing a sustainable semiconductor ecosystem.
Future Goals
In addition to contributing to establishing a sustainable ecosystem for next-generation semiconductors, through participation in Rapidus CORE, TOPPAN will contribute to creating new value as well as resolving societal issues by leveraging cutting-edge semiconductor technology.
About the TOPPAN Group
Established in Tokyo in 1900, the TOPPAN Group is a leading and diversified global provider committed to delivering sustainable, integrated solutions in fields including printing, communications, security, packaging, décor materials, electronics, and digital transformation. The TOPPAN Group’s global team of more than 50,000 employees offers optimal solutions enabled by industry-leading expertise and technologies to address the diverse challenges of every business sector and society and contribute to the achievement of shared sustainability goals.

title: TOPPAN at Hydrogen Technology World Expo 2026
content_text:
TOPPAN at Hydrogen Technology World Expo 2026
Unveiling performance data for upgraded CCMs and MEAs ideal for green hydrogen production using renewable energy
Tweet 
Tokyo – October 8, 2026 –TOPPAN Holdings Inc. (TYO: 7911) (TOPPAN Holdings) announced its upcoming participation at the Hydrogen Technology World Expo scheduled to be held in Hamburg, Germany, from October 20 to 22. 
As one of Europe’s leading hydrogen technology related events, Hydrogen Technology World Expo enjoys participation from a broad spectrum of companies across the hydrogen supply chain. The TOPPAN Holdings booth (no. 7G48) will present high-performance and high-quality electrode components (CCMs and MEAs) that can be applied in various processes involved in the production, storage, distribution, and utilization of hydrogen.
Background
Countries and regions around the world are advancing measures to achieve carbon neutrality by 2050, including renewable energy use and initiatives to enable a hydrogen society. There are high expectations for hydrogen as an energy source because it is generated from an abundant resource in the form of water and no CO 2 is emitted when used.
For the practical use of hydrogen in society, Catalyst Coated Membranes (CCMs) and Membrane Electrode Assemblies (MEAs) are critical components that determine the efficiency and economic performance of hydrogen-related applications. To this end, TOPPAN Holdings has been conducting CCM and MEA research and development since 2004 to address challenges related to performance and durability. Building on these efforts, TOPPAN aims to expand its provision of CCMs and MEAs to Europe and other markets throughout the world.
Main Solutions on Show
The booth will showcase high-performance, high-quality CCMs and MEAs that are fabricated using proprietary materials, a sheet-to-sheet process and double-sided direct coating technique developed by TOPPAN Holdings.
① CCMs for water electrolysis
Alongside a 600×800 mm CCM display, TOPPAN will unveil for the first time the core specifications of its upgraded CCMs. TOPPAN Holdings' CCMs feature high durability against voltage fluctuations, making them ideally suited for water electrolysis powered by renewable energy and contributing to the expanded adoption of green hydrogen.
TOPPAN Holdings is advancing the development of large-area CCMs in the 1.5 m × 2.5 m class. Adopting these large-area CCMs is expected to lower both capital expenditure (CAPEX) and operational expenditure (OPEX) by reducing the required number of CCM sheets and auxiliary equipment, while also contributing to lower power consumption.
② MEAs for fuel cells
TOPPAN Holdings will present five- and seven-layer MEAs stacked with subgaskets 1 and GDLs 2 that employ the TOPPAN Holding’s proprietary catalyst layer design technology. By utilizing patented proprietary materials, the technology achieves both high voltage retention performance and superior durability, even under high-load operating conditions. Consequently, applications that were previously restricted to low-load operation to preserve durability can now achieve higher power output through high-load operation, directly meeting the needs of customers seeking high-output solutions.
③ Reaction Enhancement Plate (REP)
The Reaction Enhancement Plate (REP) developed by TOPPAN Holdings is a metallic plate featuring precision micro-slits. Integrating it into a fuel cell stack increases overall system power output without requiring modifications to the MEA. At this exhibition, TOPPAN Holdings will display the REP alongside a mockup of the fuel cell stack used during testing and reveal evaluation data demonstrating its power enhancement performance for the first time.

title: AVerMedia and Stereolabs Accelerate AI Vision Deployment with NVIDIA JetPack 7.2
content_text:
AVerMedia and Stereolabs Accelerate AI Vision Deployment with NVIDIA JetPack 7.2
October 7, 2026
PDF Version 
Unified integration delivers faster time to market, broad camera compatibility, and more efficient use of memory across Jetson Orin and Thor modules 
TAIPEI, Taiwan & PARIS--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 7, 2026-- AVerMedia Technologies, Inc. and Stereolabs , an Ouster company, today announced NVIDIA JetPack 7.2 support across all Stereolabs ZED X GMSL cameras and AVerMedia’s NVIDIA Jetson carrier boards, offering robotics and edge AI developers a faster and more efficient path from development to production.
This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261007896664/en/ 
AVerMedia and Stereolabs Accelerate AI Vision Deployment with NVIDIA JetPack 7.2
The collaboration combines AVerMedia’s NVIDIA Jetson carrier-board and Board Support Package (BSP) engineering expertise with Stereolabs’ unified ZED X driver architecture. With this approach, AVerMedia can adapt the hardware-specific device tree and generate drivers for the JetPack and Jetson Linux versions required by customers, reducing the repeated exchanges previously required for each hardware or software update.
This collaboration allows AVerMedia hardware development and Stereolabs software releases to progress in parallel, shortening validation cycles and giving customers greater control over product schedules.
The unified workflow allows Stereolabs to focus on camera firmware, ISP performance, and ZED SDK capabilities, while AVerMedia manages the carrier-board-specific integration and validation required for production deployment.
More AI Capability from Available Jetson Memory 
Memory is a critical resource in embedded AI systems, particularly when multiple camera streams, perception models, and robotics applications must run simultaneously on a single Jetson module.
NVIDIA JetPack 7.2 introduces Jetson agent skills that help developers optimize memory usage across the software stack. These agent-driven workflows can tune bootloader carveouts, optimize kernel memory reservations, streamline user-space services, and improve inference memory usage. These optimizations free up critical memory for vision processing and AI workloads, enabling richer applications on smaller memory footprints and lowering total cost of ownership.
Key Customer Benefits:
Faster time to market: Hardware modifications and software releases can be integrated and validated more efficiently.
Broad compatibility: NVIDIA JetPack 7.2 supports all Stereolabs cameras across AVerMedia’s NVIDIA Jetson carrier-board portfolio, including Jetson Orin and Jetson Thor platforms.
More efficient memory utilization: Developers can make more memory available for camera processing, AI models, and robotics applications.
Greater software control: Reproducible Debian packages provide traceability of the driver, device tree, installation flow, and kernel code used in production.
Simplified lifecycle management: Drivers can be regenerated for required JetPack and Linux versions, supporting long-term maintenance, compliance, and product updates.
“By anchoring the platform-specific integration work with AVerMedia, where we’re doubling down on both companies’ hardware expertise, both teams can develop in parallel and respond to customer requirements more quickly,” said Ihsane Debbache , VP of Engineering at Stereolabs. “This integration gives developers a more efficient path to deploying Stereolabs ZED vision across AVerMedia Jetson platforms.”
NVIDIA JetPack 7.2 also provides official Yocto support, giving developers greater control over reproducible, production-ready software images for Jetson Orin and Jetson Thor platforms.
“Customers need both faster integration and more efficient use of their computing resources,” said Alex Liu , Vice President of AVerMedia. “By combining Stereolabs’ vision technology and AVerMedia’s BSP and hardware engineering expertise, we can help customers reduce integration risk, make better use of available Jetson memory, and deploy more capable AI vision systems faster.”

title: Charles River and Autolomous Partner to Transform Laboratory Execution Systems
source: Charles River - News Releases / Press Releases

Charles River and Autolomous Partner to Transform Laboratory Execution Systems
PDF Version 
Partnership reinforces continued investment in digitization, automation, and client-facing transparency 
WILMINGTON, Mass. & LONDON --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 6, 2026--
Charles River Laboratories International, Inc. (NYSE: CRL) and Autolomous today announced the launch of Apollo Orchestrate™, a new capability within Charles River's Apollo ® platform that connects and digitizes laboratory execution, built on Autolomous's autoloMATE ® digital Laboratory Execution System (LES). The launch demonstrates continued progress on   Charles River's strategic commitment to modernize and digitize laboratory workflows. Apollo ® Orchestrate™ marks a significant milestone in the Company’s broader, ongoing transition toward a fully digital laboratory experience which is connected, compliant, and scalable.
The deployment brings Apollo Orchestrate's digital execution and workflow-automation capabilities, powered by Autolomous’s autoloMATE, to Charles River Biologics Testing Solutions sites across North America and Europe , supporting quality control (QC) testing within the Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) setting. Apollo Orchestrate connects Charles River's laboratory systems, including Apollo and LabWare LIMS, supporting digital traceability from sample submission through execution to release.
"Apollo Orchestrate aligns with our modernization strategy, providing an end-to-end digital experience to deliver safe and effective medicines swiftly and safely to patients," said Kerstin Dolph , Corporate Senior Vice President of Global Manufacturing, Charles River. "The launch of Apollo Orchestrate, built on Autolomous' autoloMATE platform, will increase efficiency while providing greater transparency and collaboration for our clients."
This marks an important step in Charles River's ongoing development of an integrated digital laboratory ecosystem, enabling a more seamless workflow focused on getting results to the client in a rapid and accurate manner.
Enabled by autoloMATE’s LES, Apollo Orchestrate connects sample submission, laboratory execution, and review into one digital workflow and shifts records from paper to digital, with a path to greater client visibility over time. It enhances efficiency by minimizing manual processes, improving data accuracy, accelerating execution and review, and allowing technical and QA teams to spend less time on administrative review and more on scientific, quality, and client-focused work. Initial deployment within the GMP setting for QC testing will establish a standardized, scalable operating model for expansion across Biologics Testing Solutions sites following the initial go-live.
"Biological testing ensures that a medicine is safe, effective, and ready for patients, but data collection and management across fragmented, often manual and paper-based systems from R&D to commercial release create unnecessary delays for patients, opportunities for errors, audit risks, and lost revenue," said Alexander Seyf, CEO of Autolomous. "We designed autoloMATE to enable life sciences companies to connect that data directly into an integrated, digitized workflow and increase speed, accuracy, and cost-effectiveness."
Biologics Testing Solutions
Backed by decades of cell banking and cell line characterization expertise , Charles River’s full range of CGMP-compliant cell bank production and storage services include 9 CGMP-compliant ISO, 6 cleanroom suites, 8-10 weeks cell bank completion to release, and over 2,000 cell and viral banks produced supporting client programs from research and development through commercial manufacturing.
About Autolomous
Autolomous helps life sciences customers worldwide achieve significant cost and time savings and build resilient manufacturing and supply chains through end-to-end digitization. Powered by advanced technology and artificial intelligence, autoloMATE ® is a cloud-native, AI-enabling, modular platform that integrates seamlessly with existing systems. By creating a digital backbone across manufacturing and supply chain operations - from planning through release - autoloMATE delivers measurable gains in productivity, scalability, and cost-effectiveness. Its modular architecture allows each deployment to be configured precisely to customer needs, while the intuitive design ensures ease of use across the organization. Explore more at www.autolomous.com .
About Charles River
Charles River provides essential products and services to help pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, government agencies and leading academic institutions around the globe accelerate their research and drug development efforts. Our dedicated employees are focused on providing clients with exactly what they need to improve and expedite the discovery, early-stage development and safe manufacture of new therapies for the patients who need them. To learn more about our unique portfolio and breadth of services, visit www.criver.com .

title: Applied Materials and Intel Collaborate to Accelerate Chipmaking Innovations for AI-Driven Computing
source: Applied Materials - Applied Materials Newsroom / Newsroom / News
content_text:
Applied Materials and Intel Collaborate to Accelerate Chipmaking Innovations for AI-Driven Computing
Oct 6, 2026 at 9:00 AM EDT
\r\n PDF Version 
\r\n \r\n Collaborations at Applied’s EPIC Center in Silicon Valley and Intel’s R&D campus in Oregon aim to develop breakthroughs in next-generation transistors, interconnects and advanced packaging technologies for AI chips and systems 
\r\n Collaboration builds on the companies’ long history of working together to solve complex semiconductor device scaling challenges 
\r\n \r\n SANTA CLARA, Calif., Oct. 6, 2026 – Applied Materials, Inc. (Nasdaq: AMAT), the leader in materials engineering for the semiconductor industry, today announced it is working with Intel Corporation (Nasdaq: INTC) to accelerate development of chipmaking innovations for next-generation transistors, interconnects and advanced packaging technologies. The collaboration will bring together cutting-edge capabilities from Applied’s EPIC Center in Silicon Valley and Intel’s R&D campus in Hillsboro, Oregon to shorten time-to-market of advanced semiconductor technologies essential to AI computing.        
\r\n “Applied and Intel share a decades-long history of deep collaboration focused on pushing the boundaries of materials engineering to advance the semiconductor roadmap,” said Gary Dickerson, President and CEO of Applied Materials. “Bringing our teams together at the EPIC Center will deepen that partnership and accelerate the transistor, interconnect and packaging innovations needed to drive the future of AI computing.”
\r\n “The demand for AI computing is driving the need for major advances in performance, power efficiency, and packaging. Intel is focused on delivering those innovations and doing it in close collaboration with partners across the ecosystem,” said Lip-Bu Tan, CEO of Intel. “Applied Materials is an important partner, and we look forward to expanding our work together at the EPIC Center to help accelerate the path from the lab to high-volume manufacturing in the United States.”
\r\n Teams from Applied Materials and Intel are collaborating on next-generation materials, process technologies and device architectures for advanced logic nodes targeting AI workloads, and will continue this work at the EPIC Center. The collaboration spans both front-end and back-end-of-line advancements, including interconnect scaling. The collaboration also involves development of advanced packaging technologies for Foveros-based 3D stacking, supporting higher interconnect density, improved power delivery, and enhanced thermal performance for high-performance compute platforms designed to accelerate emerging agentic AI workloads.
\r\n “With the chipmaking roadmap becoming more complex at each process node, accelerating innovations in semiconductor devices, interconnects and packaging requires deeper collaboration across R&D and manufacturing,” said Dr. Prabu Raja, President of the Semiconductor Products Group at Applied Materials. “We look forward to working closely with Intel as a founding partner of the EPIC Center to shorten development cycles and bring new technologies to market faster.”
\r\n “Accelerating our R&D to keep pace with the rapid buildout of AI infrastructure is critical to delivering the technology, manufacturing excellence and foundry services our customers expect from Intel Foundry,” said Naga Chandrasekaran, Executive Vice President, Chief Technology and Operations Officer and General Manager of Intel Foundry. “Applied Materials’ new EPIC Center provides an environment where our teams can collaborate even more closely and at higher velocity to accelerate materials development and process innovations.”
\r\n Applied’s new EPIC (Equipment and Process Innovation and Commercialization) Center in Silicon Valley, which is scheduled to be operationally ready this year, is designed from the ground up to dramatically reduce the time it takes to commercialize breakthrough technologies from early-stage research to full-scale manufacturing. For chipmakers, the EPIC Center will provide earlier access to Applied’s R&D portfolio, faster cycles of learning and accelerated transfer of next-generation technologies into high-volume manufacturing, within a secure collaborative environment. In addition, the co-innovation programs at the EPIC Center will provide Applied with greater multi-node visibility to guide R&D investments while increasing R&D productivity and value sharing.

All forward-looking statements are based on management’s current estimates, projections and assumptions, and Applied assumes no obligation to update them.

The technology we create is essential to advancing AI and accelerating the commercialization of next-generation chips. SANTA CLARA, Calif., Oct. 6, 2026 – Applied Materials, Inc. (Nasdaq: AMAT), the leader in materials engineering for the semiconductor industry, today announced it is working with Intel Corporation (Nasdaq: INTC) to accelerate development of chipmaking innovations for next-generation transistors, interconnects and advanced packaging technologies. The collaboration will bring together cutting-edge capabilities from Applied’s EPIC Center in Silicon Valley and Intel’s R&D campus in Hillsboro, Oregon to shorten time-to-market of advanced semiconductor technologies essential to AI computing. 
“Applied and Intel share a decades-long history of deep collaboration focused on pushing the boundaries of materials engineering to advance the semiconductor roadmap,” said Gary Dickerson, President and CEO of Applied Materials. “Bringing our teams together at the EPIC Center will deepen that partnership and accelerate the transistor, interconnect and packaging innovations needed to drive the future of AI computing.”
“The demand for AI computing is driving the need for major advances in performance, power efficiency, and packaging. Intel is focused on delivering those innovations and doing it in close collaboration with partners across the ecosystem,” said Lip-Bu Tan, CEO of Intel. “Applied Materials is an important partner, and we look forward to expanding our work together at the EPIC Center to help accelerate the path from the lab to high-volume manufacturing in the United States.”
Teams from Applied Materials and Intel are collaborating on next-generation materials, process technologies and device architectures for advanced logic nodes targeting AI workloads, and will continue this work at the EPIC Center. The collaboration spans both front-end and back-end-of-line advancements, including interconnect scaling. The collaboration also involves development of advanced packaging technologies for Foveros-based 3D stacking, supporting higher interconnect density, improved power delivery, and enhanced thermal performance for high-performance compute platforms designed to accelerate emerging agentic AI workloads.
“With the chipmaking roadmap becoming more complex at each process node, accelerating innovations in semiconductor devices, interconnects and packaging requires deeper collaboration across R&D and manufacturing,” said Dr. Prabu Raja, President of the Semiconductor Products Group at Applied Materials. “We look forward to working closely with Intel as a founding partner of the EPIC Center to shorten development cycles and bring new technologies to market faster.”
“Accelerating our R&D to keep pace with the rapid buildout of AI infrastructure is critical to delivering the technology, manufacturing excellence and foundry services our customers expect from Intel Foundry,” said Naga Chandrasekaran, Executive Vice President, Chief Technology and Operations Officer and General Manager of Intel Foundry. “Applied Materials’ new EPIC Center provides an environment where our teams can collaborate even more closely and at higher velocity to accelerate materials development and process innovations.”
Applied’s new EPIC (Equipment and Process Innovation and Commercialization) Center in Silicon Valley, which is scheduled to be operationally ready this year, is designed from the ground up to dramatically reduce the time it takes to commercialize breakthrough technologies from early-stage research to full-scale manufacturing. For chipmakers, the EPIC Center will provide earlier access to Applied’s R&D portfolio, faster cycles of learning and accelerated transfer of next-generation technologies into high-volume manufacturing, within a secure collaborative environment. In addition, the co-innovation programs at the EPIC Center will provide Applied with greater multi-node visibility to guide R&D investments while increasing R&D productivity and value sharing.

title: TOPPAN to Showcase Color Data Traceability Concept at BioJapan 2026
content_text:
TOPPAN to Showcase Color Data Traceability Concept at BioJapan 2026
Delivering color data reliability and consistency across R&D and manufacturing in the bio and life sciences sectors
Tweet 
Color Data Traceability Concept 
Tokyo – October 6, 2026 – TOPPAN Inc. (TOPPAN), a TOPPAN Group company and wholly owned subsidiary of TOPPAN Holdings Inc. (TYO: 7911), will participate in BioJapan 2026 at Pacifico Yokohama from October 7 to October 9.
First held in 1986, BioJapan is the world's oldest biotechnology exhibition. Held concurrently with Regenerative Medicine JAPAN and healthTECH JAPAN, it serves as one of Asia's largest partnering events, bringing together corporations, startups, academia, and research institutions to drive global open innovation.
At the TOPPAN booth (BioJapan 2026, Booth C-37), TOPPAN will introduce its color data traceability concept based on its proprietary color management technology. 1 In R&D and manufacturing across the bio and life sciences—spanning healthcare, food, and environmental applications—subtle color changes in culture liquids and reagents serve as critical indicators for evaluating quality and status. However, digitally storing and standardizing color information has historically been challenging, leading to subjective visual evaluations, reduced reproducibility, and hindered data utilization. To address these needs for objective color data management, TOPPAN leverages its proprietary Color Management System (CMS) based services to accurately record and analyze rich color information, ensuring data reliability and consistency to drive quality control and digital transformation (DX).
Additionally, at the exhibition TOPPAN will host a luncheon seminar at Annex Hall (F204) on new frontiers in medical applications utilizing extracellular vesicles (Japanese).
Exhibition Highlights
Color Data Traceability Concept 
TOPPAN will share its new platform to ensure the reliability and consistency of color-related data in bio and life science R&D and manufacturing. Subtle color variations in test reagents and samples serve as vital evaluation criteria. TOPPAN's color data traceability concept digitizes color information directly from test samples, mitigating risks such as evaluation discrepancies caused by sample fading or ambient lighting differences, as well as data tampering or manual recording errors. By establishing an environment for reliable color data acquisition and management, TOPPAN aims to provide standardized evidence suitable for academic presentations, research papers, and quality assurance.
CAM-FIT™: Digital Image Color Correction Software Free from Environmental Lighting Effects 
TOPPAN will showcase inspection and manufacturing DX solutions powered by CAM-FIT™, a software program that restores an object's true color regardless of shooting conditions (such as lighting variations, shadows, or contrast differences). By utilizing CAM-FIT™, users can accurately save objective color information from image data that was previously susceptible to environmental inconsistencies. This enables advanced color management and data application via digital imagery, including for use in remote medical assessments, as well as color tracking/information sharing for products and research samples.
Quantification Technology for Lateral Flow Assays via Smartphone App Powered by CAM-FIT™ 
TOPPAN will demonstrate technology and a smartphone application that can be used to quantify detection results by correcting images of paper-based lateral flow assay 2 test strips using CAM-FIT™. As a practical application, TOPPAN will showcase its proprietary technology for detecting extracellular vesicles (exosomes) 3 via immunochromatography, 4 joint research initiatives, and the Exorapid-qIC™ Extracellular Vesicle Immunochromatography Kit—a research reagent kit utilizing this patented technology, commercialized by Dai Nippon Toryo Co., Ltd.

https://solution.toppan.co.jp/creative/service/colormanagementsystem.html

Title
Harnessing Extracellular Vesicles for Medical Applications: Shaping the Future through Cutting-Edge Research and Three-Way Collaboration
Date & Time

Overview
TOPPAN will present potential medical applications and manufacturing quality assurance solutions utilizing its color management and image analysis technologies for lateral flow assay measurement. Lecturer Akira Yokoi (Nagoya University Hospital / Nagoya University Institute for Advanced Research) will present cutting-edge research on extracellular vesicles. Dai Nippon Toryo Co., Ltd. will introduce material development and practical applications related to lateral flow assays (LFA), including the Exorapid-qIC™　detection kit. The session will also highlight new medical possibilities resulting from joint research among the three parties.

2 Lateral Flow Assays (LFA): A rapid, simple testing method that uses paper-based materials to detect the presence or absence of target substances simply by applying a liquid sample.
3 Extracellular Vesicles (Exosomes): Microscopic vesicles secreted by various cell types containing proteins, nucleic acids, and other molecules that play key roles in cell-to-cell communication.
4 Immunochromatography: A simple assay method that detects specific substances using antigen-antibody reactions. A type of lateral flow assay, it is widely used in pregnancy test kits and infectious disease diagnostics.

title: GE HealthCare to Acquire SOFIE Biosciences, Establishing a 'Final Mile' Footprint for PET Radiopharmaceutical Supply in the U.S.
source: GE Healthcare - Investor News Releases / Investor News / Press Releases
content_text:
GE HealthCare to Acquire SOFIE Biosciences, Establishing a 'Final Mile' Footprint for PET Radiopharmaceutical Supply in the U.S.
October 5, 2026
PDF Version 
Broadens GE HealthCare's footprint in the U.S . radiopharmaceutical industry, drives patient access to F18 labeled Positron Emission Tomography (PET) radiopharmaceuticals and enhances exposure to new high-growth areas
Pharmaceutical Diagnostics (PDx) continues to partner with other established Contract Manufacturing Organizations (CMOs) to drive and expand patient access to its radiopharmaceutical portfolio, while SOFIE Biosciences continues to supply PET products from other leading radiopharmaceutical providers
Provides U.S . rights to FAPI-74, a Phase III pipeline PET radiotracer with pan-cancer imaging potential, aiming to be among the first-to-launch in a large and fast-growing market 1 
CHICAGO --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 5, 2026--
GE HealthCare (Nasdaq: GEHC) today announced a definitive agreement to acquire SOFIE Biosciences , a leading U.S .-based CMO for PET radiopharmaceuticals, from Trilantic North America , for a purchase price of $945 million paid in cash. The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to closing conditions, including regulatory approvals, at which time SOFIE Biosciences will become part of GE HealthCare’s PDx segment.
This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261005273717/en/ 
SOFIE Biosciences has 15 CMO sites across the U.S ., manufacturing PET radiopharmaceutical products
The acquisition of SOFIE Biosciences establishes a footprint for GE HealthCare in the time-critical ‘final mile’ of U.S . PET radiopharmaceutical supply, while also enabling PDx to participate in other high growth areas outside its own product portfolio. With a U.S . network of 15 CMO sites operating 21 cyclotrons, and a theranostics-focused Contract Development and Manufacturing Organization (CDMO) site, this acquisition broadens GE HealthCare's footprint in the U.S . radiopharmaceutical industry, while driving reliable patient access to novel radiopharmaceuticals. It also further enables GE HealthCare’s ability to provide solutions along every step of the theranostics pathway, from cyclotrons to imaging technology, digital workflow tools and radiotherapeutics infrastructure.
“The PET radiopharmaceutical market is expanding rapidly with the introduction of innovative radiotracers and advances in precision care, including the growing adoption of targeted therapies. As part of GE HealthCare , SOFIE Biosciences is expected to grow in the low double digits, and enables us to participate across the radiopharmaceutical value stream, meeting customer demand through a mix of GE HealthCare owned and partner facilities. SOFIE Biosciences has a highly skilled team with deep expertise serving U.S . customers, including manufacturing our Flyrcado™ (flurpiridaz F18 injection) product,” said Kevin O'Neill , President & CEO of the PDx segment at GE HealthCare. “We will leverage our scale and expertise in radiopharmaceutical manufacturing across the U.S ., Europe and Japan to further invest in and grow SOFIE Biosciences , helping improve patient access, strengthen reliability of supply, and support the next generation of precision care products."
PET radiopharmaceuticals are used in precision medicine to visualize metabolic and molecular activity and, increasingly, to deliver targeted therapies across a range of disease areas. F18 labeled PET radiopharmaceuticals have a 110-minute half-life, with PET CMOs playing a crucial role in enabling timely and reliable patient access, both to existing and pipeline products. Industry-wide, the radiopharmaceutical pipeline is growing rapidly, with approximately 20 PET radiotracers and over 30 radiotherapeutics currently under development. 2 These include SOFIE Biosciences’ Phase III F18 Fibroblast Activation Protein Inhibitor (FAPI) asset, FAPI-74, for which GE HealthCare already holds outside-of- U.S . rights. FAPI has the potential to further expand an already fast-growing global PET imaging market, and is showing strong potential for diagnostic and theranostic use across a range of oncologic and non-oncologic indications.
GE HealthCare will continue to drive and expand access to its existing proprietary F18 radiopharmaceutical products, while advancing its pipeline of new products, both through SOFIE Biosciences , and PDx’s other established CMO partners across the U.S .
Serving SOFIE Biosciences’ Customers 
Following the transaction close, SOFIE Biosciences will continue to operate as an independent manufacturing partner to its customers, supplying its existing product portfolio, including products from other leading radiopharmaceutical providers.
Patrick Phelps , SOFIE Biosciences co-founder, President & CEO, said, “As demand continues to increase for F18 products, and pipelines for new diagnostics and therapeutics continue to expand, joining GE HealthCare marks an exciting step in our journey as a leading U.S . CMO. With Trilantic North America’s support, we have significantly expanded our capabilities and scale, and we share GE HealthCare’s ambition to improve patient outcomes by delivering on the promise of radiopharmaceuticals as we look ahead to our next phase of growth.”
Ted Rosenwasser , Partner, Trilantic North America , said, "We are incredibly proud of what Patrick and the SOFIE Biosciences team have accomplished during our partnership. SOFIE Biosciences has grown significantly, investing in its network and manufacturing capabilities to help meet growing demand and enable increased and reliable patient access to critical products. GE HealthCare's legacy and global expertise make it a natural partner to support SOFIE Biosciences’ continued growth and help expand access for U.S . patients to novel diagnostic and therapeutic radiopharmaceuticals.”
GE HealthCare’s Pharmaceutical Diagnostics segment is a global leader in imaging agents used to support 140 million procedures in 2025, equivalent to four patient procedures every second. For more than 40 years, GE HealthCare's imaging agents have been routinely used across care pathways to support diagnosis.
Financial Benefits 
GE HealthCare estimates that the transaction will be accretive to revenue growth, Adjusted earnings before interest and taxes margin* and Adjusted earnings per share* in the first full year of ownership.

title: Press Releases Group "BEYOND": Air Liquide accelerates lasting value creation with new strategic plan for 2030 October 05, 2026

content_text:
"BEYOND": Air Liquide accelerates lasting value creation with new strategic plan for 2030
Paris, France, 
October 05, 2026 
Press Releases
Group
Air Liquide today unveils "BEYOND", its strategic plan through 2030, which embodies the Group's ambition to expand in the highest-potential markets and turn major global structural shifts into opportunities. Through BEYOND, the Group sets a new frontier for lasting value creation, in line with its commitments as a high-performing, long-term responsible company. 
As an essential cornerstone of industry and healthcare, Air Liquide's molecules and solutions sit at the heart of major global trends , including the energy transition, digital and artificial intelligence acceleration, technological and industrial sovereignty, and evolving healthcare needs.   BEYOND, the Group's new strategic plan for 2030, aims to turn these transformations into sustainable growth drivers for its customers and patients . 
This ambition targets three key objectives: 
A compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of +10% (+/-2%) over the period in recurring net Earnings per Share [1] , ensuring ambitious and profitable growth; 
A recurring ROCE [2] above 11% in 2030, while maintaining a significant increase in industrial investments over the period, ensuring lasting value creation; 
And a confirmed environmental commitment , pursuing a 33% reduction in CO 2 emissions [3] by 2035 compared to 2020, ensuring a sustained societal commitment. 
In order to achieve the recurring EPS objective, three complementary levers will be flexibly deployed : 
A compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of +5% (+/-1%) [4] over the period in sales , outpacing industrial production by a factor of 2 to 3, 
A margin improvement of +400 to +600 basis points over the period [5] , 
A capital allocation of over €40 billion over the period [6] , made possible by the increased profitability initiated during the ADVANCE plan. More than half of this will be dedicated to higher industrial investments, bolt on and strategic acquisitions. In addition, a significantly higher return for both institutional and individual shareholders will be ensured by combining a sustained, regular dividend growth policy with the launch for the first time of a 4 billion euros share buyback program over the 2027-2028 period [7] . 
Attention to all stakeholders - from customers to employees, shareholders to local communities - is reinforced with specific measures for each in the BEYOND plan, built on three pillars: Listen & Care, Growth, Performance . 
François Jackow , Chief Executive Officer of Air Liquide, stated:  
"With BEYOND, Air Liquide opens an ambitious new strategic chapter in its profitable growth trajectory. The Group enters this cycle on solid foundations and with committed teams serving our customers and patients. In a constantly evolving environment, powered by the success of our ADVANCE plan, the resilience of our business model, our innovation capabilities, and our leading market positions, our roadmap is clear: reach a new frontier in lasting value creation. 
To step up our momentum, we will capture profitable growth by leveraging our global reach and our multi-local footprint, close to our customers. We will also leverage our scale, as well as the increased digitalization of our processes, to achieve an unprecedented level of operational performance. Finally, our profitability allows us to evolve our capital allocation beyond investments and acquisitions in our core businesses, notably through two new measures: rolling out a share buyback program for our shareholders and annual employee share purchase plans. 
With BEYOND, more than ever, we intend to anticipate, innovate and meet the evolving needs of our stakeholders - employees, industrial customers, healthcare providers, society and shareholders. By delivering useful and innovative solutions, creating lasting value and sharing it with all, we continue to build on the trust earned over time, and to keep inventing the future together." 
Building on the success of the ADVANCE plan (2022-2025), which demonstrated the Group's ability to combine financial and non-financial performance, Air Liquide approaches the BEYOND plan from a position of strength. It capitalizes on long-term relationships with customers and patients, leading positions in its core businesses, recognized innovation capabilities, as well as a resilient model and solid financial foundations. 
BEYOND is based on   three complementary and interdependent pillars : 
1. Listen & Care: Putting stakeholders at the center 
Operating close to its markets through a dual global and local footprint, Air Liquide makes active listening a key competitive advantage . In an accelerating, fast-changing environment, the Group’s ability to capture market signals and interact in close proximity with customers and partners to design adapted solutions serves as a major differentiator. 
This ambition translates into concrete actions for each stakeholder: 
Customers and patients : delivering safe, reliable, and innovative solutions to address their challenges; 
Employees : enhancing career development, engagement, and safety to drive collective success; and giving them a greater stake in this achievement through annual employee share purchase plans; 
Shareholders : maintaining an active, transparent, and constructive dialogue focused on consistent value creation; 
Local communities : supporting sustainable development where the Group operates. 
 
2. Growth: Unlocking diversified and high-value growth engines 
Supported by its increased financial resources and innovation capabilities, the Group has identified four strategic markets where it aims to accelerate its development: 
Electronics and AI : as the leading supplier of industrial gases and advanced materials to the semiconductors industry, Air Liquide is uniquely positioned to capture fast-growing demand driven by ever-larger fab projects, the need for more advanced materials required by evolving chip performance, and sovereignty policies encouraging fab development across regions. 
Energy Transition : capitalising on long-term structural demand where the Group is the leading player in its industry. 
Healthcare : consolidating its global leadership in home healthcare, leveraging AI as a key driver to enhance patient care and the development of new services. 
Space : leveraging its recognized expertise with a targeted positioning on the fast-accelerating private market. 
 
Air Liquide anticipates a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of sales of +5% (+/-1%) [8] over the period, outpacing industrial production by 2 to 3 times. 
To achieve these ambitions, Air Liquide plans industrial investment decisions for approximately €24 billion over the BEYOND period . This will be dedicated to targeted investments - particularly in industrial projects backed by long-term contracts - to strengthen its activities and expand its presence in major basins. This will be complemented by a reinforced acquisition strategy. Growth strategies will be specifically tailored to the challenges of each geography and market, underpinned by a disciplined capital allocation framework designed to preserve the Group's strategic flexibility while boosting shareholder returns over the plan. 
Innovation remains a core growth driver for Air Liquide. It paves the way for new applications and services across both industry and healthcare, enabling unique offerings, helping our customers enhance their competitiveness , and reducing their environmental impact. As part of its innovation strategy, the Group will rely on frontier technologies (advanced materials for semiconductors, extreme cryogenics for electricity transmission, nuclear fusion and quantum, massive oxygen production for space, etc.) and the accelerated industrialization of proprietary, patented technologies (Cryocap™, PEM electrolyzers [9] , ammonia cracking, hydrogen liquefaction). It will also continue exploring new applications and extend its leadership in electronic precursors - those proprietary materials and molecules essential for manufacturing the most advanced and high-performing semiconductors and chips. 
3. Performance: Driving competitiveness and agility 
To secure its long-term performance , Air Liquide will step up several key levers initiated under the ADVANCE plan, including: 
Continuous organizational streamlining to enhance agility for customers and unlock synergies across the Group. 
Global efficiencies , standardizing processes, expanding Global Business Services (GBS) and centralizing procurement. 
Local efficiencies through the deployment of global programs, allowing operations to fully focus on safety, customer service and deliver local operational excellence. 
AI integration : now deployed across all our operations, its rollout will be further accelerated through five dedicated roadmaps focused on high-value-creation domains. 
These priorities aim to deliver an operating margin improvement of +400 to +600 basis points over the period [10] and maintain a recurring ROCE [11] above 11% in 2030, alongside a significant increase in investments ensuring sustainable growth. 
Finally, Air Liquide reaffirms its environmental commitment , targeting a 33% reduction in Scope 1 & 2 CO 2 emissions by 2035 and carbon neutrality by 2050. Facing climate change, the Group is also anticipating and adapting its water management, introducing a -10% reduction target in water withdrawal by 2030 compared to 2025.

title: Proterial and FEV Jointly Validate xEV Traction Motor Concept Using Amorphous Alloy and High-Performance Heavy-Rare-Earth-Free Magnet Technology Simulation Study Indicates Potential for Higher Efficiency, Increased Output, and Reduced Weight
source: Hitachi Metals - Proterial 2026 Press Releases / Press Releases
content_text:
TOP 
News Release 
2026 
Proterial and FEV Jointly Validate xEV Traction Motor Concept Using Amorphous Alloy and High-Performance Heavy-Rare-Earth-Free Magnet Technology Simulation Study Indicates Potential for Higher Efficiency, Increased Output, and Reduced Weight 
R&D 
Proterial and FEV Jointly Validate xEV Traction Motor Concept Using Amorphous Alloy and High-Performance Heavy-Rare-Earth-Free Magnet Technology
Simulation Study Indicates Potential for Higher Efficiency, Increased Output, and Reduced Weight
October 5, 2026 
Proterial, Ltd.
FEV
Proterial, Ltd. (“Proterial”), a leading manufacturer of advanced materials and components, and FEV, a global engineering and consulting partner for mobility, energy, and software, have jointly investigated and validated an electrified-vehicle (xEV) traction motor concept that combines Proterial’s amorphous alloy technology with its high-performance heavy-rare-earth (HRE) -free neodymium sintered magnet technology. Bringing together Proterial’s advanced materials expertise and FEV’s capabilities in electric drive design, simulation, benchmarking, and system-level evaluation, the partners developed and assessed a traction motor concept designed to make full use of the characteristics of these materials. Simulation results indicate the potential to improve motor efficiency while simultaneously increasing output and reducing weight compared with a defined 230-kW-class reference motor. The study also highlights the potential to reduce resource and procurement risks associated with HREs. Proterial and FEV will continue exploring how advanced material technologies can be translated into tangible benefits at the traction motor and complete drive-system level. 
The results of this study will be jointly presented by FEV and Proterial at the Aachen Automotive Colloquium, to be held in Aachen, Germany, from October 5 to 7, 2026. 
1. Background
As the mobility industry continues to pursue decarbonization and improved energy efficiency, demand is increasing for traction motors and drive systems with lower power consumption, higher performance, and reduced reliance on critical raw materials. In electrified vehicles (xEVs), improving efficiency supports lower electricity consumption and longer driving range; in other applications, such as heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) equipment, data centers, electric vertical takeoff and advanced air mobility, exemplified by eVTOL aircraft, and robotics, higher-efficiency electric motors can help reduce overall energy demand. Amorphous alloy is attracting attention because it can reduce motor losses. Compared with conventional electrical steel sheets commonly used in electric motor cores, amorphous alloy offers lower iron loss. For neodymium magnets used in xEV traction motors, there is also strong demand to reduce dependence on HREs, which face resource constraints, and to mitigate procurement risk. To address these market needs, Proterial has developed continuous lamination and bonding technology for amorphous alloy ribbon suitable for punching into motor cores, as well as high-performance HRE-free neodymium sintered magnets that can be applied to xEV traction motors. Proterial established the Motor Solutions Department within its Marketing & Sales Division in November 2025 and is promoting initiatives to verify the value of its products from the perspective of traction motors and complete drive systems, and to develop optimized solutions for customer applications rather than individual products alone.
2. Overview and Results of the Study
As part of these initiatives undertaken by its Motor Solutions Department, Proterial is working with FEV, with project promotion support from Beyond Materials Corporation, to evaluate the application of amorphous alloy and HRE-free magnet technology to xEV traction motors.
In this study, FEV established a reference motor model for a 230 kW drive unit, representative of modern passenger-car battery electric vehicle (BEV) applications, using silicon steel sheets for the motor core. The effect of applying amorphous alloy was then evaluated through electromagnetic simulation. Rather than simply replacing the motor core material, the partners examined a traction motor concept that reflects current trends in electric drive systems, including inverter and reduction gears, while making best use of the low-iron-loss characteristics of amorphous alloy, due to an increased maximum motor speed. The reduction ratio of the transmission was adjusted so that the maximum torque and speed during vehicle operation would be equivalent to that of the reference drive unit (Table 1). The study also applied Proterial’s high-performance HRE-free neodymium sintered magnet, which combines high magnetic performance, due to a high remanence flux density, and strong resistance to demagnetization, due to a high coercivity, without relying on HREs. Compared with the reference, the simulation results indicate the potential to improve motor efficiency while simultaneously increasing output to 300 kW and reducing weight by 27 % (Table 1).

3. Future Outlook
Proterial and FEV intend to continue exploring how advanced material technologies can be translated into measurable benefits in electric motors and complete drive systems. Through its Motor Solutions Department and in collaboration with its business divisions, Proterial will continue to verify material value from the perspective of customer applications and propose optimized solutions. FEV will contribute its engineering, simulation, benchmarking, and system-integration expertise to assess how new materials can support next-generation electric drive concepts. Together, the partners aim to support higher-efficiency electric mobility and other emerging applications, including eVTOLs and humanoid robots, while contributing to a more sustainable society.
4. Presentation at the Aachen Automotive Colloquium
The results of this joint study will be presented by FEV and Proterial at the Aachen Automotive Colloquium, to be held in Aachen, Germany, from October 5 to 7, 2026. A mock-up of the traction motor structure examined in this study will also be on display at FEV's Booth No. 9.

About Proterial
Headquartered in Tokyo, Japan, Proterial is a leading manufacturer of advanced materials, primarily metal-based materials.
In the motor field, the company’s business divisions collaborate under the leadership of the Motor Solutions Department to serve as development partners for customers. Proterial verifies the value of materials from the perspective of motors and complete drive systems and proposes optimal solutions.
As a manufacturer capable of providing a comprehensive range of motor materials, Proterial will continue to contribute to lower electricity consumption in xEVs and reduced power consumption in air-conditioning and data-center equipment through the application of its products to high-efficiency motors. The company will also contribute to a sustainable society by providing solutions for emerging applications, including eVTOLs and humanoid robots.
About FEV
FEV is a global engineering and consulting partner for mobility, energy and software. Since 1978, FEV has been developing innovative technologies and solutions across the entire product lifecycle – from strategy and concept development through engineering and validation to implementation, optimization and support. Combining engineering expertise with software, digital technologies and AI, FEV helps its customers develop sustainable technologies, intelligent systems and future-oriented solutions. With around 5,600 employees at more than 45 locations worldwide, FEV serves customers across a wide range of industries.
About Beyond Materials
Beyond Materials is a joint venture established by Mitsubishi Corporation and FEV Consulting GmbH. By combining the two companies’ expertise in the materials industry, global networks, insights into customer needs across industries such as automotive, energy, and robotics, and capabilities in end-product design and development, Beyond Materials provides consulting and engineering-related solutions to companies throughout the materials industry and its value chain. Its services include market and technology research, strategy development, product development, and proof-of-concept testing.

xEV: A general term for electrified vehicles, including battery electric vehicles (BEVs), hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs), plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEVs), and related vehicles.

Amorphous alloy: A metallic material with no crystalline structure, obtained by rapidly cooling a molten alloy.
