title: 27 milliards de dollars en jeu : pourquoi la capacité de traitement des déchets dangereux est stratégique
source: Veolia - Financial Press Releases / Financial Press Releases RSS
content_text:
$27 Billion at Stake: Why Hazardous Waste Treatment Capacity Is Strategic
News listing 
24 Sep. 2026 
A new independent study by Charles River Associates (CRA), commissioned by Veolia, highlights the critical role of hazardous waste management in the U.S. economy. As the United States accelerates industrial development, the study finds that a treatment capacity shortfall of just 1% could reduce projected economic output by $27 billion by 2033. 
KEY FIGURES
30 million tons of hazardous waste are generated each year in the United States.
+5 million tons per year of additional hazardous waste could be generated by 2033.
$27 billion in economic output potentially at risk in the event of a 1% capacity shortfall.
$82 billion in economic output potentially at risk in the event of a 3% capacity shortfall.
A Critical Link in the U.S. Economy
Hazardous waste management is often viewed as an end-of-pipe activity. Yet it is an essential link in many economic activities.  Agriculture, food production, chemicals, pharmaceuticals and emerging technologies: numerous industries generate hazardous waste or rely on value chains that do.
According to the Charles River Associates study, a treatment capacity shortfall of just 1% could reduce projected economic output in the United States by $27 billion by 2033. With a 3% shortfall, the impact could reach $82 billion.
 
“Hazardous waste management plays a far greater role in our economies than many people realize. This analysis helps shed light on the importance of that role and underscores why access to expert, state-of-the-art and reliable waste management capacity is essential to strengthening economic stability and resilience.” 
Estelle Brachlianoff , Chief Executive Officer of Veolia. 
Supporting the Next Wave of Industrial Growth
Demand is expected to increase further in the coming years: according to CRA, the United States could generate  an additional 5 million tons of hazardous waste per year by 2033 , driven in part by the reshoring and expansion of manufacturing and the growth of strategic industries such as semiconductors and batteries.
This growth raises a major challenge: waste management capacity must be able to expand at the same pace as production capacity.
Anticipating these needs helps secure industrial supply chains while managing risks to human health and the environment. 
Protecting Communities and Preserving Resources
Beyond their economic importance, hazardous waste treatment and management serve a critical environmental and public health purpose:  preventing pollution, protecting communities and, where possible, recovering valuable resources. 
“Proper treatment and disposal of hazardous waste help protect public health while supporting economic development. During National Pollution Prevention Week, we are especially proud to highlight the role we play in protecting people and the planet through treatment processes that recover valuable resources while preventing pollution from entering the environment.” 
Bob Cappadona , Chief Executive Officer, Hazardous Waste in the United-States, Veolia.
As industrial waste streams become increasingly complex, Veolia is developing specialized solutions such as  BeyondPFAS to help customers manage waste containing persistent substances.
Veolia Expands Its U.S. Capabilities
With the acquisition of  Clean Earth , completed in June 2026, Veolia has become  the second-largest player in the U.S. hazardous waste management market. 
Its U.S. operations now include: 
100+ service centers  
33 treatment, storage and disposal facilities  
6 high-temperature incineration units  
700+ operating permits 
5,500 employees 
This footprint enables the Group to support industrial customers in regions where demand is expected to grow, particularly in  Arkansas, Texas, Arizona, New Jersey and California. 
Anticipating Tomorrow’s Needs to Support Growth
L’étude de CRA met en évidence une réalité essentielle : la gestion des déchets dangereux est une composante de The CRA study highlights a fundamental reality: hazardous waste management is a component of U.S. industrial infrastructure.
As the United States invests in expanding its production capacity,  having the infrastructure and technologies needed to manage the resulting waste will be critical to supporting sustainable growth. 
For Veolia, the priority is clear:  anticipate future needs, expand capacity and develop solutions that protect the environment while contributing to the resilience of U.S. industry. 
About the Study
Read the full Hazardous Waste Management: A Hidden Input to US Economic Growth (2026, author Alan Jaske), conducted by Charles River Associates (CRA) on behalf of Veolia.

Jenoptik secures major contract to deploy intersection safety camera systems across British Columbia
Jenoptik will deliver, implement and install more than 140 of the latest systems that combine red light violation and speed on green detection. 
24 September 2026 
JENOPTIK Canada Ltd., a leading provider of road safety and security solutions, has been awarded a contract by the Insurance Corporation of British Columbia (ICBC) to supply more than 140 intersection safety camera systems as part of ICBC’s Intersection Safety Camera Program. The project represents a significant investment in road safety infrastructure and supports ICBC’s ongoing efforts to improve safety at signalized intersections throughout British Columbia.
Under the terms of the agreement, Jenoptik will deliver, implement and install more than 140 of the latest systems that combine red light violation and speed on green detection, together with its FlowTris back-office platform. The integrated solution will support the capture, processing, and management of enforcement data, providing a secure and efficient workflow for administering the Intersection Safety Camera Program.
Intersection safety camera programs are designed to encourage safer driving behaviour by promoting compliance with traffic laws at signalized intersections. By helping to reduce high-risk driving behaviours, these systems contribute to safer roads for motorists, pedestrians, and cyclists. “We are proud to partner with ICBC in supporting its Intersection Safety Camera Program and its commitment to improving road safety across British Columbia,” said Candice Holder-Mattadeen, Head of Sales, JENOPTIK Canada Ltd. “With more than 20 years of experience delivering road safety solutions in Canada, we look forward to working with ICBC to implement a modern, reliable intersection safety camera program that helps improve safety for all road users.”
With this new partnership Jenoptik now has installations from coast-to-coast and their new office in Vancouver will bring more jobs to the community.
Jenoptik looks forward to supporting the successful deployment of the new intersection safety camera systems and contributing to safer communities across British Columbia.
An image is available for download in the Jenoptik image database. 
About Jenoptik and its SBU Smart Mobility Solutions
Jenoptik is a global technology group operating in the photonics market. Our core markets primarily include semiconductor technology, medical technology, metrology as well as smart mobility. Approximately 4,300 people worldwide work for the Jenoptik Group, which is headquartered in Jena (Germany). JENOPTIK AG is listed on the German Stock Exchange in Frankfurt and traded on the MDax and TecDax. In fiscal year 2025, Jenoptik generated revenue of 1,046 million euros.
Jenoptik Smart Mobility Solutions provides photonics-based, innovative and sustainable solutions, including technology and services for road safety and security. As an end-to-end solution provider, we support our customers with the provision of roadside equipment and software, including integration, installation, maintenance and financing models through to full-service operation of our solutions. Our strong global presence and installation base is supported by a longstanding partner network with tens of thousands of systems deployed worldwide. Leveraging 90 years of experience and 40 years in ANPR (ALPR), we have expert knowledge of local regulations and requirements in our markets, where technology performance is critical to the outcome. With innovation as our driving force, Jenoptik is a world-leading enabler for traffic law enforcement and public safety, with intelligent solutions and services constantly evolving to help make roads, journeys, communities and our environment safer around the globe.

title: Sponsorship of the 19th Amulet Sword (Omamori Katana) Exhibition
source: Hitachi Metals - Proterial 2026 Press Releases / Press Releases
content_text:
Sponsorship of the 19th Amulet Sword (Omamori Katana) Exhibition
September 24, 2026 
Proterial, Ltd.
Proterial, Ltd. (hereafter referred to as “Proterial”) is pleased to announce its sponsorship of the 19th Amulet Sword Exhibition. 
1. About the Amulet Sword Exhibition
Amulet Sword has been carried since ancient times to protect oneself from evil spirits. Even today, Amulet Sword is widely used as a gift for childbirth celebrations, weddings, funerals, and other ceremonies, with hopes for a child’s healthy growth or the protection of their owner.
The Amulet Sword Exhibition showcases selected outstanding works collected from swordsmiths and sword artisans nationwide. Since its inception in 2005, the exhibition aims to preserve and enhance traditional sword-related craftsmanship while contributing to the sound development of traditional Japanese arts.
Name: 
The 19th Amulet Sword (Omamori Katana) Exhibition 
Sponsored by: 
All Japan Swordsmith Association, Amulet, Sword Exhibition Executive Committee, Setouchi City 
Venue: 
Bizen Osafune Sword Museum (Setouchi City, Okayama) 
Date: 
Saturday, October 3, 2026, to Monday, November 23, 2026 
2. Background Behind the Co-Sponsorship of the Event
Proterial’s main factory, the Yasugi Works (Yasugi City, Shimane Prefecture), is the former site of the Unpaku-Steel Limited partnership, established in 1899 by financiers who practiced the ancient method of tatara ironmaking. Initially, they shipped kera (steel bloom), tamahagane (steel made from iron sand), and refined iron (typically used for knives) made by the tatara method nationwide. Over time, by applying the tatara method and enhancing production efficiency with corner furnaces, Proterial, while developing technology to the current day, produces world-class specialty steel by continuing the spirit of ironmaking fostered by tatara ironmaking.
Moreover, since 1977 (when Hitachi Metals, Ltd. was in charge), Proterial has been contributing to the production of tamahagane, the sole material for Japanese swords, by supporting the tatara operations organized by the Nihon Bijutsu Token Hozon Kyokai. The aim of which is to preserve the technique and culture of tatara, one of the starting points of Proterial.
Against this context, we sponsor the Amulet Sword as Proterial to support the continuation and improvement of the traditional techniques of tamahagane Amulet Sword, which embodies the essence of traditional Japanese craftsmanship.
3. Details of the 19th Amulet Sword Exhibition Sponsorship
Awarding the Proterial Prize * to the most outstanding sword
Financial support for operational expenses
Proterial will also be placing advertisements at stations, including Okayama and Kurashiki, in conjunction with the hosting of the fair.
* Note: Proterial Prize: Award to one particularly outstanding sword, including swords from jury members and invited exhibits and excluding swords from holders of Important Intangible Cultural Property.
Voting is conducted by all jurors, excluding those from the exhibition jury.

title: 23-09-2026 | Case study Accelerating commercial vehicle electrification with reliable DC-DC converters​
content_text:
Accelerating commercial vehicle electrification with reliable DC-DC converters​
Electrification is transforming the commercial vehicle industry, but the path forward is not always straightforward. Manufacturers must balance regulatory requirements, technical feasibility, and cost considerations while continuing to deliver reliable vehicles to the market. In this article, we explore how Avia Ingeniería y Diseño developed a practical micro-hybrid platform and the role that robust DC-DC conversion played in enabling its electrification journey. 
Electrification without complexity
Across Europe, commercial vehicle manufacturers are seeking ways to reduce emissions without the cost and complexity of full vehicle electrification. Hybrid architectures have emerged as a practical pathway, helping manufacturers improve sustainability while leveraging existing vehicle platforms. Supporting this transition requires more than electrified components alone. Reliable power conversion technologies play a critical role in enabling efficient vehicle architectures, reducing integration complexity, and accelerating development. The collaboration between Avia Ingeniería y Diseño and Prodrive Technologies demonstrates how proven power electronics can support practical electrification strategies while creating a foundation for future innovation
Prodrive's DC-DC converters
"One of the key advantages of working with Prodrive Technologies was the combination of a mature product and responsive engineering support. This allowed us to focus on system validation rather than solving component- level integration issues.​"  
David Sánchez​, CEO, Avia Ingeniería y Diseño​

content_text:

Recommend Facebook LinkedIn 
Jenoptik CEO Dominic Dorfner highlights strong position as an enabler of megatrends
At Thuringia’s largest technology trade show, W3+ Fair in Jena, Dr. Dominic Dorfner introduced himself to the photonics industry. In a keynote speech, he shared insights into his first weeks in office. Together with Thuringia’s Minister of Economic Affairs and the Lord Mayor of Jena, he explored the trends at the trade show. 
23 September 2026 
The W3+ Fair, taking place on September 23 and 24, 2026, brings together business and science from the fields of photonics, optics, electronics, and mechanics. On the first day of the fair, Jenoptik CEO Dr. Dominic Dorfner, who has been in office since August 2026 , spoke for the first time in front a large number of representatives from the photonics industry. At the start of the “en-tech.talks” conference, which accompanies the trade show, he delivered a keynote address about his experiences during his first weeks as CEO of the Jena-based photonics group Jenoptik.
“It’s not just our technology, but also the passion of the employees behind it that has particularly impressed me,” said Dr. Dominic Dorfner in his speech. “Every assembly, every chip, every surgical image, every critical mission begins with individuals who are passionate about their work.” This is what enables concrete applications for artificial intelligence and data communication, in semiconductor manufacturing and medical technology, as well as for security and defense. Photonics is the key enabling technology here. “The combination of passion and technology creates added value for our customers and makes us successful in our demanding markets,” said Dorfner.
Dr. Dominic Dorfner also took part in a tour of the trade show with Colette Boos-John, Minister of Economic Affairs for Thuringia, and Dr. Thomas Nitzsche, Lord Mayor of Jena.
Jenoptik has been represented as an exhibitor and sponsor since the first W3+ Fair in Jena in 2023. With its focus on photonics, optics, and sensor technology, the fair reflects Jenoptik’s core competencies and also offers many opportunities at the Group’s main location for networking with research institutions, startups, and associations, as well as for recruiting.
This year, at booth B9 under the motto “Enabling innovation with smart photonic solutions,” Jenoptik is presenting a portfolio of components, solutions, and products that demonstrates how photonics, as a key technology, is driving advancements in fields such as semiconductor manufacturing, optical communications, medical diagnostics, security technology, and automated quality inspection.
Among other things, the following are presented at the Jenoptik booth B9:
High-precision micro-optical components for semiconductor manufacturing  and optical communications  to enable efficient and reliable data transmission. Among other items, high-precision lightweight optical mirrors manufactured for communication between satellites or to ground stations will be on display.
For ophthalmology, dermatology, and endoscopy, high-precision, miniaturized OEM solutions will be presented that improve diagnostics and therapy,  including laser components and subsystems as well as solutions for illumination, imaging, and image processing.
In the field of security,  information will be provided on infrared cameras and laser rangefinders that can be integrated as compact, precise modules into mobile and autonomous applications.
A live demonstration will be given of the “SurfInspect” testing and measuring device from TRIOPTICS, a subsidiary of Jenoptik. This automated testing system is used for the objective quality assessment of the surfaces of flat optics and lenses.
Images are available in the Jenoptik image database under “Press Release.” 
About Jenoptik
Jenoptik is a global technology group operating in the photonics market. Our core markets primarily include semiconductor technology, medical technology, metrology as well as smart mobility. Approximately 4,300 people worldwide work for the Jenoptik Group, which is headquartered in Jena (Germany). JENOPTIK AG is listed on the German Stock Exchange in Frankfurt and traded on the MDax and TecDax. In fiscal year 2025, Jenoptik generated revenue of 1,046 million euros.

GE HealthCare appoints veteran finance executive Pascal Desroches to Board of Directors

CHICAGO --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Sep. 22, 2026-- GE HealthCare (Nasdaq: GEHC) today announced the appointment of Pascal Desroches , Senior Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer (CFO) of AT&T (NYSE: T), a Fortune 50 company, to its Board of Directors, effective January 4, 2027 . Mr. Desroches brings more than 30 years of leadership experience across finance, governance, and large-scale technology and digital transformation.
“Pascal is a highly respected executive and accomplished financial leader whose experience spans corporate strategy, capital deployment, and investor engagement,” said H. Lawrence Culp , Jr., Chairman of the Board of Directors, GE HealthCare . “His perspective will further strengthen our Board as we execute on our strategy to advance precision care, accelerate our next wave of innovation, and create long-term value for patients, customers, and shareholders.”
Mr. Desroches has served as CFO of AT&T since 2021 and plans to retire from the company on December 31, 2026 . Previously, he served as CFO of WarnerMedia following AT&T’s acquisition of Time Warner in 2018, overseeing financial operations, global real estate, and technology across HBO , Turner Broadcasting , and Warner Bros. As CFO of Turner Broadcasting , he played a pivotal role in the spin-off of three multi-billion-dollar subsidiaries: Time Warner Cable , AOL, and Time.
Earlier in his career, Mr. Desroches worked at KPMG and the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission , gaining broad industry and regulatory experience. He serves on the boards of Honeywell Aerospace , where he chairs the audit committee, and the Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas . He also brings healthcare governance experience through nearly four years of service on the board of DaVita.
“As a global leader in precision care, GE HealthCare plays a critical role in shaping the future of healthcare and improving outcomes for patients worldwide,” said Pascal Desroches . “I look forward to serving on the Board and working with the management team to advance the company’s strategy, make care more personal and precise, drive growth, and create long-term value.”

GE HealthCare is a leading global healthcare solutions provider of advanced medical technology, pharmaceutical diagnostics, and AI, cloud and software solutions that help clinicians tackle the world’s most complex diseases. Serving patients and providers for 130 years, GE HealthCare is delivering bold innovations designed for the next era of medicine across its Advanced Imaging Solutions, Pharmaceutical Diagnostics and Patient Care Solutions segments to help clinicians deliver more personalized, precise patient care. We are a $20.6 billion business with approximately 54,000 colleagues working to create a world where healthcare has no limits.

title: 09/22/2026 Company Evonik sharpens growth strategy Essen, Germany. With a clear focus on all its activities, Evonik will strengthen growth over the next three years. The business portfolio will be set up according to roles, and specific tasks will be assigned to the major sites in Germany.
content_text:
Evonik sharpens growth strategy
• Businesses and German sites with clear roles
• Investments to strengthen global geostrategic balance
• Efficiency program Evonik Tailor Made creates financial leeway
Essen, Germany . With a clear focus on all its activities, Evonik will strengthen growth over the next three years. The business portfolio will be set up according to roles, and specific tasks will be assigned to the major sites in Germany. At the same time, targeted growth projects will improve the geostrategic balance.
Evonik is securing financial leeway for these investments through the Evonik Tailor Made restructuring program, which aims to further lower the Group's cost base. As part of this program, 3,200 jobs will be cut worldwide, around 2,150 of them in Germany. 
As part of the annual strategy meeting, the Executive Board and Supervisory Board discussed plans up to 2030 in detail. "The Executive Board, Supervisory Board and employee representatives share one conviction: We are in a structural and economic crisis in our industry," says interim CEO Claus Rettig. " We will use this polycrisis to change old structures and position ourselves better. Even in this crisis, many parts of our business are growing. We will therefore concentrate growth on our strengths, on the right future topics and on the most lucrative markets. At the same time, we will create leeway through better cost positions."
The comprehensive transformation of Evonik will thus continue at all levels. The portfolio will be strengthened through targeted investments in growth markets. In Canada and Slovakia , for example, growth projects have been launched in healthcare and biotechnology businesses with a total volume in the three-digit million euro range.
The individual business units will consistently be aligned according to their roles and managed accordingly: as growth drivers or cash generators. For example, the new business line Designed Polymer Solutions is currently being founded. It bundles growth areas from the aerospace, automotive and gas separation markets, including biogas and hydrogen.
Evonik sees good opportunities for growth particularly in Asia and America. Further investments in these regions are currently being examined. Growth opportunities in Asia and America are also to be exploited more quickly and consistently from the existing European production network, which mainly consists of the German sites. The goal remains a balanced distribution of revenue in the three regions Europe, Asia, and the Americas.
In Germany, a clear profile will be defined for each of the six major production sites, which serve as guidelines for their future development. Implementation will begin in the next few days.
At the same time, Evonik is withdrawing from activities for which there are no prospects within the company. "Only as leaders in what we do will we be able to establish ourselves at the forefront of our industry in the long term," says Rettig. "The future will remain volatile, which means we must be able to react in a flexible manner to short-term changes in order to be a reliable partner for our customers in all regions of the world. Our positioning and innovative strength in many key technologies in specialty chemicals mean we have a better foundation for this than our competition."
The announced closures of smaller sites are part of this context. The divestments of the large businesses C 4 chemicals (Oxeno GmbH) and infrastructure (Syneqt GmbH) are progressing as planned.
Evonik Tailor Made will enter its second implementation phase in 2027, run for three years until 2029 and seamlessly follow the first phase from 2024 to 2026.
Detailed measures will be completed by the end of 2026. They include not filling positions that become vacant, early retirements and voluntary departures against severance payments. "Evonik was and is known as a company that lives social responsibility and maintains an intensive dialogue with employee representatives," says Chief Human Resources Officer Thomas Wessel. "This transformation again is one that we are tackling together, and together we will successfully bring it to fruition."
Evonik: Leading beyond chemistry
Evonik goes beyond the boundaries of chemistry with its combination of innovative strength and leading technological expertise. The global chemical company, headquartered in Essen, Germany, is active in more than 100 countries and generated sales of €14.1 billion and earnings (adjusted EBITDA) of €1.9 billion in 2025. The common motivation of the approximately 31,000 employees: to provide customers with a decisive competitive advantage with tailor-made products and solutions as a superforce for industry, thereby improving people's lives. In all markets. Every day.

title: ALNF and Rio Tinto partner to strengthen First Nations languages
content_text:
ALNF and Rio Tinto partner to strengthen First Nations languages
22 September 2026
share
SYDNEY, Australia -- The Australian Literacy and Numeracy Foundation (ALNF) and Rio Tinto have announced a new three-year partnership to support First Nations communities in preserving, revitalising and strengthening their Languages for future generations.
The partnership supports the objectives of the United Nations International Decade of Indigenous Languages (2022 to 2032), assisting Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Language communities to develop and lead locally driven language initiatives through ALNF's Living First Languages Platform. Together, communities will document, teach and share Language, strengthen local capability, and develop new digital resources that help keep Languages strong and accessible for generations to come.
Developed alongside First Nations communities, ALNF's Living First Languages Platform places language ownership firmly in community hands. Combining cultural knowledge with digital technology, the platform enables communities to capture, manage and teach their Languages in ways that reflect local priorities, cultural protocols and aspirations.
The partnership will support community-led Language initiatives in Mapoon (Queensland), Nhulunbuy/Yirrkala (Northern Territory), Bidyadanga (Western Australia), Bundjalung Country (New South Wales and Queensland), and Kalkatungu Country (Queensland).
Cultural Heritage Advisor for the Mapoon Language Project Jason Jia said the partnership represents an important investment in the future of Language and culture.
"The Mapoon Language Project is more than a program, it is a living commitment to keeping language, culture, and identity strong for future generations. Through working alongside Elders and community, we are not just recording words, but strengthening connections to Country and ensuring our stories, knowledge, and voices continue to thrive for years to come.
"This work is essential, and ongoing funding ensures that this cultural knowledge is not lost but carried forward with pride and purpose."
Australian Literacy and Numeracy Foundation Chief Executive Anne Hollonds AO said: “We greatly appreciate the opportunity to work alongside communities dedicated to seeing teaching and learning flourish in their Languages. Being able to read, write, speak, listen and understand in one's own Language has a powerful lifelong impact on education, employment, identity, wellbeing, social connection and belonging. Communities are leading this work, and we are honoured to support them and be trusted by them.”
Rio Tinto Iron Ore Chief Executive and Australia Country Head Matthew Holcz said: “This partnership will provide Indigenous communities with a range of resources to retain control and ownership of their Languages.
“For tens of thousands of years, Indigenous communities have cared for Country, and by honouring their languages, we can help strengthen and protect this deep cultural history.”
Over the next three years, the partnership will support community-led Language initiatives across Australia through training, mentoring, community governance, technology, digital language resources, interactive learning tools and opportunities for Language groups to connect and learn from one another. It will also strengthen the Living First Languages Platform, ensuring communities continue to have access to practical tools that place Language ownership and knowledge in their own hands.
About the Australian Literacy & Numeracy Foundation
The Australian Literacy and Numeracy Foundation (ALNF) is a national charity dedicated to raising language, literacy and communication outcomes across Australia. For more than 25 years, ALNF has worked alongside communities to deliver specialised, evidence-based programs that create lasting opportunities for children, young people and families. Our work spans diverse communities across Australia, with a strong focus on First Nations communities, refugee and newly arrived communities, and those experiencing barriers to literacy and education. At ALNF, we believe literacy is freedom. Strong language and literacy skills open pathways to education, connection and opportunity, enabling people to participate fully in society, express themselves and have their voices heard.

title: BASF evaluates MDI investment in India
content_text:
BASF evaluates MDI investment in India
BASF is evaluating a potential investment in India as part of its continued commitment to serving growing customer demand in the region. The company is in the advanced stages of a feasibility study for the construction of an MDI (methylene diphenyl diisocyanate) production complex and has secured an industrial land parcel in Dahej, Gujarat, for the potential investment through its Indian subsidiary, BASF India Polyurethanes Private Limited. MDI is a key building block for polyurethane products used in applications ranging from building insulation and refrigeration to automotive components, furniture and consumer goods.
“India is among the most attractive growth markets globally, with strong demand expected across a wide range of industries,” said Dr. Stephan Kothrade, member of the Board of Executive Directors and Chief Technology Officer of BASF SE. “In line with our ‘Winning Ways’ strategy, we are focusing on investments that strengthen our core businesses and create long-term value. A potential investment in India would further expand our manufacturing footprint in a key growth market and, consistent with our local-for-local approach, enable us to serve customers in India and neighboring markets with locally produced MDI.”
The final investment decision will be based on the outcome of the feasibility study and will remain subject to all necessary approvals. 
“BASF continues to invest in its global MDI production network to support customer growth and ensure reliable supply across key markets,” said Dr. Ramkumar Dhruva, President of BASF’s Monomers division. “While the commissioning of our $1 billion MDI expansion project in Geismar is entering its final phase, we are evaluating the next potential step in strengthening our global MDI footprint. A project in India would complement our existing production network and further enhance supply reliability for our customers.” 
In addition to Geismar, United States, BASF operates MDI production facilities in Antwerp, Belgium; Chongqing and Caojing (Shanghai), China; and Yeosu, South Korea.
India has been part of BASF’s growth story for more than 130 years. Today, the company operates multiple production sites across the country, serving customers in a broad range of industries. At its integrated chemical complex in Dahej, BASF India Limited already operates an MDI splitter and polyurethane production facilities, making the location a strong foundation for further growth. As India’s urbanization, infrastructure development and manufacturing activities continue to accelerate, demand for high-performance materials is expected to grow.
 
About BASF 
At BASF, we create chemistry for a sustainable future. Our ambition: We want to be the preferred chemical company to enable our customers’ green transformation. We combine economic success with environmental protection and social responsibility. Around 95,000 employees in the BASF Group contribute to the success of our customers in nearly all sectors and almost every country in the world. Our portfolio comprises, as core businesses, the segments Chemicals, Materials, Industrial Solutions, and Nutrition & Care; our standalone businesses are bundled in the segments Surface Technologies and Agricultural Solutions. BASF generated sales of around €60 billion in 2025. BASF shares are traded on the stock exchange in Frankfurt (BAS) and as American Depositary Receipts (BASFY) in the United States. Further information at  www.basf.com .
 
About BASF in India 
BASF is well rooted in India and has successfully partnered India’s progress for more than 130 years. As of the end of 2025, BASF had 2,435 employees in India with 8 production sites and more than 40 offices throughout the country. The Innovation Campus Mumbai is part of BASF’s global technology platform. In 2025, BASF registered sales of approximately €2.3 billion to customers in India. Further information is available on  www.basf.com/in .

Now, Command Brand is stepping to the forefront of home design with the Command™ DÉCOR Collection , a new line of premium metal fixtures created to be seen, not hidden.
Inspired by the growing desire to make every detail of a home feel intentional, the collection brings together real metal construction, sophisticated gallery-inspired finishes and Command Brand's signature damage-free hanging technology. The result turns everyday fixtures into purposeful design accents that add style and function to any space.
"The Command DÉCOR Collection represents an evolution for Command Brand, bringing together the function consumers know and love with design they'll want to show off," said Tate Galvin, global vice president, Home Improvement, 3M. "We know consumers want their spaces to feel personal and thoughtfully designed, down to the smallest details. With the DÉCOR Collection, we're making it possible to express that personal style while still delivering the practicality and versatility Command Brand is known for."
Available in Brushed Brass, Light Beige, Matte Black and Chrome, the Command DÉCOR Collection transforms functional fixtures into elevated design accents for every room. From creating a welcoming entryway and displaying curated collections to bringing greenery to an empty wall or creating a spa-inspired bathroom, the collection offers versatile solutions that make function part of the design.
The collection includes:
Command Large and Small Metal Hooks: Refined solutions for hanging coats, bags, hats, accessories and jewelry, ideal for creating an elevated entryway.
Command Metal Wall Planter: A stylish way to bring greenery to walls, complete with a removable plastic insert for easy watering.
Command Metal Key Rail: A sleek, tool-free solution for keeping keys organized and within reach.
Command Metal Wall Shelf: A durable display and storage solution for curated décor, keepsakes and everyday essentials.

Each fixture also uses Command Brand's damage-free hanging technology, allowing consumers to hang items securely without nails, screws or tools and remove them without leaving marks or holes. Colours of our Country returns for its 21st year
content_text:
Colours of our Country returns for its 21st year
21 September 2026
share
PERTH, Australia--(BUSINESS WIRE)--
More than 120 artworks celebrating the enduring connection between people, Country and culture in the Pilbara will go on sale this month, as Colours of our Country returns for its 21st year.
This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260920420069/en/ 
Signature Artist Kariyarra and Yindjibarndi woman Wendy Warrie
This year's exhibition will run from 21 September to 2 October, showcasing the work of 29 Pilbara artists, including artists from the Cheeditha Art Group and Yinjaa-Barni Art Centre.
A painting by Cheeditha Art Group member Wendy Warrie, titled Out on the Horizon , has been chosen as the signature artwork for the 2026 exhibition. Ms Warrie, a Kariyarra and Yindjibarndi woman, has been painting for more than two decades, using her art to share stories of Country, culture, family and community. She is this year’s Signature Artist and Artist in Residence.
Ms Warrie said: "My painting at Colours of our Country is called ‘ Out on the Horizon '. When I was painting it, I was thinking about sitting out at the beach and watching the sun go down, trying to get a fish at the same time.
“All my paintings are a true story of what I've been doing in my life."
Since its 2006 launch, Colours of our Country has sold more than 3,325 artworks, with more than A$3.6 million going directly to Pilbara artists, art centres and their communities.
Rio Tinto Iron Ore Chief Executive Matthew Holcz said: “As Rio Tinto marks 60 years in the Pilbara, Colours of our Country reminds us of the rich culture, stories and artistic traditions that have been a part of the Pilbara region for tens of thousands of years.
"What began as part of Rio Tinto Iron Ore's 40th anniversary celebrations has grown into a much-loved annual exhibition that has supported hundreds of artists and helped share Pilbara Aboriginal culture with audiences in Australia and around the world.
"For two decades, Colours of our Country has connected artists with new audiences, while ensuring the benefits of every sale flow back to artists, art centres and communities."
The exhibition will be open weekdays from 8:00am to 4:30pm at Central Park Tower, 152-158 St Georges Terrace, Perth. Artworks are available for purchase at the exhibition and online at coloursofourcountry.com with all proceeds going directly to artists, art centres and their communities.

title: 09/18/2026 JSR and IBM's joint research outcome have been accepted for publication in Nature Computational Science
content_text:
JSR and IBM's joint research outcome have been accepted for publication in Nature Computational Science
09/18/2026 
Corporate 
JSR Corporation (Representative Director, President & CEO: Tetsuro Hori, hereinafter "JSR") and IBM today announced that a joint research outcome from their collaborative AI research program for the chemical industry has been accepted for publication in Nature Computational Science . The collaboration is being conducted under a Joint Research Agreement (JRA) between the two organizations. Nature Computational Science , published by Nature Portfolio, is a leading international scientific journal featuring research that applies computational science to address complex challenges across natural sciences, engineering, and related disciplines.
The published research combines IBM's expertise in AI and algorithms with JSR's deep knowledge of chemistry and materials science to achieve both high predictive accuracy and interpretability in the prediction of material properties for organic materials.
The method developed through this research leverages topological distance information within molecules, enabling it to capture complex structural characteristics of entire molecules that are difficult to represent using conventional approaches. Researchers from both organizations validated the predictions generated by the method through molecular orbital analysis. The results demonstrated superior performance compared with representative existing methods in predicting the optical properties of complex dye molecules, while also providing chemically interpretable explanations for the predictions. The research findings offer new insights for foundation models that handle complex molecular structures as well as for quantum chemistry calculations. Looking ahead, the approach is expected to contribute to more efficient materials development and the discovery of promising material candidates through applications in materials screening and molecular design.
Takeshi Fukuda, Executive Officer, Head of Research & Development, and Director of IBM Research - Tokyo, IBM Japan, said: "This achievement marks an important step forward in Material DX, where AI and materials experts work together to accelerate the discovery of new materials. Through our continued collaboration with JSR, we are committed to advancing materials development technologies by leveraging AI and quantum computing."
Toru Kimura, Senior Executive Officer, Head of Electronic Materials Business, Next Generation Research (DS/MI, etc.), JSR Corporation, said: "This achievement is significant, demonstrating the unprecedented potential of integrating AI and materials science in materials development. JSR will further enhance its research and development process, from materials exploration and design to experimentation and verification, by combining its long-cultivated materials expertise with cutting-edge digital technologies, including AI. Moving forward, through advanced initiatives and partnership with IBM, we aim to dramatically increase the speed and quality of development to deliver materials with new value to society more quickly."
As emerging technologies and digital transformation continue to accelerate, JSR and IBM are working together to help lead a new era of technological and societal advancement. JSR's materials innovation in the semiconductor field forms part of the backbone of a wide range of industries, helping enable a more connected world through technologies that are seamlessly integrated into everyday life.

content_text:
Renishaw's Equator-X™ gauge wins AMB Award for measuring technology and quality assurance
September 2026
Renishaw's Equator-X™ dual-method gauging system wins AMB Award for measuring technology and quality assurance.
Renishaw, a world leader in measuring and manufacturing systems, has won the 2026 AMB Award in the Measuring Technology and Quality Assurance category for its Equator-X™ dual-method gauging system.
The AMB Award recognises the most innovative products and exhibits showcased at the AMB exhibition held in Stuttgart, Germany, highlighting the latest advances in the metalworking industry. The jury, comprising leading representatives from the three supporting German trade associations and members of the scientific community, selected the Equator-X system in recognition of its contribution to enhancing process control and delivering greater measurement flexibility on the shop floor.
Introduced in 2025, the Equator-X gauge extends Renishaw's Equator™ range of shop floor gauging systems by combining absolute and comparative measurement methods within a single platform. The system was developed to help manufacturers address increasing product variety, shorter production runs and the need for faster inspection closer to the point of manufacture.
The ability to select either Absolute or Compare measurement modes enables manufacturers to apply the most appropriate measurement strategy for their production environment. In Absolute mode, the Equator-X system provides fully traceable inspection results while measuring at scanning speeds of up to 250 mm/s. In Compare mode, manufacturers can achieve scanning speeds of up to 500 mm/s for high-volume production applications where throughput is critical.
Rainer Krug, Sales & Business Development Director at Renishaw GmbH, said: "We are delighted our Equator-X™ system has received the 2026 AMB Award for the best product in Measuring Technology and Quality Assurance.”
Krug concluded, “The Equator-X gauging system enables companies to adapt quickly to changing production requirements while maintaining high standards of quality and efficiency and we are proud to see the value of this innovation recognised by a judging panel of experts in the field of metalworking and associated technologies.” 
The award reflects the growing importance of flexible measurement solutions in modern manufacturing environments, where manufacturers are under increasing pressure to improve productivity while maintaining quality and process capability.
Equator-X enables measurement to move closer to production, helping to reduce inspection bottlenecks while providing the process control data needed to support confident manufacturing decisions.

title: Charles River Leverages Expertise in Rapid and In Vitro Methods to Reduce Cell Banking Timelines
source: Charles River - News Releases / Press Releases
content_text:
View printer-friendly version 
Charles River Leverages Expertise in Rapid and In Vitro Methods to Reduce Cell Banking Timelines
PDF Version 
Charles River platform offers 40% reduction in cell bank production timeline, over the industry standard of 20 weeks 
WILMINGTON, Mass. --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Sep. 17, 2026--
Charles River Laboratories International, Inc. (NYSE: CRL) has introduced rapid cell banking programs designed to significantly accelerate release timelines, enabling biopharmaceutical and advanced therapy developers   to reach critical milestones faster and bring innovative treatments to patients sooner. By combining rapid cell bank and release packages with advanced characterization using Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS), Charles River delivers a comprehensive, end-to-end solution that enhances product quality, safety, and regulatory readiness while reducing overall development timelines.
“By leveraging our long-standing expertise in rapid test methods, we can expedite pre-bank and release testing timelines, enabling clients to establish and characterize cell banks quickly and move their product forward in development,” said Matthew Hewitt , Corporate Vice President, Chief Technology Officer, Manufacturing, Charles River. "The integration of rapid cell banking with NGS technologies provides a powerful advantage for developers, helping accelerate critical milestones, de-risk development programs, and ultimately bring innovative therapies to patients faster."
At every stage of the process, Charles River provides deep regulatory rigor and support, helping clients navigate the complexities of biologic and advanced therapy development, align with global regulatory expectations, and efficiently progress programs from early development through commercialization.
This platform offering further advances the Company's commitment to the 3Rs (Replacement, Reduction, Refinement) through its Alternative Methods Advancement Project™ (AMAP™), which develops and implements alternative methods and other innovative strategies to reduce reliance on animal testing while supporting efficient product development.
Established Expertise in Delivering Rapid Test Methods
To accelerate the establishment of cell banks, Charles River offers rapid microbiological methods (RMM) for microbial detection (including Celsis ® ATP-Bioluminescence technology) and rapid mycoplasma detection using real-time PCR. These technologies replace traditional compendial testing with automated, objective results, resulting in faster pre-bank, and release testing timelines.
Leveraging In Vitro Techniques for Next-Generation Sequencing
Following the establishment of cell banks, Charles River can leverage NGS, via our iDTECT ® platform, to provide reliable in vitro characterization services. NGS is revolutionizing how cell banks and advanced therapeutics are characterized and tested, ensuring high-quality products are delivered to patients. NGS has transformed the landscape of genetic analysis and pathogen detection with its scalability, speed, and broad viral detection capabilities.
“Cell bank characterization is a critical foundation for the development of biologic products, and NGS is transforming how the industry approaches safety and quality testing,” said Colette Côté, Executive Director & Scientific Advisor, Global Biologics Testing Services , Charles River. “By combining rapid cell banking capabilities with NGS as part of the cell bank characterization package, we help clients accelerate development timelines while generating the comprehensive data needed to support regulatory submissions and build confidence in product quality and safety."
Charles River’s CGMP-compliant NGS testing services accelerate development timelines without compromising safety, while meeting stringent global regulatory expectations for accuracy, reliability, and compliance, including GMP requirements and regulatory guidance from the FDA and EMA along with ICH Q5A and Q5B. The Company's acquisition of Pathoquest, a recognized leader in NGS solutions for in vitro characterization and quality control testing of biopharmaceutical products, further strengthens these capabilities. By integrating Pathoquest’s expertise and technology platform, Charles River delivers faster, more advanced sequencing-based testing solutions, enabling clients to move efficiently through development while maintaining confidence in product quality, safety, and regulatory readiness.
About the Alternative Methods Advancement Project (AMAP)
The Alternative Methods Advancement Project (AMAP) is a Charles River-led initiative dedicated to developing New Approach Methodologies (NAMs) and exploring innovative scientific and technological solutions aimed at reducing reliance on traditional animal testing. As we enter the next frontier of drug development, AMAP enables strategic, purpose-driven investment to shape a future in which more patients can access the treatments and medicines they need safely, swiftly, and successfully. AMAP is supported by our global, cross-functional Scientific Advisory Board led by Dr. Namandjé N. Bumpus .
About Charles River
Charles River provides essential products and services to help pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, government agencies and leading academic institutions around the globe accelerate their research and drug development efforts. Our dedicated employees are focused on providing clients with exactly what they need to improve and expedite the discovery, early-stage development and safe manufacture of new therapies for the patients who need them. To learn more about our unique portfolio and breadth of services, visit www.criver.com .

all articles

Plansee Shanghai wins the “China 2026 Belonging(DEIB) Award” 
Published by: Plansee Group 
· 
Last updated:
17. September 2026 
Plansee Shanghai has been honored with the 2026 Belonging Awards in recognition of its sustained commitment and outstanding achievements in fostering Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging (DEIB). 
Launched in January 2026, this year's awards program spanned six months and attracted applications from 714 renowned domestic and international companies across more than 40 countries and regions and 48 industries. A total of 47,838 submissions were received. Following a rigorous review process and multi-dimensional evaluation, Plansee Shanghai distinguished itself among a highly competitive field of participants. 
This prestigious recognition acknowledges our DEIB accomplishments, and also highlights its ongoing efforts to build a high-performing organization, cultivate an inclusive workplace culture, and support employee growth and development. 
As a leading company in refractory metals, alloys, and composite materials in China, Plansee Shanghai continuously enhances talent development framework. Through professional skills training, leadership development programs, and cross-functional collaboration initiatives, we provides employees with diverse development opportunities, enabling them to strengthen their capabilities while achieving mutual growth with the organization. 
In the areas of innovation and collaboration, Plansee Shanghai actively promotes cross-functional teamwork and encourages employees from diverse backgrounds and professional disciplines to contribute to problem-solving and innovation initiatives. The integration of diverse perspectives not only enhances organizational effectiveness but also injects fresh momentum into our ability to address market challenges and drive business innovation. We firmly believes that leveraging the unique strengths of every employee is essential to long-term success and sustainable growth. 
At Plansee Shanghai, diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging are key drivers of sustainable business success. Looking ahead, we will continue our efforts to foster an even more open, inclusive, and dynamic work environment where every employee feels respected, trusted, and valued. By supporting individual development and growth, we aim to grow together with our employees and build a more sustainable future for all. 
About the Plansee Group: Focus on Molybdenum and Tungsten
With its products, the Plansee Group enables applications at the cutting edge of what is technically and physically feasible – in electronics, medical technology, energy supply, mechanical engineering, the construction industry, mobility, and security and defense. 
Headquartered in Reutte, Tyrol, the group specializes in the powder metallurgical processing of the high-performance materials molybdenum and tungsten . The value chain extends from the processing of scrap and ore concentrates through the manufacture of intermediate products and blanks to the development and production of customer-specific components and tools. 
The Plansee Group, with its parent company Plansee Holding AG, unites two strong business areas : 
· Plansee High-Performance Materials, specializing in metallic products made of molybdenum and tungsten. 
· Ceratizit, focused on tools made of hard metal (tungsten carbide) for the trades, machining, and industrial manufacturing. 
The Plansee Group ensures long-term security of supply for its key materials through recycling and long-term partnerships with mining operators. The Plansee Group holds a 31 percent stake in the Chilean molybdenum processor Molymet and a 10 percent stake in the tungsten mining operator Almonty. 
With 11,120 employees at 36 production sites, the Plansee Group generated consolidated revenue of 2.35 billion euros in fiscal year 2025/26. The fiscal year ends on the last day of February.

title: Dow and Amcor launch strategic collaboration to accelerate adoption of low-carbon packaging solutions
content_text:
Dow and Amcor launch strategic collaboration to accelerate adoption of low-carbon packaging solutions
Companies combine complementary capabilities to help brands and retailers advance greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions reduction efforts
MIDLAND, Mich. and ZURICH – September 17, 2026 – Dow (NYSE: DOW), a global materials science company, and Amcor (NYSE: AMCR; ASX: AMC), a global leader in developing and producing responsible packaging solutions, today announced a strategic collaboration designed to help brands and retailers accelerate adoption of low carbon packaging solutions.
AmPrima® recycle-ready solutions from Amcor (product renderings)
Building off a shared history of advancing GHG emissions reduction efforts, the collaboration connects Dow's low carbon polyethylene (PE), materials science and carbon footprint expertise with Amcor's packaging innovation, manufacturing expertise and global reach. Together, Dow and Amcor aim to help brands and retailers easily implement and scale next-generation packaging solutions that deliver the required performance, quality and functionality while helping achieve their Scope 3 targets.
Under the collaboration, Dow and Amcor will work together to identify technically and commercially viable packaging applications, engage value chain partners early in the adoption process, and provide carbon footprint information to support customers as they navigate complex packaging decisions.
“One of the biggest barriers to decarbonization is the gap between consumer interest and commercial commitment,” said Keith Cleason , business president, Packaging & Specialty Plastics at Dow. “Together with Amcor, we are testing a new commercial model through market-based mechanisms to reduce adoption risk, create clearer demand signals and help accelerate commercialization of low carbon packaging solutions across the value chain. We are making it easier for brands and retailers to evaluate and integrate low carbon packaging options that support both business growth and sustainability objectives."
This collaboration comes at a time when companies have set ambitious GHG emissions reduction targets for Scope 3 emissions 1 , which account for indirect GHG emissions across the company’s value chain and often represent the largest share of a company’s carbon footprint. Increasingly, brands and retailers are looking for scalable packaging solutions that deliver measurable emissions reductions without requiring significant packaging redesigns or new infrastructure investments.
"Scope 3 emissions occur upstream and downstream in the value chain, making it difficult to reduce. Bringing low carbon polyethylene to market in packaging that meets the same technical and design standards is one of the simplest ways to help shrink a product’s carbon footprint,” said David Clark , chief sustainability officer at Amcor. "Because it’s truly a drop-in solution for brands, we see this collaboration as an exciting opportunity for them to translate climate commitments into action."
Central to the collaboration is the Carbon Footprint Ledger (CFL) methodology, which is based on the existing industry precedents of mass balance in GHG accounting. CFL provides independently assured product carbon footprint information aligned with internationally recognized standards, including ISO 14067 and the Greenhouse Gas Protocol Product Standard. Combined with Amcor's packaging expertise, the approach gives customers greater visibility into the climate impact of their packaging choices, helping them evaluate low carbon packaging options with greater confidence and transparency.
The collaboration reflects the growing importance of coordinated value-chain action, bringing together Dow and Amcor’s complementary capabilities to help customers advance GHG emissions reductions across packaging value chains. By working across materials, packaging and customer applications, the collaboration creates a more connected approach to addressing GHG emissions challenges that can be difficult for any one company to tackle alone.
About Dow 
Dow (NYSE: DOW) is one of the world’s leading materials science companies, serving customers in high-growth markets such as packaging, infrastructure, mobility and consumer applications. Our global breadth, asset integration and scale, customer-focused innovation and leading business positions enable us to achieve profitable growth and help deliver a sustainable future. We operate manufacturing sites in 29 countries and employed approximately 34,600 people as of year-end 2025. Dow delivered sales of approximately $40 billion in 2025. References to Dow or the Company mean Dow Inc. and its subsidiaries. Learn more about us at www.dow.com .
About Amcor 
Amcor (NYSE: AMCR; ASX: AMC) is the global leader in developing and producing responsible consumer packaging and dispensing solutions across a variety of materials for nutrition, health, beauty and wellness categories. Our global product innovation and sustainability expertise enables us to solve packaging challenges around the world every day, producing a range of flexible packaging, rigid packaging, cartons and closures that are more sustainable, functional and appealing for our customers and their consumers. We are guided by our purpose of elevating customers, shaping lives and protecting the future. Supported by a commitment to safety, 75,000 people generate $23 billion in annual sales from operations that span approximately 400 locations in more than 40 countries.

SCIENCE PARK EINDHOVEN, THE NETHERLANDS. (17 September, 2026) 
Prodrive Technologies announces the upcoming customer shipments of the new  Runix- MX105 high speed camera the first camera in the Runix product family. Designed for demanding semiconductor and industrial imaging applications, the camera combines ultra-high resolution with high-speed image acquisition in a compact and robust platform. The Runix-MX105 features the Sony IMX927 - 105-megapixel image sensor and delivers up to  112 frames per second, a perfect solution for high-speed inspection applications in the semiconductor and FPD industry as well as process monitoring, motion analysis, and scientific imaging.
The launch marks an important milestone in the development of the Runix series and expands Prodrive Technologies' portfolio of advanced machine vision solutions for high-performance inspection and metrology applications.

Asahi Kasei has confirmed that a former employee was arrested today by the Aichi Prefectural Police on suspicion of violating the Unfair Competition Prevention Act (UCPA) for purloining confidential information related to the company’s latent curing agent while employed and divulging such information to a third party, a Chinese company.
Asahi Kasei deeply regrets the concern caused by this matter to its business contacts, shareholders, and other stakeholders. As the investigation by the police is currently underway, Asahi Kasei is unable to disclose further information at this time. Moving forward, Asahi Kasei will continue to cooperate fully with the authorities.
Business contact information
Based on the investigation and confirmation performed by Asahi Kasei, the confidential information divulged in this case does not include any technical documents or personal information received from business contacts.
Prevention of recurrence
As Asahi Kasei believes that rigorous compliance in information management is critical, and has continuously implemented preventive measures and employee training, the company finds it profoundly disappointing that a former employee was arrested for purloining and divulging confidential information. Asahi Kasei is now applying the following additional measures to prevent the recurrence of such an incident.
1) Reinforced management of confidential information
Strengthening group-wide measures to prevent technology divulgence
Clear identification and categorization of confidential information; thorough application of stricter management procedures
Adopting new IT tools for rigorous information management
Reviewing permissions to access confidential information
2) Tighter policies related to departing employees, including mandatory pledges and stricter handling of company-issued computers
3) Thorough training of all Executives and employees regarding the management of confidential information
Asahi Kasei will continue to strengthen efforts to prevent recurrence while ensuring thorough compliance education for all employees, etc.
Future actions
Investigation by Asahi Kasei has confirmed that the former employee purloined confidential information related to the company’s latent curing agent while employed, and divulged such information to Shandong Shengquan New Materials Co., Ltd. (Shandong Shengquan), a Chinese company, after no longer being employed by Asahi Kasei. To protect its confidential information, Asahi Kasei plans to institute civil proceedings against the former employee and Shandong Shengquan seeking cessation of use of, and destruction of, the confidential information, as well as other remedies.
Furthermore, Asahi Kasei will continue to investigate whether the divulged confidential information has been improperly used, and should such use be identified, take similar firm measures against the parties involved.

Company outlines a $213 billion market opportunity as power becomes the foundational technology layer from infrastructure to physical applications
SCOTTSDALE, Ariz., Sept. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- onsemi (NASDAQ: ON) today outlined its long-term growth strategy to lead one of the largest and most consequential technology shifts of the next decade by solving the growing power constraints limiting the advancement of AI, electrification and automation. As these markets converge around common technology requirements, onsemi is leveraging its differentiated portfolio across power and sensing to address a $213 billion market opportunity and solve the needs of some of the most important technology trends shaping the global economy.
“Every transformational technology eventually encounters a physical constraint. As AI, electrification and automation continue to scale, power density is emerging as one of the defining engineering challenges of this decade,” said Hassane El-Khoury, President and CEO of onsemi. “The companies that lead in the next era of innovation will be those that can deliver more energy while consuming less space. As that challenge becomes more urgent, power has become a foundational technology layer that will help shape the pace of innovation, economic growth and global competitiveness. We have spent years building deep expertise and a broad portfolio across power and sensing to help customers solve this challenge and enable the next generation of intelligent machines.”
Unlocking a $213 Billion Opportunity 
onsemi sees a $213 billion total addressable market by 2030 spanning automotive, industrial, AI data center and emerging applications. Although these markets are often viewed separately, they increasingly rely on the same underlying capabilities: efficient power conversion, perception of the physical world, precision actuation and control, and connectivity.
This convergence allows onsemi to deploy common technology platforms across multiple end markets. A high-voltage technology developed for automotive electrification, for example, can also support industrial energy systems and AI data centers. Advances in sensing and connectivity can extend across vehicles, factories, robotics, medical systems and other autonomous applications.
The company expects this platform-based model to increase the revenue potential of its core technologies by moving from individual components to higher-value solutions and system architectures that address a larger share of each customer's design requirements. Through this approach, onsemi can generate greater leverage from its R&D investments, reduce dependence on any single end market or technology cycle, and grow faster than the markets it serves.
“Throughout history, foundational technologies have created outsized value because they enable everything built above them,” El-Khoury said. “Power has become the common denominator across these end markets. For onsemi, that creates opportunities to innovate beyond any market trend, with multiple paths to expand content, gain share and capture more value.”
Solving the Next Challenge: Power Density 
Capturing this opportunity requires addressing a growing constraint facing AI infrastructure and other intelligent systems – power density – or the ability to deliver greater performance and capability using less energy and less physical space.
Increasing power density requires electrical, thermal, mechanical and physical performance to be optimized simultaneously. Increasing power typically generates more heat, while reducing system size can make that heat more difficult to remove. Improving efficiency may require new materials, device architectures and integration methods. Historically, these trade-offs forced system designers to make compromises among power, size, cost and thermal performance.
As these challenges become more complex, value increasingly shifts to companies that can optimize across the entire system. onsemi has expanded beyond traditional power semiconductors to build capabilities spanning technologies, products, solutions and systems. onsemi highlighted three technology platforms that will shape the next generation of intelligent systems and drive long-term growth across its key end markets:
High-Voltage Technologies: The Device Layer
onsemi's high-voltage portfolio spans silicon, silicon carbide (SiC) and gallium nitride (GaN), giving customers a range of options to optimize performance, efficiency, power density and cost. The portfolio includes vertical gallium nitride (vGaN), a differentiated technology, exclusive to onsemi, designed for next-generation high-voltage applications that can increase efficiency, improve switching performance and reduce system size where conventional power technologies are reaching their limits.
Treo: The Intelligence Layer
Modern systems must do more than convert power. They must monitor operating conditions, communicate across the system, respond to changing loads and protect critical functions in real-time. The Treo platform’s high precision analog, high density digital and high voltage capabilities, enable systems to become more precise, adaptive and autonomous. This allows onsemi to add these capabilities around the power device, increasing the functionality and value within a customer’s system.
Embedded Power Platform (EPP): The Integration Layer
EPP reimagines the package from passive housing into an active contributor to system performance. By using the silicon wafer itself as the package, EPP enables the seamless integration and interconnection of silicon, SiC and GaN technologies within a highly integrated wafer-level architecture. Multiple devices, including FETs, drivers and controllers, can be embedded together in a single package and co-optimized for electrical, thermal and mechanical performance. This enables complete power-system co-design, allowing electrical, thermal and mechanical characteristics to be evaluated and optimized together from day one. The result is higher power density, improved system performance, reduced development complexity and faster time-to-market.
As customers increasingly seek complete solutions rather than individual components, onsemi solves a larger portion of the customer’s challenge by reducing design complexity and accelerating development across automotive, industrial, AI data center and emerging applications. With this focus on the entire system-level solution, onsemi creates a competitive advantage that is difficult to replicate through individual components alone.
Beyond the Data Center: AI's Next Frontier is the Physical World 
While today's AI investments are largely focused on building the infrastructure needed to train and run increasingly sophisticated models, the next phase of growth will occur at the edge, where intelligence moves beyond the data center into machines that interact directly with the physical world.
These physical AI systems must sense, decide, act and adapt safely in real-world environments, in real-time. Whether deployed in a robot, vehicle, factory, medical system or autonomous platform, each system requires four capabilities to operate together:
Power to provide the energy foundation that enables intelligent systems to operate
Sense to perceive and understand the physical environment
Control to execute decisions through precise real-world actions
Connected Compute to process, share and continuously adapt information at the edge
As this transition happens, many of these same technologies onsemi developed for automotive and industrial applications can be applied to this emerging market. onsemi's ability to combine these capabilities through system-level co-design and optimize performance across the full stack, positions it to deliver differentiated solutions and capture a larger share of the value created by physical AI.
“The most attractive opportunities of the next decade are emerging as markets converge around the same technologies,” El-Khoury said. “The ability to efficiently deliver power, sense the environment and enable intelligent decision-making will define the next generation of intelligent machines. Our differentiated technology platforms enable us to solve power density across the device, intelligence and integration layers in a way no other semiconductor company can, positioning us to expand our content and grow as AI moves from infrastructure into the physical world.”
