title: Infineon extends collaboration with SolarEdge to enable
content_text:
Infineon extends collaboration with SolarEdge to enable solid-state protection for 800 VDC AI data centers
Business & Financial Press
Sep 09, 2026 
Companies extend collaboration into solid-state circuit breaker (SSCB) technology in line with leading industry framework for 800 Volts direct current (VDC) architecture 
SSCB technology is designed to interrupt DC faults orders of magnitude faster than electromechanical breakers, addressing one of the key challenges in deploying high-voltage DC power architectures 
The collaboration advances a DC-native power architecture from medium-voltage grid connection through distribution to the rack, to support higher density, greater reliability and reduced environmental impact for AI data centers 
Munich, Germany and Milpitas, California – 9 September, 2026 – Infineon Technologies AG (FSE: IFX / OTCQX: IFNNY) and SolarEdge Technologies, Inc. (NASDAQ: SEDG), a global leader in smart energy, today announced an extension of their collaboration to advance solid-state circuit breaker (SSCB) technology for high-voltage DC distribution in AI and hyperscale data centers. The collaboration addresses a key challenge in the adoption of 800 VDC architecture: Safe operation of increasingly power-dense infrastructure requires a very fast fault-isolation to achieve selectivity while maintaining high efficiency.
Extending the collaboration to solid-state protection addresses a critical gap in the distribution layer between the solid-state transformer (SST) and the compute rack, advancing a comprehensive grid-to-rack solution. SolarEdge is leading the design of the SSCB solution, with Infineon providing its silicon carbide (SiC) JFET technology at the core of the protection devices.
As rapidly increasing AI compute density drives the industry toward higher-voltage DC distribution, solid-state circuit breakers address one of the most fundamental challenges in enabling safe and reliable operation. Unlike conventional alternating current (AC) systems, DC protection presents a different engineering challenge. Without a natural current zero, mechanical interruption faces challenges with arcing. It is comparatively slow, and as such requires a different approach to circuit protection than conventional AC systems. Solid-state circuit breakers are designed to interrupt faults within a few microseconds, with no mechanical contacts to separate, while Infineon's CoolSiC™ JFET devices deliver efficient operation and superior robustness. Together, these capabilities help protect high-value compute equipment and enable more compact, higher-density DC distribution designs.
The collaboration builds directly on SolarEdge's SST platform with Infineon SiC components, first announced in November 2025. The SST is designed to enable direct medium-voltage (13.8-34.5 kV) to 800-1500 VDC conversion at over 99 percent efficiency, collapsing multiple conversion stages into a single solution while reducing physical footprint. 
"High-density AI infrastructure at 800 VDC demands uncompromising efficiency and protection", said Shuki Nir, Chief Executive Officer of SolarEdge. "Solid-state protection will enable operators to achieve both, delivering ultra-fast and dependable fault isolation without sacrificing conversion performance. Infineon's silicon carbide technology is what makes it practical at scale."
"Today’s data infrastructures have become more vulnerable to electrical faults, thereby driving the demand for smarter, faster and more robust power distribution systems," said Andreas Weisl, Executive Vice President and Chief Sales Officer of Industrial & Infrastructure at Infineon. "By combining our advanced silicon carbide JFET technology with SolarEdge’s expertise in final power distribution, we are addressing these demands to ensure fast, safe and reliable operations in AI data centers."
Building on more than 15 years of leadership in DC-coupled power electronics, SolarEdge is developing an 800 VDC powertrain for AI factories, a DC-native chain that carries power from the medium-voltage grid connection through conversion, distribution and protection to the compute rack. Infineon's broad portfolio of silicon, silicon carbide and gallium nitride solutions provides that foundation, supporting the decarbonization of AI infrastructure through lower losses, reduced environmental impact, and improved total cost of ownership.
About SolarEdge 
SolarEdge is a global leader in smart energy technology. By leveraging world-class engineering capabilities and with a relentless focus on innovation, SolarEdge creates smart energy solutions that power our lives and drive future progress. SolarEdge developed an intelligent inverter solution that changed the way power is harvested and managed in photovoltaic (PV) systems. The SolarEdge DC optimized inverter seeks to maximize power generation while lowering the cost of energy produced by the PV system. Continuing to advance smart energy, SolarEdge addresses a broad range of energy market segments through its PV, storage, EV charging, batteries, and grid services solutions. SolarEdge is online at www.solaredge.com .

title: Infineon enters into agreement to sell NOR Flash and F
content_text:
Infineon enters into agreement to sell NOR Flash and F-RAM business to Winbond and sharpens focus on core growth areas 
Business & Financial Press
Sep 16, 2026 
Transaction valued at $1.12 billion supports Infineon's strategic focus and profitable growth 
Transaction reflects the strong market position and value created by the NOR Flash and F-RAM business 
Infineon to retain portfolio of specialty memory solutions including SRAM, HYPERRAM™, nvSRAM and SONOS based radiation-hardened memory solutions 
Munich, Germany – 16 September 2026 – Infineon Technologies AG (FSE: IFX / OTCQX: IFNNY) today announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement under which Winbond Electronics Corporation, a Taiwan-based global supplier of semiconductor memory solutions, will acquire Infineon’s NOR Flash and F-RAM business in an all-cash transaction valued at $1.12 billion on a cash and debt free basis. The business comprises a portfolio of NOR Flash memory as well as F-RAM products serving customers across automotive, industrial and infrastructure markets. Subject to obtaining the required regulatory approvals, the parties currently target closing the transaction in the second half of 2027.
“The transaction represents a highly compelling strategic outcome for all stakeholders,” said Peter Schiefer, President of Infineon’s Automotive Division. “It allows Infineon to further focus its portfolio and capital allocation on its core growth drivers. At the same time, it enables our NOR Flash and F-RAM business to unlock its full potential.”
Winbond is a leading provider with a focus on memory solutions which makes the company a good fit to unlock future growth possibilities for Infineon’s NOR Flash and F-RAM business. The combination of Winbond’s existing memory portfolio and Infineon’s NOR Flash and F-RAM business will provide customers with a broad and complementary portfolio of NOR Flash and F-RAM products. Winbond will operate the acquired business as a standalone entity with headquarters in Silicon Valley in the United States.
Infineon will continue to offer a portfolio of specialty memory solutions, including SRAM, HYPERRAM™, nvSRAM and SONOS based radiation-hardened memory solutions. These technologies remain an important part of Infineon's portfolio across automotive, industrial, infrastructure, aerospace and defense applications, including a strong product offering of high-reliability memory solutions for space missions.

title: Infineon Wins Integrated Communication Award 2026 for
content_text:
Infineon Wins Integrated Communication Award 2026 for Integrated Communication Management 
Business & Financial Press
Sep 23, 2026 
Munich, Germany – 23 September 2026 – Infineon Technologies AG has been honored with the Integrated Communication Award 2026 in the category “Integrated Communication Management.” The award was presented on 22 September during the 19th German Brand Summit at the F.A.Z. Tower in Frankfurt am Main. Through this recognition, the F.A.Z. Institute and an expert jury acknowledge companies that consistently organize their communications strategically, from alignment with overarching business objectives and clear governance structures to technology-enabled processes and a collaborative communication culture.
“Strategic and integrated communication makes a decisive contribution to business success. We are pleased to receive this recognition,” said Florian Martens, Executive Vice President & Chief Communications Officer at Infineon. “In an increasingly complex communications landscape, we can only create impact by breaking down silos and addressing topics holistically. This award recognizes the progress our team has achieved together over the past several years. My sincere thanks go to all colleagues who have helped shape this journey.”
Infineon’s communications function operates within an integrated organization that brings together all communication disciplines, ranging from public affairs and corporate communications to marketing communications, regional communications, and communication services. Content is planned and managed across functions and channels, topic ownership is bundled, and communication activities are aligned with strategic objectives. Clear performance indicators are used to measure success. In this way, communications makes a significant and measurable contribution to Infineon’s corporate strategy and business performance.
The jury particularly recognized the holistic approach with which Infineon manages communications across the company: “What impressed us was the consistent way communication has been transformed into an integrated management system. Planning, processes, topic management, and measurement are systematically interconnected. Particularly noteworthy are the clear governance framework and the transparent management architecture, which create a traceable link between communication activities and business objectives.”
The Integrated Communication Award, presented by the F.A.Z. Institute, recognizes outstanding approaches to integrated communications. In the category “Integrated Communication Management,” Allianz, Bayer, GEA, and Merck were also nominated alongside Infineon. The jury comprises communications experts from both industry and academia and is chaired by Prof. Dr. Ansgar Zerfass of Leipzig University.

title: Infineon and Eaton leverage silicon carbide technology
content_text:
Infineon and Eaton leverage silicon carbide technology to advance solid-state transformers for 800 VDC AI data center power architectures
Business & Financial Press
Sep 29, 2026 
Infineon and Eaton are partnering to drive solid-state transformer (SST) technology 
The collaboration addresses demand for more efficient power conversion solutions in AI data centers 
Infineon’s silicon carbide power devices help enhance efficiency, power density and system reliability of Eaton’s SST platform 
Munich, Germany – 29 September, 2026 – Infineon Technologies AG (FSE: IFX / OTCQX: IFNNY) will deliver silicon carbide (SiC) power devices to Eaton, an intelligent power management company, for use in its medium-voltage solid-state transformer (MVSST) 2.0 platform designed for deployment across APAC. The collaboration helps increase the efficiency and reliability of the power conversion required to connect AI data centers to the electricity grid. It targets 800 Volts direct current (VDC) data center power distribution architectures.
The rapid expansion of AI data centers and rising power requirements are driving demand for more efficient ways to connect high-density computing infrastructure to the grid. At the same time, advances in medium-voltage DC distribution technologies are accelerating the need for next-generation power conversion solutions that can improve efficiency, power density, scalability and reliability.
"As energy demand from AI data centers and industrial applications continues to grow, the demand for efficient, reliable and sustainable power conversion is increasing," said Andreas Weisl, Executive Vice President and Chief Sales Officer of Industrial & Infrastructure at Infineon. "By joining forces with Eaton, we aim to advance solid-state transformer technology and contribute to the development of a more scalable, efficient and sustainable infrastructure for powering the AI data centers of the future."
"Against the backdrop of rapidly increasing requirements for power efficiency, system reliability and scalability in AI data centers, our goal is to advance the development and adoption of SST technology. Thus, we aim to create greater value for data center and power grid operators as well as the renewable energy sector," said David Zheng, Vice President of R&D for Power Quality in APAC at Eaton. "Infineon’s advanced SiC technology is helping us accelerate the deployment of these next-generation power architectures." 
Designed for high-density computing infrastructures and emerging 800 VDC AI data center power distribution architectures, Eaton’s MVSST 2.0 platform reduces conversion stages compared with conventional architectures, improving efficiency, power density and deployment flexibility. As one of the first medium-voltage solid-state transformer platforms to achieve IEC certification, it combines advanced silicon carbide technology with Eaton's expertise in power distribution and conversion to support next-generation energy infrastructure. 
Looking ahead, Eaton and Infineon are exploring next-generation SST platforms based on 2.3 kV and 3.3 kV SiC power modules to support higher system voltages, greater efficiency and enhanced reliability for future AI data centers, grid modernization and renewable energy applications.

Annual report 2025
The fiscal year 2025 was marked by various challenges for Jenoptik, particularly from the semiconductor equipment and automotive markets. Nevertheless, we have continued to focus on our relevant growth potentials in our core markets of semiconductors, medical technology, metrology and smart mobility, and we look to the future with optimism thanks to our strong growth platforms. 
Overview over the fiscal year 2025
Jenoptik performed well overall in a challenging market environment in 2025.
Despite a 6 percent decline in revenue , we were able to maintain our profitability at a good level, with an EBITDA margin of 18.4 percent, thanks to cost reduction measures implemented early on.
We succeeded in further improving key balance sheet and financial ratios. The Group increased its equity ratio to around 60 percent, and free cash flow before interest and taxes rose by approximately 50 million euros.
The Executive Board and Supervisory Board will propose a dividend  payout of 0.40 euros per share to the Annual General Meeting.
The Group’s organizational structure has been realigned more closely with our growth areas of semiconductors, medical technology, metrology, and smart mobility.
With the opening of the new fab  for innovative micro-optics in Dresden, Germany, an important foundation was laid to realize further growth potential in this area.
Our approach to sustainability : As an “enabler,” we use our expertise and innovative products to make an important contribution to overcome social and climate challenges, enable customers worldwide to contribute more efficiently and sustainably to conserving resources and protecting the climate.
Outlook : We expect to return to a growth path in fiscal year 2026.

In Asia-Pacific, Air Liquide operates at the heart of the global technology race and amid the most dynamic industrial reconfigurations. Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany to Acquire Silence Therapeutics, Strengthening Rare Disease Pipeline with Innovative siRNA Asset 
We enter into a definitive agreement to acquire biotechnology company Silence Therapeutics, focused on siRNA-therapies in areas of high unmet need. 
Subscribe
Share 
Icons revealed to the left 
19 Oct 2026 
| 
Darmstadt, Germany 
Purchase price of $20 per ADS in cash represents an enterprise value of $1.1 billion and an equity value of approximately $1.3 billion 
Silence Therapeutics is a UK-headquartered biotechnology company with a potentially best-in-class Phase 3-ready investigational siRNA therapy for rare disease, polycythemia vera (PV) 
Planned acquisition will strengthen the position of Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany in rare diseases, a high-value growth driver, and advance its Healthcare ambition to become a leading Global Specialty Innovator 
Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, a leading science and technology company, today announced its entry into a definitive agreement to acquire Silence Therapeutics plc (Nasdaq: SLN), a global clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered in London, UK, focused on pioneering the design and development of siRNA (short interfering RNA) therapies in areas of high unmet need.
The purchase price of $20 per ADS in cash, with each ADS representing three ordinary shares of Silence Therapeutics (or $6.6667 per ordinary share), represents an enterprise value of $1.1 billion and an equity value of approximately $1.3 billion. The consideration represents an 82% premium to Silence Therapeutics’ 30-day volume-weighted average price of $10.99, as of the close of trading on October 16, 2026, the last trading day prior to the transaction announcement. The transaction is subject to satisfaction of customary closing conditions.
“The planned acquisition of Silence Therapeutics will strengthen our capabilities to serve patients with targeted specialty and rare diseases,” said Kai Beckmann, Chairman of the Executive Board and Group CEO of Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany. “Following the acquisition of SpringWorks Therapeutics last year, we continue to transform our pipeline toward areas of high specialization and unmet medical need, with an ongoing commitment to external innovation. The proposed transaction follows our strategic priority to address attractive end markets also through M&A, creating value over the mid- to long-term.”
The transaction, once completed, will add Divesiran ─ a potentially best-in-class, phase 3-ready siRNA investigational therapy, in development for phlebotomy-dependent polycythemia vera (PV) ─ to Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany’s pipeline. Divesiran is dosed subcutaneously once every 3 months.
PV is a chronic myeloproliferative neoplasm ─ a type of rare blood cancer ─ characterized by the excessive production of red blood cells, which can be associated with a higher rate of death from cardiovascular and thrombotic events.
Divesiran is designed to selectively silence TMPRSS6, a gene involved in regulating hepcidin, the body’s key regulator of iron metabolism. By increasing hepcidin levels, Divesiran aims to limit iron availability for red blood cell production, helping to control hematocrit levels and potentially reducing the need for frequent therapeutic phlebotomies.
Divesiran met its primary endpoint in the Phase 2 SANRECO study with an 88% responder rate versus 19% for placebo (p “The planned acquisition of Silence Therapeutics marks a significant step forward in our strategy to become a Global Specialty Innovator in Healthcare,” said Danny Bar-Zohar, member of the Executive Board and CEO Healthcare at Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany. “Silence Therapeutics’ primary siRNA pipeline asset, Divesiran, is supported by promising Phase 2 efficacy data, a potentially best-in-class, once-every-three-month dosing schedule, and a safety profile that appears manageable, with the added advantage of targeting a well-defined, homogeneous patient population. The planned acquisition also provides an entry point into hematology through a biologically validated mechanism of action. With this transaction, we are advancing our efforts to build a differentiated, sustainable pipeline as we bring more medicines to more patients, faster.”
“We are pleased to have reached this agreement with Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, which follows a competitive sale process and delivers significant, immediate and certain value to our shareholders,” said Iain Ross, Interim Principal Executive Officer and Chairman of the Silence Therapeutics’ Board. “This transaction follows potentially best-in-class Phase 2 polycythemia vera data for Divesiran and reflects the important progress we have made advancing our differentiated siRNA pipeline. It also provides a new home for our innovative programs within Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, placing Divesiran with a company that has the scale, resources and commercial capabilities to accelerate its Phase 3 development and bring this potentially best-in-class siRNA therapy to patients in need. We are incredibly grateful to our employees for their dedication and contributions in building Silence Therapeutics into the company it is today.”
The transaction has been unanimously approved by Silence Therapeutics’ Board of Directors and Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany’s relevant corporate bodies and is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, subject to satisfaction of customary closing conditions, including receipt of required regulatory approvals and approval by Silence Therapeutics’ shareholders. In connection with the transaction, certain securityholders of Silence Therapeutics holding securities representing approximately 14% of Silence Therapeutics’ voting power have entered into a voting and support agreement with Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, under which the securityholders have agreed among other things, to vote their voting securities of Silence Therapeutics in favor of the transaction. Silence Therapeutics is a UK company, with ADSs, each representing three of its ordinary shares, listed on NASDAQ. As is customary for similar transactions, the transaction will be effected through a UK scheme of arrangement.
The planned acquisition will be funded through proceeds from new debt.
Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany is committed to leveraging advanced technologies and data science to accelerate the discovery and delivery of breakthrough medicines. This acquisition is another step forward in its broader strategy to enhance research productivity and the output of its pipeline sustainably, focusing on indications that can be derisked through proper preclinical and early clinical testing to ensure that more patients gain access to effective treatments.
Silence Therapeutics employs approximately 80 people and operates from locations in the UK, the US and Germany.
A&O Shearman is acting as legal counsel to Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany.

title: EU and UK Risk Falling Further Behind Global Agricultural Competitors, Weakening Strategic Autonomy
content_text:
EU and UK Risk Falling Further Behind Global Agricultural Competitors, Weakening Strategic Autonomy
Summary
Europe’s crop output has grown more slowly than in major agricultural markets including the US, Brazil, China, Canada and India, a new study finds / Geopolitical and climate pressures are increasing risks for farmers while global peers gain faster access to new technologies, widening Europe’s resilience gap / Consumers support science-based innovation and want farmers to have access to technologies that help strengthen food security, resilience and affordability
Leverkusen, October 15, 2026 – The EU and the UK risk falling further behind major agricultural competitors like the US, Brazil, China, Canada and India unless farmers gain faster access to innovation that can help address growing climate and productivity pressures. A more proportionate regulatory framework and more openness to new technologies could help reverse this trend. These are the main takeaways of a new report commissioned by Bayer, combining economic analysis by Oxford Economics, representative polling of more than 8,000 consumers and in-depth farmer interviews across eight European markets. 
The findings identify crop agriculture as a strategically important sector that underpins food security and contributes 246 billion euros to EU GDP and 5.7 billion euros to UK GDP, with every 1 billion euros of crop agriculture output supporting almost 3 billion euros of downstream production in other sectors. However, crop output growth in Europe has significantly lagged global peers between 2011 and 2023, averaging just 0.1 percent a year. In the UK, growth was even lower, at 0.0 percent. This compares with 1 percent in the US, a global average of 2 percent, and between 2 and 3 percent in China, Canada and India. Brazil was among the fastest-growing markets, with annual growth averaging 3.3 percent over the period. The longer-term comparison is equally stark: average EU production was only 2 percent higher than in the previous decade, compared with increases of 16 percent in the US, 44 percent in Canada and 51 percent in Brazil. 
These competitive pressures are being compounded by sharply rising input costs and the growing impact of climate change. Climate-related risks already cause estimated average annual losses of 17.4 billion euros—equivalent to 6.4 percent of EU crop production—with significant variation across regions. By 2050, these losses are projected to rise to between 24.8 billion euros and 28.9 billion euros. 
The research identifies a growing risk arising from the rapid pace at which pressures on farmers are intensifying, combined with the time it takes for innovations to reach the field. European farmers compete against producers from other regions who have access to a wider variety of seed technologies, crop protection solutions and digital technologies or gain access to such innovations faster. According to Oxford Economics, better access to modern technologies can support farmers in addressing the significant climate and geopolitical challenges, strengthening the agricultural sector’s competitiveness and resilience. 
“The EU and the UK are confronted with a widening resilience gap. To counter that, agriculture must be understood as a critical strategic sector for Europe’s autonomy and competitiveness,” said Frank Terhorst, Head of Strategy & Sustainability for Bayer’s Crop Science Division. “It is critical to embrace innovation as an opportunity rather than a risk to be managed. Europe has the capabilities to lead, but we need to ensure that enough solutions are available to farmers and that innovation can reach the field faster.” 
Research highlights regulatory barriers to agricultural innovation 
The report argues that European farmers need access to a broader range of solutions, including innovative seed technologies, modern crop protection products, precision agriculture, automation and artificial intelligence. Just recently, Bayer announced an upcoming phase of major innovation launches with new seed and trait solutions, including genome editing, and the AI-enabled discovery of new modes of action for crop protection. However, the availability of these agricultural solutions depends largely on regulatory frameworks. 
The research findings highlight a growing concern among farmers that their toolbox is becoming increasingly constrained: While more than 1,000 active ingredients were authorised in the EU in the early 2000s, only around 420 remain approved today. Farmers have lost access to 92 active ingredients in the last seven years, while only one new synthetic active ingredient reached the market over the same period. The UK has approved four entirely new active ingredients since 2022 that remain unapproved or pending in the EU while maintaining approval of 15 crop protection active ingredients whose EU licences have expired or been banned since Brexit. However, the dynamic alignment with the EU regulatory framework currently under discussion could lead to a withdrawal of these approvals, potentially impacting crop yields and farm incomes if transitions are not managed carefully. 
As a consequence, the research points to the need for a more predictable and proportionate regulatory environment that supports innovation while maintaining high standards of safety and stewardship. It highlights lengthy approval processes, increasing administrative burdens and slower adoption pathways as factors limiting access to new technologies across Europe. 
“An approval approach based on real-world risks and benefits instead of theoretical hazards can help ensure farmers gain access to proven innovations while maintaining Europe's high safety standards. Recent UK approvals demonstrate how proportionate pathways can support quicker access to innovation,” added Frank Terhorst. “The report’s findings underscore the urgent need for agricultural innovation. We invest heavily in such new solutions, and we want European farmers to benefit from them like their global peers do.” 
Consumers recognise the importance of agriculture and support science-based innovation 
The consumer polling reveals public awareness of the strategic importance of agriculture. Across Europe, 84 percent of consumers agree that food security is a matter of national security. Consumers see farmer resilience, food affordability and food security as interconnected elements of the same challenge. 
Europeans are also broadly supportive of science and technology. 84 percent say farmers should have access to the latest technology and innovation, so that innovation moves faster, farmers get better harvests and food prices come down. They perceive regulatory barriers, too: 77 percent say cutting bureaucracy and red tape would help make sure Europe can produce enough food. 63 percent say they are more likely to vote for a party that backed farmers using new science and technology. 
“Europeans are more open to innovation and technology than many would assume. People see the connection between resilient farming, food security and affordable food,” summarised Matthias Berninger, Head of Public Affairs, Science, Sustainability & HSE at Bayer. “The findings are a call to action for political, business and civil-society leaders to champion science and new technologies. Europe has spent too much time admiring problems rather than seizing opportunities. While regulation must ensure safety and build trust, it should also enable progress in areas such as AI and agriculture. Europe must move from a culture of risk avoidance to one of innovation.” According to Berninger, Europe has exactly what it takes: “This summer’s decision on New Genomic Techniques demonstrated that Europe can choose innovation over hesitation. We must not lose that momentum. We have great farmers, scientific expertise, good soils and industrial capabilities. We now need to translate these strengths into greater resilience and competitiveness.” 
About the report: 
The research was commissioned by Bayer and combines economic analysis conducted by Oxford Economics, representative polling of more than 8,000 consumers and in-depth interviews with around 90 farmers across eight European markets (Benelux, France, Germany, Italy, Poland, Romania, Spain, United Kingdom). It examines the role innovation can play in strengthening the productivity, competitiveness and resilience of European agriculture, as well as the conditions affecting access to and adoption of new technologies.

title: Vividion Therapeutics Expands Clinical Development of WRN Inhibitor VVD-214 with Phase II Combination Study in First-Line Patients with Advanced Colorectal Cancer
content_text:
Vividion Therapeutics Expands Clinical Development of WRN Inhibitor VVD-214 with Phase II Combination Study in First-Line Patients with Advanced Colorectal Cancer
Not intended for UK Media
Summary
First patient dosed in global Phase II study evaluating VVD-214, an oral Werner helicase (WRN) inhibitor, plus pembrolizumab in front-line patients with advanced MSI-high or dMMR colorectal cancer / Study broadens clinical development of VVD-214 into the first-line setting, complementing ongoing Phase Ib study in patients whose disease has progressed following prior therapy / Colorectal cancer remains an area of significant unmet medical need, and approximately 15 percent of tumors are MSI-high, representing the largest population of patients with MSI-high disease 1  
 
San Diego, CA, USA, and Berlin, Germany, October 15, 2026 – Vividion Therapeutics , Inc. (Vividion), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company and a wholly owned and independently operated subsidiary of Bayer AG, today announced that the first patient has been dosed in a Phase II clinical trial of VVD-214, an investigational oral inhibitor of Werner helicase (WRN). The randomized study will evaluate VVD-214 in combination with pembrolizumab versus pembrolizumab alone as first-line treatment for patients with advanced microsatellite instability-high (MSI-high) or deficient mismatch repair (dMMR) colorectal cancer. Colorectal cancer remains an area of significant medical need, and approximately 15 percent of tumors are MSI-high, representing the largest population of patients with MSI-high disease. 
The Phase II trial expands clinical development of VVD-214 to investigate its potential applicability in earlier treatment lines for advanced colorectal cancer. Vividion’s recently initiated Phase Ib clinical trial ( NCT06004245 ) is additionally evaluating VVD-214 in combination with bevacizumab in patients with MSI-high or dMMR colorectal cancer whose disease has progressed following prior lines of therapy. 
“The progress of VVD-214 has strengthened our conviction in WRN inhibition and created an opportunity to broaden the program in front-line colorectal cancer, where effective and better tolerated treatment options are needed,” said Aleksandra Rizo, M.D., Ph.D., President and Chief Executive Officer of Vividion. “Supported by encouraging early clinical data and strong investigator interest, we are moving rapidly into Phase II to evaluate VVD-214 in the first-line setting and explore its potential to improve outcomes for more patients.” 
VVD-214 is an investigational oral small-molecule inhibitor of WRN, a DNA repair enzyme and synthetic lethal target for MSI-high or dMMR cancers. By inhibiting WRN, VVD-214 is designed to selectively induce lethal DNA damage in cancer cells while minimizing harm to normal cells. Preliminary data from the Phase Ia study presented at the American Association for Cancer Research (AACR) 2025 Annual Meeting and published in Nature Medicine showed that VVD-214 was well tolerated with early signals of activity. 2 
“The encouraging clinical evidence generated to date gives us confidence to broaden the program into the first-line setting and evaluate VVD-214 as a meaningful new treatment option for patients with MSI-high or dMMR colorectal cancer,” said Christian Rommel, Ph.D., Global Head of Research and Development at Bayer’s Pharmaceuticals Division. 
The global Phase II trial of VVD-214 ( NCT07811193 ) is planned to enroll approximately 140 patients at clinical sites across approximately 21 countries in North America, Latin America, Europe and Asia. The primary endpoint is six-month progression-free survival rate, with secondary endpoints including objective response rate, disease control rate, duration of response, overall survival and safety. 
Vividion also has ongoing Phase I trials evaluating an oral KEAP1 activator in advanced solid tumors and a RAS-PI3Kα inhibitor designed to target RAS-driven cancers. The company is advancing multiple innovative drug discovery programs toward the clinic, with a growing early discovery pipeline, emerging from its chemoproteomics platform, that spans oncology and immunology. 
References: 
1 Vilar E, Gruber SB. Microsatellite instability in colorectal cancer-the stable evidence. Nat Rev Clin Oncol. 2010;7(3):153-62. 
2 Yap TA, Fontana E, Cook N, et al. Werner helicase inhibitor for advanced microsatellite instability solid tumors: a phase 1 trial. Nat Med. Published online September 29, 2026. doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04657-3. 
About Vividion 
Vividion Therapeutics, Inc., a wholly owned and independently operated subsidiary of Bayer AG, is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company utilizing novel discovery technologies to unlock difficult-to-drug targets with strong disease-links, and to develop small molecule precision therapeutics for devastating cancers and immune disorders. The company’s platform has enabled it to identify hundreds of previously unknown functional pockets on well-validated protein targets implicated in a wide range of diseases, while simultaneously identifying compounds from its proprietary covalent chemistry library that interact in a highly selective manner with those pockets. The company is leveraging its proprietary chemoproteomic platform to advance a diversified pipeline of highly selective small molecule therapeutics targeting high-value, traditionally undruggable targets in oncology and immunology. title: Bayer Foundation honors five outstanding scientists with the Science Awards 2026
content_text:
Bayer Foundation honors five outstanding scientists with the Science Awards 2026
Summary
Otto Bayer Award goes to plant researcher Sarah O’Connor / Early Excellence in Science Awards recognize outstanding early-career research in biology, chemistry, medical science and plant science / Plant Science award presented for the first time
Leverkusen, October 14, 2026 – In 2026, Bayer Foundation honors five outstanding scientists whose research opens up new perspectives and areas for action in health, agriculture and biomedical innovation. The prestigious Otto Bayer Award goes to Sarah O’Connor. The Early Excellence in Science Awards are presented to Colinda Scheele (Biology), James Eills (Chemistry), Antonia Morita Saktiawati (Medical Science) and Bruno Pok Man Ngou (Plant Science). 
Otto Bayer Award 2026: Sarah O’Connor 
Bayer Foundation presents the 2026 Otto Bayer Award to Sarah O’Connor, Director at the Max Planck Institute for Chemical Ecology in Jena. She is recognized for her pioneering research into the biosynthesis of natural plant compounds. Her work deciphers how plants produce complex molecules that can be used, among other applications, as medicines against cancer and other diseases. 
Through her research, O’Connor has uncovered numerous previously unknown biochemical processes that lead to the formation of valuable natural products, including medically important alkaloids such as vinblastine, quinine and ibogaine. These compounds are used, for example, in the treatment of cancer (vinblastine) or malaria (quinine), or are in clinical trials for treatment of mental health and substance use disorders (ibogaine). Her work lays the foundation for producing important active ingredients more sustainably and efficiently in the future, while opening up new opportunities for drug discovery and development. 
The Otto Bayer Award is one of Bayer Foundation’s most prestigious science awards and among the most highly endowed research prizes in Germany. Presented every two years in alternation with the Hansen Family Award, it recognizes leading scientists working in German-speaking countries for groundbreaking research contributions in chemistry or biochemistry. The award, endowed with EUR 75,000, was established in 1984 through a generous provision in the will of Otto Bayer, a former Director of Research at Bayer AG. 
With the Early Excellence in Science Awards, the Foundation has recognized emerging talents for remarkable research contributions in the natural sciences since 2009. To date, 51 talents have received the awards. Each Early Excellence in Science Award includes prize money of EUR 10,000 for the researcher. 
Early Excellence in Science Award in Biology: Colinda Scheele 
The Early Excellence in Science Award in Biology goes to Colinda Scheele from the VIB–KU Leuven in Belgium. She investigates how cancer develops and why some altered cells form tumors while others are stopped by the surrounding tissue. 
Her research has shown that even breast tissue that appears healthy from the outside can already contain genetic changes that precede cancer. At the same time, she has identified protective mechanisms in the tissue that prevent tumor formation. These insights open up new possibilities for detecting breast cancer earlier, improving prevention and further advancing therapies. 
Early Excellence in Science Award in Chemistry: James Eills 
The Early Excellence in Science Award in Chemistry is presented to James Eills from Forschungszentrum Jülich. His research improves methods in magnetic resonance spectroscopy and imaging that are used to visualize biological processes. 
Together with his research team, he develops new hyperpolarization methods that significantly increase the sensitivity of these measurement techniques. In the future, this could make it possible to visualize metabolic processes in the body faster, more cost-effectively and without radioactive markers. This opens promising perspectives for cancer diagnostics and other medical applications. 
Early Excellence in Science Award in Medical Science: Antonia Morita Saktiawati 
In the Medical Science category, Antonia Morita Saktiawati from the Center for Tropical Medicine at Universitas Gadjah Mada in Indonesia is recognized. She develops AI-supported diagnostic tools that can detect infectious diseases such as tuberculosis at an early stage and can be deployed in remote areas, making diagnosis possible even in regions with limited medical infrastructure. 
Her research developments include an AI-based system for interpreting chest X-rays (TBScreen.AI) as well as an artificial nose system, also known as an electronic nose or e-Nose, that can detect diseases based on breath samples. Her research helps make life-saving diagnostics faster, more affordable and accessible to significantly more people. 
Early Excellence in Science Award in Plant Science: Bruno Pok Man Ngou 
The award in Plant Science is new and will be presented for the first time in 2026 to Bruno Pok Man Ngou from the RIKEN Center for Sustainable Resource Science (CSRS) in Japan. His research explores how plants recognize pathogens and defend themselves against them. 
Pok Man Ngou has uncovered fundamental mechanisms of the plant immune system and identified new classes of immune receptors. Building on these insights, he is developing new approaches to equip plants with enhanced defense mechanisms. His findings could help to breed crops that are more resistant to disease and to improve harvest yields in the future. 
Science with societal impact 
With its Science Awards, Bayer Foundation recognizes outstanding research that pushes scientific boundaries while holding the potential to address concrete societal challenges in health, agriculture and the environment. This year’s awardees exemplify a new generation of scientists whose insights are helping advance health, food security and sustainable innovation. 
About Bayer Foundation 
Bayer Foundation is the corporate foundation of Bayer, dedicated to advancing Science and Social Innovation for a world with Health for All and Hunger for None . Guided by the claim “Innovation that matters,” the Foundation supports transformative innovations in health and agriculture to address systemic challenges, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. 
Since 2007, Bayer Foundation’s science programs have reached more than 1,000 early-career scientists with fellowships across 40 countries. Bayer Foundation’s prestigious awards have recognized more than 80 outstanding scientists, of whom five later became Nobel Laureates. In Germany, Bayer Foundation is also driving the support of STEM education and has funded more than 700 STEM school projects with more than EUR 6 million. 
For more information, please visit the Bayer Foundation website .

content_text:
10/01/2026 Martina Gartner Reinforces Schmalz's Executive Management Team
Effective October 1, 2026, Martina Gartner will join the Managing Director team at Schmalz. With her many years of experience in corporate management, controlling, and organizational development, she will help shape the strategic growth of this globally active industrial company in the commercial sector.
Martina Gartner, Schmalz's new Managing Director.
“I look forward to actively shaping the future of Schmalz together with the employees and driving the group’s continued development,” says Martina Gartner, who joined Schmalz’s management team today and is reinforcing the role of Managing Director. “Schmalz stands for innovative strength, long-term thinking, and a unique corporate culture. It is precisely these values and the trusting nature of our collaboration that inspire me.”
I'm inspired by the company culture and the trusting way we work together. ∼ Martina Gartner 
Together with Dr. Kurt Schmalz, Dr. Johannes Schmalz, and Andreas Beutel, Martina Gartner will now steer Schmalz’s course as a member of the executive board. “With Martina Gartner, we are gaining an experienced colleague for our executive management team,” said Dr. Kurt Schmalz, Managing Shareholder. “As our global corporate group becomes increasingly international, the commercial side of the business is growing more complex. By creating a fourth position for a Managing Director, we are responding to this development.”
The Schmalz managing directors (from left): Dr. Kurt Schmalz, Dr. Johannes Schmalz, Martina Gartner, and Andreas Beutel.

title: maxon acquires strategic minority stake in Synapticon
content_text:
maxon acquires strategic minority stake in Synapticon
The Synapticon Headquarter in Schönaich near Stuttgart, Germany
Download 
Contact us 
Share current page 
The Swiss maxon Group is expanding its expertise in the field of motion control through a strategic partnership with the German company Synapticon. The goal of the collaboration is the joint development of high-performance drive solutions with integrated functional safety, based on optimally combined components from both companies. 
As part of this partnership, the maxon Group has acquired a minority stake in Synapticon. The company, based in Baden-Württemberg, Germany, is a leading provider of intelligent motion control solutions with integrated, certified safety functions. Together, the partners are building a comprehensive portfolio of mechatronic drive systems, which already includes market-ready solutions.
Synapticon follows a "software-first" approach and develops pioneering software and hardware for drive control in robotics and mechanical engineering. The company offers one of the world’s leading portfolios of highly compact, powerful, and intelligent motion control technologies. Its products are used in robotic arms, autonomous transport systems, and complex industrial machinery, among others.
Customers are already benefiting from intelligent, highly integrated solutions based on technologies from maxon and Synapticon. The close collaboration enables efficient further development of existing products and targeted alignment with new applications.
Considering increasing functional safety requirements in many high-tech industries, this investment represents an important strategic step for maxon. The partnership strengthens maxon's position as a provider of future-proof drive systems in dynamically growing markets such as robotics, medical technology, intralogistics, and industrial automation.
Nikolai Ensslen, CEO of Synapticon, states: “This partnership with maxon is of great strategic importance for Synapticon. Together, we will push the boundaries of motion control even further. The market opportunities arising from this collaboration are tremendous.”
Dr. Stefan Müller, CTO of the maxon Group, adds: “Our collaboration with Synapticon opens new possibilities for expanding our expertise in highly integrated drive systems. It enables us to offer even more powerful and safer solutions to our customers.”
The companies have agreed not to disclose the financial terms of the investment.

title: maxon at the SPS 2025: New drive solutions for robotics, automation and mobility
content_text:
maxon at the SPS 2025: New drive solutions for robotics, automation and mobility
Strain wave gearhead
Download 
Contact us 
Share current page 
At the SPS trade fair from November 25 to 27, 2025, maxon will present a wide range of new products. From highly integrated robotic actuators to powerful servo drives and controllers: a diverse technology portfolio awaits visitors at the maxon booth in Hall 3, Stand 468.
One focus at the maxon booth will be the further developed robotics solutions, in particular the High Efficiency Joints (HEJ). These compact, highly integrated quasi-direct drive (QDD) actuators combine motor, gearhead, sensors, and electronics in a single, robust housing. Following the successful launch of the HEJ 90 (140 Nm), the HEJ 70 with 62 Nm torque now follows - ideal for smaller robots. The HEJ 50 variant is also currently in production and will be available from early 2026. The powerful HEJ "Hercules" with over 250 Nm is under development.
With this scalable platform, maxon consistently pursues the goal of shortening development times and reducing the overall costs for modern robotics.
Additions to the maxon portfolio
At SPS, maxon will present several additions to its product portfolio: 
IDX 70 - Compact high-performance servo drive with safety certification 
The new IDX 70 combines high power density with a compact footprint, making it ideal for mobile robotics, cobots, and driverless transport systems (AGVs). The IDX 70 offers an excellent torque-to-weight ratio and is suitable for demanding industrial environments thanks to its robust design. The certified Safe Torque Off function (STO) and Safe Brake Control (SBC) ensure compliance with the highest safety standards.
EC frameless DT 50 - Flexible, dynamic, efficient 
The new EC frameless DT 50 is a brushless motor without a flange and now also available with integrated Hall sensors. The design allows for optimal installation versatility, whether in articulated joints, machine tools, or exoskeletons. With high torque density and outstanding efficiency, it enables precise, dynamic motion with minimal heat generation. Additional sizes — 38 mm, 65 mm, and 85 mm — will be available next year.
Strain wave gearheads - precision in the smallest space 
With the new Strain wave gearheads, maxon expands its portfolio, especially for applications with high demands on precision in torque transmission. The backlash-free design ensures exact motion control in minimal installation space – ideal for robotic arms, surgical instruments, or optical applications. In combination with maxon drives, this results in a perfectly matched drive system from a single source - currently available in diameters of 55mm and 62mm. Additional sizes and variants are planned and will be presented at SPS. 
EPOS4 Module/Compact 60/20 STO - Compact controllers with integrated safety 
The new positioning controllers, with certified STO function up to SIL 3 / PL e category 3, combine advanced control performance and safety in a compact form. They enable precise motion control in modular machines, collaborative robots, or autonomous vehicles. Thanks to versatile interfaces, they can be seamlessly integrated into existing automation systems.
MiniMACS6 AMP 4IF1 Profinet - multi-axis controller for networked systems 
The MiniMACS6 AMP 4-IF1 Profinet adds a Profinet communication interface to the successful MACS family. This positions the controller as a key link between motion control and industrial networking. In production environments and robotic systems, it ensures precise real-time coordination of multiple axes and processes.
BIKEDRIVE AIR S e-bike drive: efficiency meets driving experience 
In addition to industrial applications, maxon will also be showcasing its latest innovation in the field of lightweight electromobility: the BIKEDRIVE AIR S –the lightest full-power e-bike drive in its class. With a drive weight of just 2 kg, 90 Nm torque, and whisper-quiet operation, the system sets new standards for a sporty yet natural riding experience.

At Hannover Messe 2026, maxon will present itself with an updated trade fair appearance. From April 20 to 24, the maxon Germany team will showcase the latest highlights from our product portfolio.
At Hannover Messe, maxon traditionally introduces its latest portfolio additions. Here is what visitors can expect at our booth:
Robotics solutions: maxon’s High Efficiency Joints (HEJ) bring motion to robotics. They enable humanoid robots to operate in unstructured environments and are also suitable for industrial applications. At Hannover Messe, we will present the proven High Efficiency Joint 90, as well as the new, smaller HEJ 70.
Drives: In our highlight showcases, we present a wide range of maxon drives combined with gearheads and sensors. Among them is the EC frameless DT 50 M: easy to integrate into customer applications thanks to its separate stator and rotor design, offering high efficiency and dynamic torque. Another example is the ECX PRIME 16L - the long version of our brushless motor with ironless winding. These are just two of many new additions.
EC frameless DT50M 
1 / 6 
Gearheads: Since launching our new GSW strain wave gear series, we have continuously developed it further. Our gearheads transmit high torques precisely and efficiently and can be combined with a wide range of maxon drives. In Hannover, we will, for example, present the GSW 20 in combination with an ECX PRIME drive.
Industrial drives: Our IDX series meets industrial standards and is a proven plug-and-play solution - for industrial applications or autonomous vehicles in intralogistics. At Hannover Messe, we will present the IDX 70 Safe Control, featuring integrated functional safety up to SIL3 / PL e, Cat. 3.
Precision, performance and integrated safety
Electronics: Functional safety is also becoming increasingly important in this field, which is why maxon continues to develop its control solutions accordingly. One example is the EPOS4 Compact 60/20 STO (Safe Torque Off). Visitors can also see the smallest controllers in the maxon portfolio: ESCON2 Nano 24/2 and ESCON2 Micro 60/5. We will also present the MiniMACS6, our freely programmable multi-axis controller, now also available with a PROFINET interface. In addition, we will demonstrate our predictive maintenance solution, maxon MIND, and explain why the motor is the best sensor in a customer application.
Parvalux: The UK-based company Parvalux, part of maxon, specializes in small and medium-sized geared motors. Parvalux solutions drive windshield wipers in high-speed trains or move patients in hospitals. At Hannover Messe, we will show how maxon and Parvalux products can be ideally combined, for example, the maxon IDX industrial drive with the Parvalux GB 28 right-angle gearbox.
At our booth, we will also present various live demos showcasing our drive solutions in action. The maxon Germany team will be available for any questions.
You can find us at Hannover Messe in Hall 13, Booth C51.

The completely revised maxon catalog 2026/2027 has been released

In addition, the areas of Robotics, Space, and Electronics are presented separately within the Market Solutions. This demonstrates maxon’s broad market competence and enables targeted browsing while maintaining a clear overview of the core markets. The section “Technology – short and to the point” has also been completely revised.
The stars of the new catalog, of course, remain the products. The portfolio has been expanded with several highlights, including the brushless ECX PRIME 4-pole motors for high speeds and torque, the powerful ECX FLAT flat motors with fan, new diameters of the EC frameless high‑torque motors, and the backlash-free GSW planetary gearheads. title: Investment in LOMBY Inc., through Nabtesco Technology Ventures Sep 30, 2026 Business Investment and Alliance
content_text:
Investment in LOMBY Inc., through Nabtesco Technology Ventures
Sep 30, 2026 
Business 
Investment and Alliance 
Nabtesco Corporation (Head Office: Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo; President & CEO: Kazumasa Kimura) is pleased to announce that Nabtesco Technology Ventures L.P. (Managing Partner: Hiroshi Nerima), the corporate venture capital fund established by Nabtesco, has invested in LOMBY Inc. (LOMBY), a Tokyo-based robotics company developing, manufacturing and operating autonomous mobility robots.
LOMBY is a startup company that develops outdoor autonomous mobility solutions combining robotics and AI. Its flagship product, the LM-A autonomous delivery robot, is an autonomous mobility robot that travels on sidewalks and similar areas under a remote-monitoring framework, having completed the required notification as a "remote-controlled compact vehicle" under the Road Traffic Act, thereby contributing to labor savings and greater efficiency in delivery operations. Commercial operation has already commenced in certain areas, and in the future the company also envisions expanding beyond the delivery field into services that support the mobility of people.
In the logistics industry, addressing labor shortages and improving delivery efficiency have become critical challenges, and expectations for autonomous delivery technology are rising. To date, Nabtesco has supplied wireless charging systems manufactured by WiBotic Inc. of the United States, which the Company distributes, for LOMBY's delivery robots. This investment builds on that existing business relationship and is intended to support LOMBY's business expansion.
Through this investment, Nabtesco will further build its knowledge of the autonomous delivery robot market and related infrastructure, while exploring the creation of new business opportunities and synergies through collaboration with LOMBY.
Going forward, Nabtesco will continue to deepen its collaboration with promising startup companies through open innovation activities, pursuing new business opportunities and working to enhance its corporate value.

title: Hydro signs strategic partnership with CHANEL Fragrance and Beauty to accelerate the development of low-carbon aluminium Hydro and CHANEL Fragrance and Beauty have signed a strategic partnership to accelerate the development of low-carbon aluminium for the beauty and fra ... September 28, 2026
content_text:
Hydro signs strategic partnership with CHANEL Fragrance and Beauty to accelerate the development of low-carbon aluminium
Hydro and CHANEL Fragrance and Beauty have signed a strategic partnership to accelerate the development of low-carbon aluminium for the beauty and fragrance industry. The agreement sets out a shared roadmap between 2026 and 2030 to develop low-carbon aluminium for fragrance, makeup, and skincare packaging.
As global demand for aluminium continues to grow and the material takes on increasing strategic importance, the cosmetics sector is emerging as a powerful driver of innovation in responsible sourcing. Although it accounts for only a limited share of global aluminium volumes, the luxury beauty sector sets high standards for quality, design, and traceability, standards that will help raise the bar across the entire value chain and encourage innovation.
Under the agreement, the partners will work together to develop aluminium packaging solutions whose carbon footprint will approach 3.0 kilograms of CO₂ equivalent per kilogram of aluminium by 2030, while meeting the highest requirements for quality, performance and design.
The partners will also jointly explore various ways of reducing emissions, including the development and testing of aluminium produced in specific batches, enhanced traceability and the use of aluminium recovered from end-of-life products. 
Advancing low-carbon aluminium for packaging
Produced in Norway using renewable energy, this low-carbon aluminium is certified with a carbon footprint of no more than 4.0 kilograms of CO₂ equivalent per kilogram of aluminium, less than one third of the global average. The work will initially be based on Hydro REDUXA primary aluminium sheet ingot , which will subsequently be rolled into aluminium sheet used for packaging. Hydro and CHANEL Fragrance and Beauty will work to further reduce this footprint, while preserving the quality, creativity, and excellence expected in fragrance and beauty packaging.
“Our most ambitious customers often drive innovation by setting clear and demanding goals. By combining Hydro’s broad product portfolio, quality, and service with our low-carbon and circular aluminium solutions, we can develop materials with a lower carbon footprint for fragrance and beauty packaging,” says Hanne Simensen, Executive Vice President of Hydro Aluminium Metal.
Julien Garry, Chief Operations Officer, CHANEL Fragrance and Beauty, Hanne Simensen, Executive Vice President of Hydro Aluminium Metal. Photo: ©MarieBrunel 
Strengthening traceability and the use of recycled aluminium
The partners will study the possibility of incorporating more recycled aluminium, as part of a more circular approach.
“Aluminium is a strategic material, and making its production and processing more responsible requires action across the value chain. At CHANEL Fragrance and Beauty, we believe that creating exceptional products and sustainability must go hand in hand. This partnership reflects our conviction that lasting progress depends on working with partners who share the same long-term ambition. Together, we can go further in developing materials that make our products both more sustainable and desirable,” says Julien Garry, Chief Operations Officer, CHANEL Fragrance and Beauty.

Announcement Regarding Establishment of Sponsored ADR
(American Depositary Receipt) Program
Tokyo Electron Limited (TEL) hereby announces that it has established a sponsored Level I American
Depositary Receipt (“ADR”) program in the United States, with JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. acting as the
depositary bank. Trading of TEL’s ADRs is expected to commence in the United States on September 17,
2026 (U.S. Eastern Time). This sponsored ADR program will not involve any capital raising through a U.S.
listing, issuance of new shares, or any other financing activities. Consequently, the total number of
outstanding shares of TEL will not increase, and there will be no dilution of shareholder value.
1. Purpose of Establishing this Sponsored ADR Program
This sponsored ADR program is intended to broaden TEL’s investor base and attract new investors by
providing U.S. investors with greater access to TEL shares and expanding the range of investment
options available in the U.S. capital markets. TEL also expects the program to enhance its visibility and
market presence in the United States, thereby strengthening engagement with the global investment
community.

American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) are negotiable securities issued by a U.S. depositary bank

representing ownership interests in the underlying shares of a non-U.S. company. ADRs enable
investors to trade, settle, and hold shares of non-U.S. companies in the same manner as U.S.
securities within the United States.
2. About Sponsored ADRs
Sponsored ADRs are issued by a designated depositary bank pursuant to a deposit agreement with
the issuer of the underlying shares. Such agreements define the rights and obligations of the issuer,
the depositary bank, and ADR holders. Sponsored ADR programs are generally classified into three
categories: Level I, Level II, and Level III, depending on whether they are listed and/or involve a
public offering. The level of disclosure required by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
(SEC) varies accordingly.
⚫ Level I ADR programs are unlisted programs traded in the over-the-counter market.
⚫ Level II ADR programs are listed on a U.S. securities exchange such as the New York Stock
Exchange.
⚫ Level III ADR programs are listed programs involving capital raising through the issuance of
new shares.
3. Transition from Unsponsored ADRs
TEL’s ADRs that have previously traded in the U.S. securities markets as unsponsored ADRs
without TEL’s involvement are expected to transition to the sponsored ADR program established
by TEL.
This announcement is not intended as an offer to sell or a solicitation of an offer to purchase securities.

title: (Marine Vessel Equipment) Onboard Validation Begins for Autonomous Control System Integrated with an Optimal Navigation Application for Domestic Coastal Vessels Sep 16, 2026 Business Marine Vessel Equipment
content_text:
(Marine Vessel Equipment) Onboard Validation Begins for Autonomous Control System Integrated with an Optimal Navigation Application for Domestic Coastal Vessels
Sep 16, 2026 
Business 
Marine Vessel Equipment 
The Marine Control Systems Company of Nabtesco Corporation (Head Office: Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo; President: Kazumasa Kimura) has completed the development phase of the “Development of an Autonomous Control System Integrated with an Optimal Navigation Application for Domestic Coastal Vessels,” which was selected for the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism’s FY2025 Support Program for Technology Development to Promote Transformation of Domestic Coastal Shipping, and has now moved into the onboard validation phase.
This technology development project is being carried out to address challenges facing the domestic coastal shipping industry, including the shortage of crew, while maintaining and improving navigational safety. Through onboard validation, we will verify the effectiveness, safety, and operability of the system and continue our efforts toward commercialization in 2027.
In this project, Nabtesco has developed an optimal navigation application that performs weather routing (*) and calculates optimal vessel speed, together with an autonomous control system that supports vessel operations. By enabling the system to provide optimal operating conditions and support control of engine output commands, which have traditionally been determined by onboard personnel as part of voyage planning, the project aims to reduce crew workload while supporting safe vessel operation.
This system is designed as a support system and is not intended to replace the judgment or ship-handling of crew. It is operated under the supervision and final decision-making authority of onboard personnel. The system is designed to allow crew intervention and manual operation whenever necessary and is not intended for fully autonomous navigation.
( * ) Weather routing is a technique that predicts meteorological and oceanographic conditions encountered during a voyage and determines the optimal route by taking into account vessel performance and estimated arrival time.
The onboard validation of this system will be conducted on the domestic roll-on/roll-off vessel Haru Maru No. 5, operated by Daio Kaiun Co., Ltd. Misuga Kaiun Co., Ltd. is participating as a technical advisor on vessel operation and management. The verification will be carried out by utilizing practical knowledge gained from actual vessel operations, while implementing sufficient safety measures in cooperation with all parties involved and giving the highest priority to navigational safety.
Domestic roll-on/roll-off vessel “Haru Maru No.5”
Development image of autonomous control system
Image of weather routing application
Nabtesco will continue to work closely with Daio Kaiun, Misuga Kaiun, and other related parties to advance the demonstration program with safety as its highest priority. By further developing this technology as a safe navigation support technology that complements the knowledge and judgment of crew, we aim to contribute to the sustainable development and enhanced safety of the domestic coastal shipping industry.

title: First-Generation Precision Reduction Gear RV Registered as a “Future Technology Heritage” by National Museum of Nature and Science, Tokyo Sep 15, 2026 Business Precision Reduction Gears
content_text:
First-Generation Precision Reduction Gear RV Registered as a “Future Technology Heritage” by National Museum of Nature and Science, Tokyo
Sep 15, 2026 
Business 
Precision Reduction Gears 
Nabtesco Corporation (Head Office: Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo; President & CEO: Kazumasa Kimura; hereinafter “Nabtesco”) is pleased to announce that its Precision Reduction Gear RV TM Series RV-135 has been registered in the 2026 Essential Historical Materials for Science and Technology (commonly known as “Future Technology Heritage”), a designation awarded by the National Museum of Nature and Science, Tokyo.
The Precision Reduction Gear RV TM Series RV-135 was the first model in our Precision Reduction Gear RV TM Series for industrial robots, developed in 1985. Based on technologies cultivated through the development of reduction gears for construction machinery, the product features a unique design that integrates a cycloidal mechanism with a planetary gear mechanism. This innovative structure enabled the low vibration, high reduction ratio, compact size, light weight, superior durability against shock loads, high rigidity, and high precision required for industrial robots.
As a result, the RV-135 made a significantly enhanced performance of industrial robots at the time. In recognition of its technological innovation and historical significance, resulting in its registration in the Essential Historical Materials for Science and Technology.
Precision Reduction Gear RV TM Series RV-135
■About the registration system for Essential Historical Materials for Science and Technology 
Based on studies and research conducted by the National Museum of Nature and Science, Tokyo, this system identifies and registers scientific and technological heritage materials that either:
・Significant contribution in the development of science and technology and constitute an important heritage to the next generations; or
・Remarkable impact to people’s lives, the economy, society, and culture. These materials will be registered into the “Registry of the Essential Historical Materials for Science and Technology”. This system will promote the accumulation of materials that are important in the development of science and technology in Japan.
End

title: Hydro joins Siemens Mobility led project to recycle aluminium from end-of-life trains Working alongside Siemens Mobility, TSR Group and Voestalpine, Hydro will recycle aluminium recovered from decommissioned trains to produce new rail c ... September 11, 2026
content_text:
Hydro joins Siemens Mobility led project to recycle aluminium from end-of-life trains
Working alongside Siemens Mobility, TSR Group and Voestalpine, Hydro will recycle aluminium recovered from decommissioned trains to produce new rail components. The Train2Train project demonstrates how collaboration and a focus on traceability can keep aluminium in use across the rail sector.
In this pilot study, Hydro will recycle aluminium from decommissioned trains at its recycling facility in Ghlin, Belgium . The aluminium comes from TSR Group , which has dismantled the rail vehicles and retrieved the materials with the aim of recycling them into new rail parts. TSR will also retrieve the steel material from the rail vehicle and ship this to Voestalpine for recycling and further production.
Upon melting, the aluminium will be processed into extrusion billets, which in turn will be used as input material at Hydro’s extrusion facility in Lichtervelde, Belgium . 
Accelerating circularity in the rail industry
The Train2Train project is a demonstration of Hydro’s commitment to low-carbon aluminium and circular economy, showing how collaboration across the value chain can keep valuable materials in circulation.
" Aluminium can be recycled repeatedly without losing its properties. By combining recycling expertise, digital traceability and manufacturing capabilities, we can create new opportunities for circular solutions in the rail industry. This project builds on Hydro’s ambition to accelerate the transition towards a more circular and low-carbon aluminium industry,” says Piotr Chmielewski, Vice President Automotive, Rail and Automation, Hydro Extrusions Europe.
Hydro and the rail industry
Hydro supplies a variety of aluminium solutions for the rail industry, supporting manufacturers with lightweight, durable, and recyclable materials for applications including train structures, interiors, and components. 
With expertise across aluminium extrusion, recycling, and low-carbon aluminium production, Hydro works with customers throughout the value chain to develop solutions that improve modern trains and help manufacturers meet challenging sustainability ambitions.
About the project
The Train2Train project aims to demonstrate that the materials from a decommissioned train can be recovered, recycled and reborn into a brand new one. At a time when global supply chains are under increasing pressure, gaining greater control over material flows is becoming increasingly important. The project brings together the full value chain, from dismantling and recycling to material processing and manufacturing, with each partner playing a critical role in creating a transparent and circular material loop.

title: PI Advanced Materials receives industry award for world-first 4µm polyimide film technology
source: Arkema - High Performance Polymers News / Newsroom / News
content_text:
Products 
Innovation 
Sep 10, 2026 - NEWS 
PI Advanced Materials receives industry award for world-first 4µm polyimide film technology
PI Advanced Materials, an Arkema Affiliate, has received the 2026 KPCA Industry award for contributions to the world’s first mass-production for 4µm ultra-thin polyimide film using an unstretched process. The 4µm polyimide film achieved comparable mechanical, thermal and adhesion performance at approximately one-third the thickness of conventional 12.5µm polyimide film.
Sanghak Lee, Gumi Production Team Leader at PI Advanced Materials, received the “2026 KPCA Proud PCB & Semiconductor Packaging Industry Award” in recognition of his contribution to the development of the world’s first mass-production technology for 4㎛ ultra-thin polyimide (PI) film using an unstretched process.
The award ceremony was held on September 9 at Gyeongwonjae, Incheon. The award recognizes PI Advanced Materials’ world-class technological capabilities in ultra-thin polyimide film and its contribution to the advancement of the materials industry.
Drawing on PI Advanced Materials’ extensive expertise in polymerization, film casting, and winding technologies, Sanghak Lee played a key role in establishing the core technologies required for the mass production of ultra-thin PI film. In particular, he led the optimization of the T-DIE-based film casting process and the development of precise process control technologies, overcoming key technical challenges and enabling the successful commercialization of the world’s first 4㎛ ultra-thin PI film produced through an unstretched process in 2024.
PI Advanced Materials ’ 4㎛ ultra-thin PI film is approximately one-third the thickness of the 12.5㎛ PI film widely used in the industry, while maintaining comparable mechanical and thermal properties as well as adhesion performance. The film also offers excellent thickness uniformity and low, consistent loop stiffness, enhancing processability and expanding its potential for a wide range of applications.
The technology can support increasingly demanding requirements for lighter, thinner, and higher-performance products across a range of advanced industries, including flexible printed circuit boards (FPCBs), displays, semiconductor packaging, and electric vehicle batteries.
Building on its successful mass production of 5㎛ PI film, PI Advanced Materials has further demonstrated its world-class technological capabilities in ultra-thin polyimide film through the production of the world’s first 4㎛ product.
PI Advanced Materials will continue to support customers in developing high-value-added products through differentiated material technologies and continuous R&D, while further strengthening its competitiveness in the global advanced materials market.

content_text:
Tokyo Electron Issues Information Security Report 2026
Tokyo Electron (TEL; Head Office: Minato-ku, Tokyo; President: Toshiki Kawai) considers information security a material issue requiring focused and prioritized responses. Accordingly, TEL has issued the Information Security Report 2026, which systematically outlines the relevant activities of the TEL Group. In light of the ever-changing business environment and technological trends, the TEL Group is implementing various information security initiatives to both ensure business continuity and increase corporate value, as detailed in the report.
The report covers the following main topics:
(1) The governance and risk management structures related to information security and cybersecurity, as well as how they are coordinated with TEL's management strategies.
(2) Measures to strengthen the TEL Group's global business security, including protection against cyberattacks and physical security risks, as well as securing manufacturing plants and products.
(3) External security engagements and human resource development programs that aim to improve the information security level of the semiconductor industry and society as a whole.
To learn more, please visit:
https://www.tel.com/sustainability/management-foundation/security/#report
