GaN Power Semiconductor Market Trends 
Rising migration of GaN adoption from consumer chargers into higher-power EV, data center, and industrial applications.
Growing shift toward 200mm and larger GaN-on-silicon wafer production improving unit economics and manufacturing scale.
Expanding use of integrated GaN power ICs combining switching, driver, and protection functions on a single chip.
Increasing GaN deployment in 800V HVDC data center power architectures supporting AI computing infrastructure.
Rising vertical integration and strategic partnerships between GaN specialists and established semiconductor foundries.
Growing adoption of higher-voltage GaN devices as automakers transition toward 800V electric vehicle platforms.
U.S. GaN Power Semiconductor Market Size Outlook 
The U.S. GaN Power Semiconductor Market was valued at USD 0.12 Billion in 2025 and is expected to reach USD 1.09 Billion by 2035, growing at a CAGR of 24.60% from 2026-2035.
The United States sits at the center of GaN innovation largely because so many of the companies pushing the technology forward, Navitas, EPC, Power Integrations, Texas Instruments, are headquartered here, backed by a domestic semiconductor ecosystem that keeps churning out new device generations. That concentration of expertise matters, because GaN adoption isn't just about having a good chip, it's about convincing automakers, data center operators, and consumer electronics brands that the technology is reliable enough to design around for the long haul, and American suppliers have generally led that qualification push. Demand here is increasingly tied to two very different but equally hungry markets: electric vehicle charging infrastructure and the AI data center buildout, both of which need power conversion that's smaller, cooler, and more efficient than silicon alone can deliver.
In 2025, Navitas Semiconductor partnered with GlobalFoundries to develop and manufacture next-generation GaN technology in the U.S. for AI data centers, energy infrastructure, and industrial applications. 
GaN Power Semiconductor Market Segment Analysis 
By Device Type, the Discrete GaN Power Devices segment dominated the GaN Power Semiconductor Market with approximately 51.60% share in 2025, while the Integrated GaN Power ICs segment is the fastest growing with a CAGR of approximately 35.60%.
By Voltage Rating, the 100–650V segment dominated the GaN Power Semiconductor Market with approximately 58.60% share in 2025, while the Above 650V segment is the fastest growing with a CAGR of approximately 32.60%.
By Application, the Consumer Electronics segment dominated the GaN Power Semiconductor Market with approximately 42.60% share in 2025, while the Automotive segment is the fastest growing with a CAGR of approximately 33.60%.
By Device Type, Discrete GaN Power Devices Dominates the GaN Power Semiconductor Market and Integrated GaN Power ICs Grows Fastest 
Discrete GaN devices hold the largest share of this market mostly because they're the easiest entry point for engineers already comfortable with silicon-based designs. A discrete transistor lets designers swap into an existing converter topology without redesigning the whole system around it, which is a much smaller ask than committing to an entirely new integrated architecture. That flexible migration path has made discrete devices the default choice as companies first dip their toes into GaN before going all-in.
Integrated GaN power ICs are where the real excitement lies, though, growing considerably faster than the discrete category. By combining the switching transistor with its driver and protection circuitry on a single chip, these devices shrink board space, cut component count, and squeeze out extra efficiency in ways a discrete solution simply can't match. Companies including Navitas have built their entire competitive identity around this integration advantage, and as more applications prioritize compactness and reliability over familiar design patterns, integrated ICs are capturing an increasing share of new GaN designs.
By Voltage Rating, 100–650V Dominates the GaN Power Semiconductor Market and Above 650V Grows Fastest 
The 100 to 650V range currently does the heavy lifting for this market, and it's easy to see why: this band covers the sweet spot for consumer fast chargers, server power supplies, and a wide range of industrial motor drives, applications with enormous unit volumes and well-understood performance requirements. Devices in this voltage class have also had the longest time to mature, giving engineers a deep well of reference designs and proven reliability data to draw on.
Above 650V is where the market's growth energy is concentrated, though, largely on the back of the automotive industry's push toward 800V electric vehicle platforms. Higher-voltage architectures cut charging times and reduce resistive losses, but they demand power semiconductors capable of handling voltages that were, until recently, considered a stretch for GaN. As suppliers keep pushing the technology's voltage ceiling higher, this segment is positioned to keep growing faster than any other voltage category through the forecast period.
By Application, Consumer Electronics Dominates the GaN Power Semiconductor Market and Automotive Grows Fastest 
Consumer electronics remains GaN's biggest application by a comfortable margin, and that's really a legacy of where the technology first proved itself commercially. Fast chargers for phones and laptops were the first mainstream product category willing to pay a premium for GaN's size and efficiency advantages, and that early foothold has translated into sustained volume as more device categories, from gaming laptops to compact power banks, adopt the same compact charging technology.
Automotive is where things are moving fastest now, though, as electric vehicle adoption keeps climbing and automakers look for every possible efficiency gain in onboard chargers, DC-DC converters, and increasingly the main traction inverter itself. GaN's ability to switch faster and run cooler than silicon translates directly into smaller components and better energy efficiency, both of which matter enormously to automakers chasing every extra mile of EV range, making automotive the application category to watch as this market scales.

Asia Pacific dominated the GaN Power Semiconductor Market with approximately 45% of the global market share in 2025 and is projected to remain the largest and fastest-growing region, expanding at around 27% CAGR during 2026–2035. China's electronics manufacturing base runs deep, and the country also plays an outsized role in gallium supply itself, giving it a genuinely substantial GaN ecosystem, though that same material concentration creates real procurement risk for overseas buyers who depend on Chinese supply.
Japan and South Korea contribute their own strengths through advanced electronics manufacturing, sophisticated packaging capability, and high-reliability application demand from sectors like automotive and industrial equipment. India’s emerging Semiconductor Mission is also beginning to incorporate a longer-term outlook as well, seeking to develop local manufacturing capabilities that may one day enable it to become a more significant player in downstream GaN integration. Taken together, however, this combination of manufacturing prowess, access to materials, and developing capabilities will ensure that Asia Pacific remains ahead through 2035.

North America GaN Power Semiconductor Market Insights 
North America holds a substantial share of this market, anchored by the United States' concentration of GaN technology leaders and a mature automotive and renewable energy sector eager to adopt the efficiency gains GaN offers. A strong domestic semiconductor manufacturing base, paired with significant capital flowing into renewable energy infrastructure, keeps this region firmly in the mix even as growth rates elsewhere start to outpace it.
Canada contributes modestly to regional demand as its own clean energy and industrial sectors continue to grow. Continued domestic investment in wafer manufacturing scale and higher-voltage device development should keep North America a significant, if no longer the fastest-growing, force in this market through the forecast period.
Europe GaN Power Semiconductor Market Insights 
Europe carries meaningful weight in this market too, anchored by Germany's deep automotive and industrial electronics base. European automakers have been early and aggressive adopters of wide-bandgap semiconductor technology as they push toward more efficient electric vehicle platforms, and that appetite continues to pull GaN demand through the region's substantial component supply chain.
France, Italy, and other Western European markets are contributing steady demand as regional suppliers extend GaN adoption from automotive into broader industrial and renewable energy applications. European regulatory incentives supporting green-field semiconductor fabs are also starting to bring more GaN manufacturing capacity onto the continent itself, rather than relying entirely on Asian production.
MEA & Latin America GaN Power Semiconductor Market Insights 
The Middle East & Africa market for GaN power semiconductors remains small today, though growing renewable energy investment across the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia is starting to create some genuine interest in efficient power conversion technology. Local manufacturing capacity is essentially nonexistent, so nearly all regional demand flows through imports.
Latin America's story centers on Brazil, where a developing industrial base is beginning to explore GaN adoption in select power electronics applications. Mexico is adding incremental demand of its own as nearshoring continues to draw electronics manufacturing investment into the region, though adoption across Latin America overall remains at an early stage relative to more established markets.
Market Dynamics 
Growth Drivers: Energy Efficiency Demand and Electric Vehicle Adoption 
The push for genuinely better energy efficiency is doing most of the heavy lifting behind this market's growth. GaN's ability to switch faster while wasting less energy as heat makes it a natural fit for a world that's paying closer attention to power consumption everywhere, from data centers trying to control operating costs to phone chargers trying to fit more power into a smaller brick. As energy efficiency regulations tighten across major markets, GaN's inherent advantages over silicon become harder for manufacturers to ignore.
Electric vehicle adoption is the other major engine here. As automakers push toward faster charging and longer range, every efficiency gain matters, and GaN's combination of faster switching and lower losses translates directly into smaller, lighter power electronics that help vehicles go further on the same battery. That direct line from GaN adoption to a tangible consumer benefit, more range, faster charging, keeps automotive demand climbing even as other applications mature.
Restraints: High Device Costs and Automotive Qualification Hurdles 
GaN still costs more than equivalent silicon solutions, and that price gap remains a real obstacle in cost-sensitive applications where every cent of bill-of-materials matters. Manufacturing scale is improving, but it hasn't yet reached the point where GaN can win purely on price against an incumbent technology that's been optimized for decades.
Automotive qualification adds its own friction. Getting a new power semiconductor technology approved for use in a vehicle involves years of reliability testing and validation, and automakers are understandably cautious about betting critical systems on a technology with a shorter track record than silicon. That qualification hurdle slows the pace at which GaN can expand into the automotive sector even when the underlying performance case is strong.
Opportunities: 800V EV Platforms and AI Data Center Power Architecture 
The industry's shift toward 800V electric vehicle platforms opens a genuinely large opportunity for suppliers who can push GaN's voltage ceiling higher. As more automakers commit to these higher-voltage architectures for their next-generation platforms, GaN devices capable of reliably handling that voltage range stand to capture significant new demand that simply didn't exist a few years ago.
AI data centers are emerging as an unexpectedly large opportunity too, as the industry's rapid buildout of high-density computing infrastructure creates enormous demand for compact, efficient power delivery. Partnerships like Navitas' collaboration with NVIDIA around 800V HVDC architectures for AI data center racks point to where a meaningful chunk of future GaN demand may come from, an application that barely registered on anyone's radar just a couple of years ago.

Cognex to Acquire RealSense, Expanding Machine Vision Leadership into High-Growth Robotic Perception Market

Acquisition adds leading 3D robotic perception platform, expands Cognex's served market, and supports long-term growth diversification 
NATICK, Mass. and CUPERTINO, Calif. , Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Cognex Corporation  (NASDAQ: CGNX ), the global technology leader in industrial machine vision, today announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire RealSense , the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI. The acquisition advances Cognex's strategy to diversify its growth engine by entering the robotic perception market, a high-growth adjacency that expands its served market opportunity.
"RealSense represents a compelling strategic expansion for Cognex into robotic perception, one of the most attractive adjacent markets in machine vision," said Matt Moschner , President and Chief Executive Officer of Cognex. "RealSense brings a leading 3D perception platform with proprietary technology, a strong developer community and a compelling value proposition for customers. Combined with Cognex's machine vision expertise and global reach, RealSense positions us to offer a full-stack visual intelligence platform, spanning industrial ID, 2D and 3D machine vision measurement to 3D depth perception and robotic navigation, built to serve the full spectrum of Physical AI."
"RealSense was built on a simple idea: robots and autonomous systems can't act intelligently in the physical world if they can't first perceive it accurately. We've called that mission the Visual Cortex of Physical AI. Joining Cognex puts that mission on an entirely new scale, giving us access to a global industrial customer base and go-to-market reach that would have taken us years to build on our own. This is a combination that makes both businesses stronger," said Nadav Orbach , Chief Executive Officer of RealSense.
Originally founded by Intel in 2014 and spun out in 2025, RealSense has established a leading position in 3D robotic perception, with applications across fixed arm perception-guided robotics, autonomous mobile robots, quadrupeds and humanoids. The acquisition expands Cognex's served market opportunity by adding exposure to a robotic perception market estimated at $600 million today and expected to grow more than 25% annually to approximately $1.6 billion by 2030. RealSense is expected to generate revenue of $80 million to $90 million in 2026, representing more than 50% growth over the prior year.
"This transaction is highly aligned with our disciplined M&A strategy," said Dennis Fehr , Chief Financial Officer of Cognex. "RealSense is expected to be strongly accretive to Cognex's growth profile. Over time, we expect the business to scale in line with Cognex's through-cycle financial framework, including attractive Adjusted EBITDA margins and strong free cash flow conversion."
Under the terms of the agreement, Cognex will acquire RealSense for approximately $500 million, financed entirely from existing cash and investments on its balance sheet. Cognex also expects to provide a three-year $56.5 million cash retention program at target for RealSense employees, subject to performance modifiers, and to grant restricted stock units valued at approximately $50 million under Cognex's existing 2023 Stock Option and Incentive Plan dependent on the grant-date share price. The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to customary closing conditions.
Prior to closing, RealSense will spin out its Facial Authentication product line into an independent company, including all necessary functions to continue its focused growth strategy in the biometrics market.
Evercore served as financial advisor to Cognex on the transaction.

Valens Semiconductor and onsemi Partner to Develop Integrated 3MP Automotive Camera Sensor
Fiona Craig 
September 22, 2026 2 min read 
VLN 
ON 
Semiconductor ©PickPik Valens Semiconductor (NYSE:VLN) has entered into a collaboration agreement with onsemi (NASDAQ:ON) to develop a cost-optimised image sensor incorporating MIPI A-PHY connectivity for high-volume automotive camera applications. 
The agreement, announced on 22 September 2026, focuses on integrating Valens' connectivity technology directly into onsemi's image sensors, targeting the 3-megapixel (3MP) segment. 
The companies aim to provide automotive manufacturers and Tier 1 suppliers with an integrated solution that supports adoption of the MIPI A-PHY standard. 
Collaboration Targets Simplified Automotive Camera Design 
Under the agreement, Valens will work with onsemi to incorporate MIPI A-PHY connectivity into the image sensor itself. 
The integrated approach is intended to reduce the number of separate components required in automotive camera systems while supporting industry-standard connectivity. 
Ahmed Salem, Vice President and General Manager of the Intelligent Sensing Group at onsemi, said the collaboration aims to enable: 
"a more streamlined camera architecture that reduces component count, supports industry standards, and ultimately makes advanced vision systems easier to deploy." 
The companies are targeting applications where manufacturers require cost-efficient camera systems that can be produced in high volumes. 
Companies Focus on 3MP Automotive Camera Market 
Most automotive image sensors currently target resolutions between 1 and 3 megapixels, according to the companies. 
Valens and onsemi said their planned 3MP offering addresses this established market while also targeting demand from automotive manufacturers upgrading to higher-resolution camera systems. 
The collaboration is intended to provide an additional route for original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) and Tier 1 suppliers to incorporate MIPI A-PHY connectivity into their camera designs. 
MIPI A-PHY is an industry standard designed for high-speed sensor connectivity in automotive applications. 
Partnership Expands Valens' A-PHY Product Offering 
Valens has previously announced design wins with multiple automotive OEMs for its VA7000 MIPI A-PHY chipsets. 
The collaboration with onsemi extends its approach to include connectivity integrated directly into image sensors, complementing its existing standalone chipset products. 
Yoram Salinger, Chief Executive of Valens Semiconductor, said the new offering: 
"complements Valens' existing solutions, bringing A-PHY to a much broader range of use cases." 
He added that working with onsemi strengthens the technology ecosystem by giving: 
Story Continues 
"automakers the supplier choice they expect from an industry standard." 
The agreement establishes a development partnership between the two semiconductor companies. Neither a commercial launch date nor financial terms were disclosed in the announcement.

Biopharmaceutical manufacturing has undergone multiple waves of transformation.
Single-use technologies have brought flexibility, process intensification has improved productivity and digital systems have increased visibility into operations and product quality.
Together, these advances have helped the industry to manufacture increasingly complex biologic medicines with greater speed and consistency . 
Beate Mueller-Tiemann , Chief Technology Officer at Cytiva , reports.
A new challenge is emerging
The next generation of therapies is becoming more diverse, more complex and, often, more difficult to develop , transfer and manufacture at scale.
Bispecific antibodies, antibody-drug conjugates, cell and gene therapies, viral vectors, RNA-based medicines and other emerging modalities place very different demands on process development and manufacturing.

West Pharmaceutical stock slips after recent Fed-driven drop but Q2 2026 results stay strong
Published on 09/18/2026 at 13:33 | Editorial responsibility: Rafael Müller, Editor-in-Chief AD HOC NEWS 
West Pharmaceutical stock fell about 2.3 percent on the New York Stock Exchange on September 17, 2026 after the latest Federal Reserve rate hike. The company previously reported Q2 2026 revenue of USD 872.3 million and adjusted EPS of USD 2.37, both above consensus.
West Pharmaceutical (ISIN US9523901012) stellt in sterilen Reinräumen Vials und Elastomer-Verschlüsse für Injektionssysteme her, Illustration mit AI erstellt. 
West Pharmaceutical Services, Inc. stock (ISIN US9553061055) weakened recently, with trading data showing a decline of about 2.3 percent on the New York Stock Exchange on September 17, 2026 following the latest Federal Reserve rate decision, even as the company continues to post robust quarterly figures with revenue and earnings ahead of expectations.
Q2 2026 results beat consensus
West Pharmaceutical Services, Inc. reported strong results for the second quarter of 2026, delivering adjusted earnings per share of USD 2.37, which exceeded the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 13.9 percent and underlined solid profitability in its medical packaging and delivery business, according to Zacks on September 18, 2026.
In the same Q2 2026 period, West Pharmaceutical generated revenue of USD 872.3 million, which surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 4.2 percent, according to TradingView on September 17, 2026.
The combination of a 13.9 percent earnings surprise and a 4.2 percent revenue beat in Q2 2026 indicates that West Pharmaceutical managed to expand margins and grow sales faster than the market had anticipated, reinforcing its position as a key supplier of containment and delivery solutions to the global pharmaceutical industry.
Stock reacts to Fed hike despite earnings strength
Despite the strong operational performance, West Pharmaceutical stock came under pressure after the latest Federal Reserve rate hike, with the shares losing about 2.3 percent in the session on September 17, 2026 and closing clearly below their recent high, according to New York Stock Exchange trading data summarized by Ad-hoc-news on September 18, 2026.
Per that trading overview, the intraday low on September 17, 2026 remained below the closing level while the high stayed above it, meaning that the stock finished in the lower half of its daily range and signaling sustained selling pressure into the end of the session as investors repositioned after the central bank move.
As Ad-hoc-news reported on September 18, 2026 with reference to MSN data, West Pharmaceutical was among the names indicated lower in futures trading after the Federal Reserve rate hike, with the stock marked down around 2.25 percent alongside other rate-sensitive companies.
Analyst view and long-term growth profile
Analysts have highlighted West Pharmaceutical’s solid earnings track record and longer-term growth prospects. According to Zacks on September 18, 2026, West Pharmaceutical, which currently carries a Zacks Rank 2 (Buy), has an estimated long-term earnings growth rate of 16 percent.
The same overview notes that West Pharmaceutical’s earnings surpassed estimates in each of the trailing four quarters, with an average surprise of 17.4 percent, underscoring a pattern of consistent outperformance compared with analyst expectations and suggesting that the company’s demand environment and cost discipline have been stronger than modeled.
For investors, this backdrop of double-digit expected earnings growth and repeated quarterly beats provides a counterweight to short-term share-price volatility driven by broader interest-rate and macroeconomic concerns, and positions West Pharmaceutical as a potential beneficiary of ongoing innovation and volume growth in injectable and biologic therapies.
Stock level and market context
Recent market wraps indicated that West Pharmaceutical stock had previously closed at USD 365.00 on the New York Stock Exchange on September 15, 2026, up 2.76 percent from the prior session, with an intraday range between USD 354.65 and USD 370.67 and elevated trading volume, according to a corporate-news summary from Ad-hoc-news dated September 17, 2026.
In that earlier session, the share price move was linked to robust recent quarterly results and a higher full-year outlook, showing how operational news and guidance can quickly translate into stock-market reactions when market conditions are supportive.
Looking at the current setup around September 18, 2026, the key tension for West Pharmaceutical stock is that strong Q2 2026 fundamentals and a positive analyst stance coexist with short-term pressure from interest-rate decisions. For medium-term oriented investors, the numbers from Q2 2026 and the indicated long-term earnings growth rate of 16 percent may therefore be more relevant than the single-session drop triggered by the Federal Reserve.

Physical AI drives autonomous driving upgrade; three efficiency factors lift AI accelerator demand
Jasper Jiang , Analyst
End-to-end autonomous driving has become the mainstream technology path, and the inference demand created by Physical AI in autonomous driving systems is, in turn, reshaping automotive system-on-chip (SoC) design.
Abstract
End-to-end autonomous driving has become the mainstream technology path, and the inference demand created by Physical AI in autonomous driving systems is, in turn, reshaping automotive system-on-chip (SoC) design. DIGITIMES presents a 3x3 matrix of key automotive SoC indicators for the AI era, organized around underlying hardware specifications, mid-layer efficiency performance, and upper-layer solution compatibility, as an evaluation framework for next-generation automotive SoC solutions. DIGITIMES believes that the AI accelerator will become the compute core of next-generation automotive SoCs, meeting the low-latency, low-system-power, and low-memory-bottleneck requirements of AI inference in autonomous driving systems.
As global industry consensus gradually forms around the three stages of AI evolution, attention is also shifting to the underlying engineering, core tasks, and key metrics for each stage, with hardware requirements differing accordingly. In the Agentic AI stage, AI systems must handle not only inference but also auxiliary tasks such as task scheduling and tool calling, so they rely on the compute strengths of the central processing unit (CPU), which is supporting demand for CPUs. Looking ahead to Physical AI, AI systems will need to perform real-time, accurate inference in diverse and changing physical environments. DIGITIMES believes the neural processing unit (NPU) will become the main compute core for Physical AI development.
This report covers how physical AI evolution is impacting automotive SoC design and the specifications offered by major vendors such as Nvidia, Qualcomm, and Mobileye.

TOPPAN Group Inaugurates New BOPP Film Manufacturing Line at Irplast in Italy
Enhancing supply capabilities using simultaneous biaxial orientation technology to bolster global supply of sustainable solutions
Tweet 
Tokyo – September 17, 2026 – TOPPAN Inc. (TOPPAN), a TOPPAN Group company and wholly owned subsidiary of TOPPAN Holdings Inc. (TYO: 7911), and its Italy-based film manufacturing subsidiary Irplast S.p.A. (Irplast), today announced the inauguration of a new manufacturing line for high-performance biaxially oriented polypropylene (BOPP) films, marking the occasion with a ceremony on September 15, 2026.
An overview of this development will be included at the TOPPAN booth (East Hall 2, Booth No. 2R10) during TOKYO PACK 2026, to be held at Tokyo Big Sight from Wednesday, October 14 to Friday, October 16, 2026.
Background and Objectives
In its packaging business, the TOPPAN Group is accelerating the establishment of its global supply network for recycle-ready mono-material packaging to meet tightening environmental regulations - such as the EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR) - and to drive the transition toward a circular economy.
Irplast, a TOPPAN Group company, is a premium film manufacturer equipped with advanced simultaneous biaxial orientation technology. Its unique expertise in minimizing thermal shrinkage provides BOPP films with exceptional heat resistance, mechanical strength, and superior transparency.
Through the operation of this line, together with existing capabilities, the plant will be able to establish an overall supply infrastructure of up to 30,000 tonnes per year for high-performance BOPP films. This deployment expands the TOPPAN Group’s production capabilities and enhances manufacturing efficiency, ensuring a stable, local supply to meet the surging demand for sustainable packaging in Europe and beyond.
Features of the New Manufacturing Line
・Developing High-Value Applications through Simultaneous Orientation Technology: 
The films produced on this line offer uniform physical properties and high dimensional stability achieved through the LISIM 1 simultaneous stretching process. Leveraging this robustness, TOPPAN and Irplast will actively develop high-end packaging applications that require durability even under demanding conditions, such as retort sterilization.
・Reducing Environmental Impact through Package Down Gauging: 
Utilizing the film’s superior mechanical strength, development will be focused toward "down gauging" (reducing film thickness). This enables a steady and continuous reduction in plastic consumption while maintaining essential packaging functions, directly supporting resource conservation goals.
Future Activities
The new line is expected to commence full commercial operations by late 2026, supplying high-performance BOPP films to packaging converters and global brand owners.
The combination of Irplast’s BOPP film manufacturing expertise and the TOPPAN Group’s broad base of technologies and solutions will expand sustainable solutions worldwide by driving use as a next-generation substrate in transparent GL BARRIER 2 films as well as unlocking new possibilities for high-performance, sustainable packaging solutions that contribute to a circular economy.
1 LISIM is Bruckner’s simultaneous stretching technology utilized by Irplast.
URL: https://www.irplast.com/bopp-film-division/ 
2 GL BARRIER is TOPPAN’s proprietary brand of transparent film products that deliver world-class barrier performance. Stable performance is enabled by a multi-layer structure combining a unique coating layer with a high-quality vapor-deposited layer. In recognition of their numerous outstanding features, GL BARRIER products are used in a wide variety of fields, including the food, healthcare/pharmaceutical, and industrial materials sectors. Combining the functions of the printing and barrier substrate layers into a single layer provides an alternative to aluminum foil with a streamlined layer structure.
https://www.toppan.com/en/living-industry/packaging/products/barrier_film/ 
About the TOPPAN Group
Established in Tokyo in 1900, the TOPPAN Group is a leading and diversified global provider committed to delivering sustainable, integrated solutions in fields including printing, communications, security, packaging, décor materials, electronics, and digital transformation. The TOPPAN Group’s global team of more than 50,000 employees offers optimal solutions enabled by industry-leading expertise and technologies to address the diverse challenges of every business sector and society and contribute to the achievement of shared sustainability goals.

Mayo Clinic teams with Thermo Fisher to form biomedical data group Precure
By
Joseph Keenan 
Sep 15, 2026 11:46am 
Mayo Clinic 
Thermo Fisher Scientific 
partnership 
Big Data 
The Mayo Clinic and Thermo Fisher Scientific formed a group to reap data that could lead to the development of new treatments, devices and diagnostics. ()
The Mayo Clinic has partnered with Thermo Fisher Scientific to launch a new group focused on reaping large-scale data that could lead to the understanding and development of new treatments, devices and diagnostics.
The newly formed Precure LLC is tasked with creating one of the largest biomedical datasets using human multi-omics data generation that integrates proteomic, genomic and longitudinal clinical data to help identify early biological signals of disease, the clinic said in a release.
The goal is to better understand and identify early biological signals that develop before a disease is clinically diagnosed. By connecting molecular and clinical data early on, researchers could get a head start that could lead to faster drug development and earlier diagnosis across a wide range of diseases, including cancer, cardiometabolic disease, neurological disorders and immune-mediated disease. 
Related
Thermo Fisher Scientific teams up with Nvidia, TetraScience for next-gen AI workflow projects 
“Precure has the potential to create a step change in how we generate and apply multi-omics data to improve human health,” Marc Casper, Thermo Fisher Scientific’s chair and CEO, said in a statement. 
“By combining Thermo Fisher's leadership in scientific technology with Mayo Clinic's leadership in clinical care, research and innovation, we can create new opportunities at unprecedented scale to detect disease earlier, accelerate drug development and enable more precise therapies.”
The newly formed group is designed to complement Mayo Clinic’s Precure Research, which is part of an effort to gain insight into biological changes that happen as people move from health toward disease.
Precure Research looks to identify early disease signals while Precure LLC would provide the scale and infrastructure for collecting molecular data that could lead to new diagnostics, therapies and other solutions.
Mayo Clinic said any financial returns it earned from the endeavor would be used to further its mission of patient care, research and education.

09-15-2026 05:00 PM CET | Health & Medicine 
Press release from: Future Market Insights 
Single-Use Downstream Bioprocessing Market, USA Single-Use Downstream Bioprocessing Market
The global single-use downstream bioprocessing market is projected to grow from USD 4.2 billion in 2026 to USD 13.6 billion by 2036, registering a 12.5% CAGR during the forecast period. Future Market Insights estimates that the market will add approximately USD 9.4 billion in incremental opportunity as biopharmaceutical manufacturers expand disposable filtration, chromatography, sampling, and connection technologies across downstream workflows.
Single-use filtration systems are estimated to account for 32.0% of product type demand in 2026, supported by their use across clarification, concentration, and polishing. By end user, biopharmaceutical manufacturers are projected to lead with 49.0% share, while purification is expected to represent 35.0% of workflow demand. Commercial-scale operations are estimated to account for 52.0% share, reflecting the growing standardization of qualified disposable assemblies for repeated production campaigns.

Why Flexible Downstream Capacity Matters for Biopharmaceutical Manufacturers
Biopharmaceutical manufacturers are increasingly adopting flexible downstream processing systems as multiproduct facilities handle diverse biologic production campaigns. Disposable flow paths can allow manufacturers to configure downstream processes with less reliance on fixed product-contact infrastructure.
Single-use filtration systems are at the center of this shift. With a projected 32.0% share in 2026, filtration remains important across clarification, concentration, and polishing stages following cell harvest.
The commercial case extends beyond faster setup. Manufacturers must demonstrate that disposable components deliver consistent performance across production campaigns while maintaining validated flow paths and appropriate material characteristics.
Supplier reliability is therefore becoming part of procurement strategy. Buyers increasingly evaluate component traceability, change notifications, qualification documentation, and consumable availability before expanding a single platform across multiple manufacturing sites.
Market Snapshot

The single-use downstream bioprocessing market is forecast to expand at 12.5% annually through 2036, reaching USD 13.6 billion from USD 4.2 billion in 2026.
What's Driving Near-Term Demand?
The expansion of biologics manufacturing is increasing demand for downstream technologies capable of handling purification, concentration, buffer exchange, and product recovery with greater process flexibility.
Multiproduct facilities are an important source of demand. Shared manufacturing infrastructure can require adaptable downstream systems that support different products and production campaigns without creating excessive fixed-equipment constraints.
Purification is projected to account for 35.0% of workflow demand in 2026, reflecting the importance of downstream separation and purification in biologic manufacturing.
Monoclonal antibodies represent another significant opportunity. The segment is forecast to hold 38.0% of application demand, supported by established capture and polishing sequences and the continued importance of antibody-based biologics.
Commercial-scale operations are estimated to account for 52.0% of demand, increasing the need for standardized assemblies that can be repeatedly deployed while maintaining qualification and process consistency.
Why Is Supply and Change Control Becoming a Procurement Priority?
Single-use downstream processing depends heavily on consistent materials and reliable component supply. A change to a disposable component can potentially affect an established manufacturing process, making supplier change control an important consideration for biopharmaceutical companies.
The United States Food and Drug Administration treats supplier changes, material changes, and extensions of disposable-material use as manufacturing changes requiring assessment and appropriate reporting. As a result, manufacturers increasingly examine supplier documentation before approving changes to established single-use platforms.
Material consistency is particularly important where multiple components form a validated fluid path. Changes in tubing, filters, connectors, membranes, or other components may require additional qualification to establish that downstream performance remains comparable.
Reliable consumable supply is equally important. Production interruptions caused by shortages or extended lead times can affect campaign scheduling, increasing the value of suppliers with established manufacturing capacity and distribution networks.
Where Are the Key Market Opportunities?
Future Market Insights covers the United States, Japan, Germany, the United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, and South Korea in its analysis of the single-use downstream bioprocessing market.
The United States remains an important market because of its established biopharmaceutical manufacturing base and concentration of biologics production infrastructure. European markets, including Germany and the United Kingdom, also provide opportunities as manufacturers modernize downstream processes and expand flexible production capacity.
Japan, Canada, Australia, and South Korea represent additional markets covered in the report, with adoption influenced by local biologics manufacturing capabilities, facility investments, regulatory requirements, and access to qualified single-use technologies.
What Challenges Could Constrain Adoption?
Material changes and supplier substitutions can trigger requalification requirements, potentially increasing implementation time and validation costs. Manufacturers must therefore assess individual components within the context of the complete downstream process.
Supply interruptions represent another risk. Single-use manufacturing depends on recurring access to filters, assemblies, connectors, sampling components, and other consumables. Delayed deliveries can disrupt production campaigns.
Process qualification also remains essential. Faster setup does not remove the requirement to establish appropriate performance, integrity, material compatibility, and process consistency.
As single-use platforms expand across manufacturing sites, suppliers will need to demonstrate reliable change-control practices and provide sufficient technical documentation to support regulatory assessments.

Sartorius AG, Cytiva, Merck KGaA, Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc., and Repligen Corporation offer broad downstream processing portfolios. Specialist suppliers focus on specific filtration, fluid-management, and disposable processing requirements.
Companies capable of supplying qualified components consistently across development, clinical, and commercial production can strengthen customer relationships as biopharmaceutical manufacturers standardize platforms across multiple facilities.

content_text:
Research
Mayo Clinic and Thermo Fisher Scientific launch Precure, LLC to identify signs of disease before symptoms appear
By
Tom Millikin
September 15, 2026 
Share this:
Pioneering initiative will generate data at the frontier of healthcare to help transform early biological signals into new opportunities for prevention, diagnosis and treatment 
ROCHESTER, Minn. and WALTHAM, Mass. — Mayo Clinic today announced the launch of Precure, LLC, with founding partner Thermo Fisher Scientific, the world leader in serving science, to help transform how the life sciences community understands the biological changes that occur as people move from health toward disease.
Precure, LLC will create one of the world’s leading biomedical datasets through one of the largest human multi-omics data-generation efforts, integrating proteomic, genomic and longitudinal clinical data to help researchers identify early biological signals of disease and provide a foundation for new discoveries in disease biology, diagnostics and therapeutics.
Many diseases begin developing biologically years before symptoms lead to a clinical diagnosis. By connecting molecular and clinical data over time, Precure, LLC has the potential to help researchers better understand these early changes, accelerate drug development and create new opportunities for earlier diagnosis, intervention and more personalized care across a wide range of diseases, such as cancer, cardiometabolic disease, neurological disorders and immune-mediated disease.
Precure, LLC will bring together molecular data generated from one million biospecimens, linked with longitudinal clinical information collected over several years, integrating genomic and proteomic information with Mayo Clinic’s clinical data and expertise in a highly standardized setting. Advanced AI and large-scale data-analytics will be integral to identifying patterns within these complex datasets and translating them into actionable insights. Mayo Clinic will serve as the majority owner of Precure, LLC. Thermo Fisher joins the partnership as a minority owner.
"At Mayo Clinic, we are committed to transforming patient care through innovation," says Gianrico Farrugia, M.D. , president and CEO, Mayo Clinic. "By harnessing the full potential of multi-omics data, Precure, LLC aims to help us better understand disease before symptoms appear, accelerating discoveries that can lead to earlier diagnoses, more targeted treatments and better outcomes for patients."
Together, the organizations contribute complementary expertise designed to generate the molecular and clinical data needed to accelerate discovery and translate new insights into advancements in patient care:
Mayo Clinic combines world-class clinical and research leadership with advanced AI and data science capabilities, extensive biospecimens and longitudinal de-identified clinical data to accelerate discovery and translate insights into advances for patients.
Thermo Fisher brings industry-leading proteomics expertise and solutions, including its cutting-edge proteomics platform, Olink™ Explore HT, and Thermo Scientific Orbitrap Mass Spectrometry, kits and reagents to help build Precure, LLC’s multi-omics ecosystem.
“Precure LLC has the potential to create a step change in how we generate and apply multi-omics data to improve human health,” said Marc Casper, Chairman and CEO, Thermo Fisher Scientific. “By combining Thermo Fisher’s leadership in scientific technology with Mayo Clinic’s leadership in clinical care, research and innovation, we can create new opportunities at unprecedented scale to detect disease earlier, accelerate drug development and enable more precise therapies.”
Precure, LLC complements Precure Research, Mayo Clinic’s investigator-led scientific effort to understand the biological changes that occur as people move from health toward disease. Precure Research advances the science of identifying and understanding early disease signals, while Precure, LLC provides the scale, infrastructure and collaborations needed to generate population-scale molecular data and help translate discoveries into new diagnostics, therapeutics and other healthcare solutions. Mayo Clinic provides the pathway to validate discoveries and ultimately brings meaningful advances into patient care.
Mayo Clinic's involvement in Precure, LLC is intended to advance its nonprofit mission. Any financial returns to Mayo Clinic would be reinvested in its mission of patient care, research and education.
Visit mayo.edu/research/precure for more information. 
###
About Precure, LLC 
Precure, LLC is a Mayo Clinic-controlled company established to generate and responsibly integrate population-scale molecular data with longitudinal clinical information. Precure, LLC creates the infrastructure and scale needed to enable external collaborations, disease-focused discovery and the development of new diagnostics, therapeutics and other healthcare solutions. It complements Mayo Clinic’s investigator-led research and clinical translation activities.
About Mayo Clinic 
Mayo Clinic is a nonprofit organization committed to innovation in clinical practice, education and research, and providing compassion, expertise and answers to everyone who needs healing. Visit the  Mayo Clinic News Network  for additional Mayo Clinic news.  
About Thermo Fisher Scientific  
Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc. is the world leader in serving science, with annual revenue over $45 billion. Our Mission is to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. Whether our customers are accelerating life sciences research, solving complex analytical challenges, increasing productivity in their laboratories, improving patient health through diagnostics or the development and manufacture of life-changing therapies, we are here to support them. Our global team delivers an unrivaled combination of innovative technologies, purchasing convenience and pharmaceutical services through our industry-leading brands, including Thermo Scientific, Applied Biosystems, Invitrogen, Gibco, Fisher Scientific, Unity Lab Services, Patheon and PPD. For more information, please visit www.thermofisher.com .

content_text:
Is Moderna, Merck's mRNA cancer vaccine win the start of a 'personalized medicine revolution'?
By
Marissa Russo 
Sep 11, 2026 9:00am 
Moderna 
Merck & Co. 
mRNA 
cancer vaccine 
"This is going to catalyze so much incredible ... innovation," Johns Hopkins University's Jeff Coller, Ph.D., told Fierce. (wildpixel/Getty Images)
The announcement from Merck & Co. and Moderna last month that their mRNA cancer vaccine had successfully lengthened patient survival in a phase 3 study affirmed the two companies' years of hard work and reignited hopes for the field of personalized medicine.
There's a lot riding on exactly how well intismeran autogene—alternatively known as V940 or mRNA-4157—performs, and the companies have held back any detailed data for a future medical meeting. But intismeran seems to do its best work against resected late-stage melanoma when paired with the standard-of-care immunotherapy Keytruda. 
Merck and Moderna's INTerpath-001 trial enrolled 1,137 patients who had previously had their cutaneous melanoma surgically removed. These participants either received intismeran along with Keytruda, or Keytruda alone. According to the August update, the group who received the adjuvant therapy showed statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvements in recurrence-free survival, the study's primary endpoint, and survival without a distant metastasis, a secondary endpoint.
Since that announcement, experts and industry insiders have suggested to Fierce that the news has not only renewed hopes in the intismeran program, which hit a regulatory hurdle back in 2024, but also boosted prospects for other biopharmas exploring mRNA as a vehicle for personalized cancer treatments.
What continues to make oncology treatments so difficult to perfect is that every type of cancer is different and even patients who have the same cancer have tumors that behave differently under the same treatments. Being able to customize a vaccine to each patient’s particular tumor would be a boon.
“I think it's the start of a personalized medicine revolution,” said Jeff Coller, Ph.D., a professor of RNA biology and therapeutics at Johns Hopkins University, when speaking with Fierce about the intismeran update. “This is going to catalyze so much incredible research and development and innovation.”
When the full data do become available, investors will be looking to see whether intismeran could be used against other cancers and as broadly as Keytruda, said Myles Minter, Ph.D., a William Blair analyst. 
“We’ll have to see what the data look like, but if they look really good and this is a stepwise change in efficacy, this is standard-of-care shifting,” he told Fierce.
Knock-on effect
By the time the markets closed on the day of the therapy's phase 3 announcement, Moderna’s stock was up 177% —but it wasn't alone. Share prices were up as much as 20% for other biotechs that are playing in the mRNA arena, such as Arcturus Therapeutics. 
The San Diego-based biopharma has been developing therapies for infectious diseases, such as COVID-19 and influenza, as well genetic conditions like cystic fibrosis and ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency, the most common urea cycle disorder. Currently, its COVID-19 vaccine Kostaive is approved in Japan, the U.K and the EU.
Arcturus’ approach to mRNA therapies is to leverage self-amplifying mRNA, which CEO Joseph Payne argued is better at expressing the antigen than personalized antigens. Arcturus’ self-amplifying mRNA includes a replicase, which allows for more and sustained protein production. 
The uniqueness of this type of mRNA also means it can be administered at lower doses with higher antibodies and for a longer time, Payne told Fierce. In combination with this platform, Arcturus has developed a lipid nanoparticle delivery system, Lunar, which it's testing in a phase 2 trial as an inhalable mRNA therapy for patients with cystic fibrosis.
Arcturus entered into a research pact with London-based Achilles Therapeutics in 2024 to explore personalized mRNA cancer vaccines. The goal of the collaboration is to combine Achilles' AI platform Peleus, which identifies patient neoantigens, with Arcturus’ self-amplifying mRNA technology.
For now, Arcturus' broader strategy focuses on infectious and life-threatening genetic diseases, but Payne does think the technology can be applied to cancer. “I think the field is moving towards oncology,” he said.
German biopharma BioNTech is already in that race. Even before its pivot to become a “fully integrated immunotherapy powerhouse,” the company had been working on its FixVac mRNA cancer vaccine platform , which uses a fixed combination of mRNA-encoded non-mutated tumor antigens in an effort to enhance the stability of mRNA in the body. Vaccines from the platform are designed to target antigen-presenting dendritic cells and trigger a strong immune response.
The lead candidate, dubbed BNT113, is an mRNA cancer immunotherapy candidate that encodes a fixed set of two oncoproteins that are frequently found in human papillomavirus type 16 positive (HPV16+) solid tumors. BNT113 has reached phase 2/3 development in head and neck cancer with a readout on the first of its two primary endpoints anticipated this year.
Ugur Sahin, M.D., and Özlem Türeci, M.D., founded BioNTech in 2008 to research mRNA technology, which was overlooked in science at the time. The company made its name during the COVID-19 pandemic, with the release of Pfizer-partnered Comirnaty, the first COVID-19 vaccine to get a full approval from the FDA .
In collaboration with Genentech, BioNTech has another flagship personalized mRNA platform known as individualized neoantigen-specific immunotherapy (iNeST). The iNeST platform encodes up to 20 patient-specific neoantigens and uses a unique delivery platform called a lipoplex that enables administration of the vaccines to key “boot camps of the immune system,” like the spleen, lymph nodes and bone marrow, a BioNTech representative explained to Fierce. 
With this approach, the company aims to eliminate polyclonal residual disease and is focusing on cancers for which immunotherapies have not worked well, such as pancreatic cancer. 
BioNTech recently scrapped a phase 2 study of an iNeST candidate called autogene cevumera in patients with surgically removed stage 2 or 3 colorectal cancer. Genentech originally told Fierce that this move was down to “more deaths in the vaccine arm in this specific patient population,” with a representative from BioNTech later clarifying that the “decision was not safety-related” and was instead due to a “numerical imbalance in overall survival between treatment arms.”
BioNTech noted that a phase 2 trial evaluating autogene cevumera in combination with checkpoint inhibitors and chemotherapy in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma “will not be affected and continues as planned.”
Another contender in the programmable mRNA field is Strand Therapeutics, which is studying two self-replicating mRNA therapies that deliver IL-12, an immune signaling protein, for treatment of solid tumors. STX-001 was designed to be injected directly into tumors and is being tested in phase 1/2 trials as a monotherapy or in combination with Keytruda for triple-negative breast cancer and melanoma. Strand is concerned not just with delivery, cell-selective expression, and durability but also with controlling the RNA after delivery, according to CEO Jacob Becraft, Ph.D.
Jacob Becraft, Ph.D.
(Strand Therapeutics)
“Some of the most powerful therapeutic proteins have been difficult to use safely throughout the body,” Becraft said in an interview with Fierce. “Our goal is to make those proteins usable by programming where and how they are produced.”
Phase 1 data from the study unveiled at the American Society of Clinical Oncology conference last year included a confirmed complete response and multiple partial responses from patients with immune checkpoint inhibitor-refractory solid tumors.
Strand, which has received Big Pharma backing from the likes of Regeneron, Amgen and Eli Lilly, has another key asset in the form of STX-003. The programmable mRNA cancer immunotherapy was developed to be injected intravenously and enable IL-12 expression in tumors, allowing for a possible multi-pronged approach to targeting disease at multiple sites.
“What excites me most is the possibility of opening up an entirely new set of usable medicines,” Becraft said. “Once we can reliably deliver and control RNA in a particular cell type, we can explore multiple therapeutic payloads using that foundation. That could substantially accelerate how quickly new biological insights become treatments.”
Looking back
Moderna and Merck may have captured the headlines with intismeran, but the two companies have been working together since 2016 to develop a series of mRNA vaccines. mRNA, short for messenger ribonucleic acid, makes it possible for every cell in the body to transform DNA code into an active protein the cell uses to do a specialized job. Although scientists first discovered these naturally occurring little helpers in 1961, it would take them three more decades to wrangle mRNA as a tool for vaccination against viruses and yet another three decades before that application found mass commercial success in humans. 
Along this slow rise, squaring up mRNA vaccine technology against the vagaries of cancer specifically has remained elusive. All of this time and anticipation is latched to intismeran's journey to FDA approval and the impact such an approval would have on other mRNA therapies.
“This program sits at the convergence of decades of advances in cancer research, genomic sequencing, computational biology and informatics,” said Michelle Brown, Ph.D., Moderna's oncology lead for intismeran. “mRNA is the technology that was able to galvanize and bring it all together.” 
Moderna has centered itself on mRNA medicines since its founding in 2010, but as with BioNTech, it was the COVID-19 pandemic that pushed the technology mainstream. Moderna developed the Spikevax vaccine as part of Project Warp Speed during President Trump’s first term.
“Those policies that were made by the Trump administration really have led to this new revolution in neoantigen personalized cancer approaches,” Coller told Fierce.
Despite this initial support, the tone changed last year when the Department of Health and Human Services announced a plan to end mRNA vaccine work funded by the Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority (BARDA), a major escalation of Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s campaign against both vaccines and mRNA in general.
Moderna executives explained to Fierce a few months later that this shift in sentiment had encouraged the biopharma to focus its efforts on cancer rather than infectious disease. Still, the company secured a major success in the latter category last month when the FDA made mFlusiva the first-ever mRNA flu vaccine to receive regulatory approval in the U.S.
Accelerated approval, again 
Intismeran is customizable because it targets neoantigens, proteins that appear on the surface of cancer cells that are specific to each patient, almost like “tumor fingerprints,” Moderna's Brown told Fierce. Before receiving intismeran, each patient had their tumor sequenced and scientists designed the vaccine to fit its unique signature.
Michelle Brown, Ph.D.
(Moderna)
To make this match, the tumor's sequence was funneled into a bioinformatic algorithm that ranked the mutations based on expression, not just presence. The algorithm assessed whether antigens were “up and available for the immune system to see,” Brown said, and which neoantigens would be able to generate the best killer T-cell response while also recruiting other immune cells to the tumor.
For Merck and Moderna, 34 neoantigens was the ideal number, compared with iNest’s 20. Intismeran’s phase 2 study, which launched in 2019, cut the risk of disease recurrence by 49% at five years of follow-up . “It was the first time that we saw an inkling that a doublet could improve upon [Keytruda] standard of care,” Brown said. “It also showcased the ability to create benefit on recurrence-free survival and distant metastasis-free survival.”
The wider intismeran program encompasses a total of nine phase 2 and 3 trials in indications beyond melanoma, such as non-small cell lung cancer and renal cell carcinoma.
But it hasn't all been plain sailing for the vaccine. Back in 2024, intismeran encountered a regulatory setback when the biopharmas attempted to secure an accelerated approval pathway and the FDA rebuffed them. At the time, Moderna said it would not return to seek accelerated approval until it had a “substantially enrolled” phase 3 trial in for an adjuvant melanoma therapy. 
That patience appears to have paid off with the recent announcement of the trial's primary endpoint win. Despite holding back the data, the companies said they plan to engage with regulators on filing approval submissions for a combo regimen of intismeran and Keytruda. Moderna’s Brown remains steadfast in waiting for the full phase 3 data readout, although she is excited about what is to come with intismeran and the wider field of immunotherapy.
“It increases our confidence in the biological rationale and the power of what mRNA can provide, and it definitely showcases the clinical benefit in melanoma,” Brown said. “It gives us learnings for the rest of the portfolio overall.”

Hydro all aboard for railcar recycling effort
The global aluminum producer is working with Siemens Mobility to recycle aluminum from end of life railcars.
Hydro calls the Train2Train project a demonstration of its commitment to low-carbon aluminum and circular economy, showing how collaboration across the value chain can keep valuable materials in circulation.
Photo courtesy of Norsk Hydro ASA 
By
Brian Taylor, Senior Editor 
Published September 11, 2026
Listen to article 
/ 
Recycled-content aluminum producer Norsk Hydro ASA says it is working in collaboration with several other companies in Europe to recycle aluminum recovered from decommissioned trains and then produce new rail industry components.
Hydro, which is based in Norway and has aluminum melt shops in Europe and the United States, says it is working alongside rail industry supplier Siemens Mobility, Germany-based metals recycling firm TSR Group and Austria-based steelmaker Voestalpine on the Train2Train project.
In a pilot study that is part of the project, Hydro will melt recycled aluminum from decommissioned trains at its facility in Ghlin, Belgium. 
The aluminum comes from TSR Group, which has dismantled the rail vehicles and separated aluminum from steel with the aim of recycling the metals into new rail parts. Hydro receives the recyclable aluminum, while Voestalpine receives the ferrous scrap.
After being melted, the aluminum scrap will be processed into extrusion billets, which will be used as input material at a Hydro extrusion facility in Harderwijk, Netherlands. 
Hydro calls the Train2Train project a demonstration of its commitment to low-carbon aluminum and the circular economy, showing how collaboration across the value chain can keep valuable materials in circulation.
“Aluminum can be recycled repeatedly without losing its properties,” says Piotr Chmielewski, a vice president with Hydro Extrusions Europe. “By combining recycling expertise, digital traceability and manufacturing capabilities, we can create new opportunities for circular solutions in the rail industry. This project builds on Hydro’s ambition to accelerate the transition towards a more circular and low-carbon aluminum industry.”
Hydro says it supplies a variety of aluminum products for the rail industry, supporting manufacturers with “lightweight, durable and recyclable materials for applications including train structures, interiors and components.”
The Train2Train project aims to demonstrate that the materials from a decommissioned train can be recovered, recycled and reborn into a new one. 
In the United States, Sweden-based steelmaker SSAB has collaborated with metals recycler Alter Trading, St. Louis, and railcar builder Greenbrier Companies, Lake Oswego, Oregon, in a project that establishes a similar loop .
Hydro  says, “At a time when global supply chains are under increasing pressure, gaining greater control over material flows is becoming increasingly important. The project brings together the full value chain, from dismantling and recycling to material processing and manufacturing, with each partner playing a critical role in creating a transparent and circular material loop.”

More than 15 companies implicated in commercial antibody image manipulation scandal 
A recent scientific report found almost 19,000 doctored images of antibodies available in the commercial market.
Millie Hoe , Reporter, BioProcess International September 9, 2026
schedule 4 Min Read 
Wikimedia, Masur 
link 
A landmark investigation published by Northwestern University’s Reese Richardson found widespread image manipulation in the commercial antibody market. In the online article, more than 15 well-known biotechnology companies were implicated in using doctored images in their antibody catalogs. 
Richardson and his colleagues found almost 19,000 images online of antibody assays that had been subject to photo editing. This included several established vendors of commercial antibodies, such as Millipore Sigma, GeneTex, and Abnova, among others. 
“As part of our ongoing quality efforts, we continue to conduct a portfolio-wide review of antibody imagery to ensure that supporting information meets our standards for accuracy and reliability,” a spokesperson for MilliporeSigma told BPI/BioXconomy. 
“When questions arise about an image, our immediate response is to remove the image and review both the image and associated product.” 
Related: “Don’t call it continuous!” AstraZeneca expert talks integrated bioprocessing at BPI 
One of the biggest companies implicated was Thermo Fisher Scientific, whose website Richardson said featured more than 5,000 doctored images affecting more than 4,000 antibody products. 
“The investigation into Thermo Fisher yielded several hundred images that showed the same background pattern as one another,” Richardson told us . “Several other vendors all sold products with the same background, which was the first indication that this was a broader industry-wide problem.” 
The compiled images also revealed a high likelihood of widespread private labeling in the commercial antibody market, where large brands sell third-party products under their own name. Several images containing validation assays such as Western blot and immunofluorescence appeared to be replicated and doctored across multiple different antibody products. 
“Many of the affected images were apparently made up wholesale,” noted Richardson. “I remain doubtful that many of these antibodies were validated, meaning that no quality control was actually performed.” 
Some of the antibody products with doctored images failed to meet the mark in validation tests in open science communities, such as Only Good Antibodies . Of the more than 50 antibody products with manipulated photos investigated, 83% failed in at least one of its listed applications. 
Andrew Lane, an immunologist and independent life sciences consultant, was not involved in the investigation but has written publicly about the revelations. He spoke with us about the findings and detailed their greater ramifications. 
“Some of the doctoring reported could be complete fabrication of results, which brings into question whether or not a particular antibody has even been tested in a specific technique,” Lane said . “If that truly is the case, then clearly customers are being misled and suppliers are making unsubstantiated claims.” 
Related: BPI Asia Digital Series 
In response to Richardson’s report, which was picked up by several major scientific journals, Thermo Fisher publicly stated that the company “takes antibody validation, specificity, and accurate product documentation seriously,” and that “the company fully stands by the data and underlying science.” 
“We are reviewing Western blot images (including those provided by third parties) on our website to ensure that any Western blot images are clearly identified as either ‘raw-unedited’ or as an image that ‘may have been edited, optimized, or otherwise adjusted,’” said Thermo Fisher. 
As well as commercial implications for the antibody market at large, Richardson pointed out that false validation assays have serious consequences within scientific research. 
“Often, scientists do not have the time or funds to properly validate their antibodies; they'll take the manufacturers at their word that the antibodies work as intended,” he said. “If the antibodies are non-sensitive or non-specific and this is not caught, this can (and often does) lead to erroneous conclusions propagating through the scientific literature.” 
Related: BPI Spring Digital Week 
Of the 15 companies implicated, six have made public statements vowing to evaluate all affected products mentioned in the report. However, until then, Richardson said it will be difficult for scientists to ensure that the antibody they pay for will meet the mark. 
“Thirty-eight percent [of antibody products with doctored images] fail every application for which data is available,” Richardson said. “I believe that the quality control and marketing of research antibodies should, at a minimum, be regulated by a public authority.” 
Lane believes the onus falls on major suppliers to be forthcoming about their quality control protocols and the production origins of their products. 
“I think companies need to be transparent not only about the images that they publish, but also about the provenance of the antibody itself,” he added. “Companies should make it clear if they are the original manufacturer of an antibody, or if a third party has manufactured the antibody.” 
“Perhaps even less than perfect results should be shown. I’m sure that companies who do undertake their own manufacturing and validation will make it even clearer after this episode.”

4th Cell Therapy for Autoimmune Disease Summit
Event
As cell therapy for autoimmune disease transitions from breakthrough clinical case studies to broad clinical validation, developers are racing to overcome challenges around safety, scalability, durability of response, and patient access while advancing the next generation of immune reset therapies.
In this context, the 4th Cell Therapy for Autoimmune Disease Summit (December 1-3, 2026) returns to Philadelphia, PA, bringing together biotech, pharma, academic, and clinical leaders working across autologous, allogeneic, and in vivo cell therapy approaches to accelerate the development of transformative treatments for autoimmune diseases.
Organizations including Artiva Biotherapeutics , Cabaletta Bio , PolTREG , Moderna , Mesoblast , Sail Biomedicines , CPTx , Kite Pharma , Overland Therapeutics , and the University of Pennsylvania are confirmed to participate, sharing the latest scientific, clinical, and commercial insights shaping the field.
Over three days, attendees will gain exclusive access to the latest advances in autoimmune cell therapy development, spanning preclinical innovation, translational research, clinical trial progress, manufacturing strategies, and commercialization considerations. Moderna and Merck’s mRNA success fuels focus on ‘scaling out and scaling down’
September 8, 2026  |  
2 min read  |  
Nick Paul Taylor 
Twitter 
LinkedIn 
Facebook 
Email
Print
iStock, Christoph Burgstedt 
After mastering mass-market mRNA production during the pandemic, the industry now needs to achieve the timely delivery of individualized vaccines to thousands of patients.
The recent clinical success of Merck and Moderna’s intismeran autogene raised expectations for personalized mRNA cancer vaccines across the industry. Yet getting the products to patients presents new challenges.
In the past, the industry was focused on scaling up, Roberta Duncan, founder and principal of strategic consulting firm The Modeste Duncan Group, told BioSpace . Now, the conversation is about “scaling out and scaling down,” added Duncan, who also serves on the board of the Alliance for mRNA Medicines.
To make intismeran, Moderna sequences an individual’s cancer and healthy cells and analyzes the data using an automated bioinformatics system to identify up to 34 patient-specific neoantigens. Formulated in a lipid nanoparticle delivery system, mRNA encoding the neoantigens triggers protein production in the body to drive an immune response against the tumor.
By 2025, Moderna had reduced the time from sample collection to vaccine administration to around six weeks, down from roughly seven to eight weeks in 2019 . The turnaround time “can probably be brought under one month,” Guggenheim Securities analysts said in an Aug. 21 note to investors, citing Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center computational oncologist Benjamin Greenbaum.
Moderna has set up a dedicated facility in Massachusetts to support intismeran’s planned launch. The company calculates that the facility can support the vaccine “for several years,” Moderna President Stephen Hoge said on an earnings call in July. The plant should “satisfy the initial indication” of melanoma, Hoge added, and Moderna will add more capacity to meet demand beyond an initial launch.
Hoge was speaking before the INTerpath-001 trial readout raised expectations for intismeran. Last month, an earlier-than-expected trial readout showed the personalized vaccine combined with Keytruda improved outcomes in patients with melanoma, nearly doubling Moderna’s share price while Merck’s stock jumped 12% .
Cancer 
Moderna stock nearly doubles as Merck-partnered mRNA cancer vaccine meets Phase 3 goal 
Melanoma was slower to recur in patients receiving Merck and Moderna’s mRNA vaccine with Keytruda, supporting use of the combination in adjuvant treatment. The partners plan to take the data to the FDA.
August 19, 2026
 ·  3 min read
 ·  Nick Paul Taylor 
Read more 
Moderna, which is primarily responsible for manufacturing intismeran under the terms of its deal with Merck, did not respond to BioSpace ’s questions about how the clinical success has affected the company’s thinking about demand and capacity.
Moderna’s ability to make intismeran for the thousands of patients in active trials of the vaccine is built on years of investment in in-house capabilities. Biotechs without such capabilities can supply the market by working with CDMOs, Duncan said, provided they can find partners “willing to invest in miniaturizing scale, because they’re all built for large-scale manufacturing.”
As personalized mRNA vaccines come to market, Duncan warned, “we’re going to have to have a really hard conversation about cost of goods and the cost of manufacturing.” Believing that clinical data show the novel modality works, Duncan now sees the speed and cost of production as the keys to commercial success.
“It’s not going to be on the biology,” she said. “It’s going to be on the logistics and the cost.”
Editor’s note: Heather McKenzie contributed reporting to this story.

content_text:
GeoCue Integrates Ouster’s BABA-Compliant Rev8 OS1 Max Lidar Into TrueView Drone Payloads
September 3, 2026 by Ian McNabb Leave a Comment 
Native color digital lidar joins TrueView 1 payloads and LP360 software for utility corridor and large-scale infrastructure mapping across the U.S. 
Ouster (Nasdaq: OUST) and GeoCue announced a strategic partnership on September 1, 2026 from San Francisco. The two companies will integrate Ouster’s Rev8 OS1 Max digital lidar into GeoCue’s TrueView product line. The sensor complies with the Build America, Buy America Act (BABA). BABA compliance matters for federal projects with domestic content rules. Joint flight testing and firmware tuning took place in Huntsville, Alabama.
The partnership targets utility and infrastructure customers. GeoCue’s TrueView 1 payloads and LP360 point-cloud software will pair with the Ouster sensor to deliver survey-grade data. The move builds on prior GeoCue TrueView expansions , including the TrueView 540 lidar co-developed with CHC Navigation.
“We are moving America’s drone surveying onto American sensing by pairing our TrueView payloads with Ouster’s Rev8 OS1 Max,” said Frank Darmayan, CEO of GeoCue. “This transition allows us to offer our customers a compliant, high-performance solution that delivers the survey-grade data they depend on for critical infrastructure monitoring and large-scale mapping projects.”
Rev8 OS1 Max advantages for TrueView
The Rev8 OS1 Max offers four gains for GeoCue customers. A smaller spot size and tighter beam resolve thin objects such as power lines and structural edges. The 200-meter (656-foot) range at 10% reflectivity clears altitude limits around utility corridors. Operators fly higher without losing data quality. The sensor captures native color alongside 3D lidar, so every point arrives aligned to its color. That gives LP360 an added RGB reference beyond the dual cameras in every TrueView payload, tightening sensor fusion. And 256 channels in 2K and 4K modes keep point density high at fast flight speeds. That supports long-corridor surveys by propeller and fixed-wing aircraft.
“Our partnership with GeoCue is a testament to how native color digital lidar can serve as the bedrock for physical AI applications that have a profound impact on infrastructure and public safety,” said Angus Pacala, CEO of Ouster. “By integrating our Rev8 OS1 Max sensor, we are providing the survey-grade precision and reliability required to empower the next generation of drone mapping professionals.”
Live demo at Commercial UAV Expo
Ouster will demo the Rev8 OS1 Max at Booth 1653 during the Commercial UAV Expo in Las Vegas. The show runs September 1-3, 2026. More information is available at Ouster .
